units.la: ANUS ac decrepitus ille Simeon, Spiritu Dei praeditus, de infantulo Iesu recens nato, in hunc modum vaticinatur: Ecce, hic positus est in signum, cui contradicetur. Praedicit Sanctissimus Senex, huic nostro Servatori tam vehementer contradicturum iri, ut omnes omnium saeculorum hostes impias in ipsum tela, tanquam in signum sint directuri, & ad hunc veluti scopum de industria ac data opera collimaturi.
units.tr: The aged and decrepit Simeon, filled with the Spirit of God, prophesied in this manner over the newly born infant Jesus: "Behold, this child is set for a sign which shall be spoken against." The most holy old man foretold that this our Saviour would be opposed so fiercely that all the enemies of every age would aim their impious weapons at him as at a mark, and would deliberately and purposefully take him as their target.

units.la: Impletum hoc, proh dolor! omnib. retrò seculis, si historia Evangelica, & Ecclesiastica Chronica, nostrorum etiam temporum experientia confirmantur. Quomodo n. mox Iudaei Christo con- tradixerunt, & quidem non verbis modo, sed & lapidibus, quin imò tandem plane ipso cofixo? Neque vero etiamnum hodie à furore isto, remiserunt quicquam. Animus tamen haret execrabiles blasphemias & errorum portenta recensere, eaque scribendo consignare manibus refugit, quasi scelerati Iudaei in Iesum Christum Servatorem nostrum evomere ore scelerato non verentur.
units.tr: Alas, this has been fulfilled in all the ages past, as the Gospel history and the ecclesiastical chronicles confirm, and as the experience of our own times also shows. For how soon the Jews spoke against Christ, and not only with words but with stones, and at last even nailed him to the cross! Nor have they relented at all in that rage even to this day. Yet my mind shrinks from recounting their execrable blasphemies and monstrous errors, and my hand recoils from setting them down in writing, though the wicked Jews do not hesitate to vomit them with a wicked mouth against Jesus Christ our Saviour.

units.la: Impurus vero ille Mahometus in Alcorano se Idololatram, lascivum, mulierosum, adulterum (egregios me Christi flosculos!) profitetur, & ut quidem verbis, qua vel agasonem referre pudeat. Christum impudens ac maledicum istud os, Dei quidem Sermonem, Dei Spiritum, ac virtutem, imò & animam Dei, ex Maria virgine certè natum absq; virili operâ, neq; tamen ullo modo Deum, aut Dei filium, licet bene prophetam, ac Dei legatum insignem agnoscit ac profitetur.
units.tr: That impure Mahomet, in the Alcoran, professes himself an idolater, lascivious, a lover of women, an adulterer (splendid little flowers of Christ!), and he uses words that would make even a carter blush to repeat. That impudent and slanderous mouth acknowledges and professes Christ as the Word of God, the Spirit of God and the power of God, indeed even the soul of God, born certainly of the virgin Mary without male agency; yet in no way does he acknowledge him as God or the Son of God, though he grants him to be a prophet of some note and a distinguished envoy of God.

units.la: Verùm istos praetereo lubens. Sunt enim hostes, praeter illos, alii viciniores, qui haereses horrendas & dogmata in Dn. Jesum Redemtorem nostrum blasphema, ad quae tenebris obducatur coelum, & terra cotremiscat, spargere in vulgus promiscuum non erubuere, et quae post Cerinthum et Ebionem, Arius, inque primis Samosatenus & Photinus, hominum monstra, proximo elapso seculo nostro interpolarunt, & ex inferis revocata veluti postliminio in Ecclesiam Christi introduxere, ut Satan seipsum plane superasse videri possit.
units.tr: But I gladly pass over these. For there are other enemies, nearer to us, who have not been ashamed to spread among the common people horrible heresies and dogmas blasphemous against our Lord Jesus Christ, at which heaven would be darkened and the earth would tremble. After Cerinthus and Ebion, Arius, and above all Samosatenus and Photinus, these monsters of men in the last century have corrupted these doctrines anew, and, as if recalled from the dead by right of return, have introduced them into the Church of Christ, so that Satan might seem to have surpassed himself.

units.la: Primus inter hos prodeat David Georgius Batavus, qui se postea Johannem à Bruk appella-ri voluit, impostor perniciosissimus & fœdissimus hæreticus. Hic igitur asseruit, se verù Christum & Messiam esse, Dei patris charissimù Filium, in quo se oblectet pater, natù nò ex carne, sed Spiritu S. et Spiritu Jesu C., præter alia plura, eàq; horrendiora, quæ lubens taceo. Ipse Basileæ, ubi duodecennium splendidissimè vixerat, anno salutis Christianæ 1556. mortuum & honorificè sepultus quidè, at triennio tamè post effosso cadavere, unà cum imagine, 13. Maji crematus fuit.
units.tr: Foremost among these let David Georgius of Batavia come forward, who afterwards wished to be called Johannes à Bruk, a most pernicious impostor and most foul heretic. He asserted that he was indeed the true Christ and Messiah, the most beloved Son of God the Father, in whom the Father is well pleased, born not of the flesh but of the Holy Spirit and the Spirit of Jesus Christ; besides many other things, even more horrible, which I gladly pass over. He himself died at Basel, where he had lived most splendidly for twelve years, in the year of Christian salvation 1556, and was indeed honourably buried; but three years later his corpse was dug up together with his image and burned on the 13th of May.

units.la: Postellus vero, homo ex omnibus quantumvis monstrosis hæresibus veluti conflatus, ausus est publice profiteri, Iohannam, nescio quam, Venetam, venisse servandis mulieribus, sicut Christus vivos redemisset.
units.tr: Postellus, moreover, a man compounded, as it were, out of all the most monstrous heresies, dared to profess publicly that a certain Joanna, I know not who, of Venice, had come to save women, just as Christ had redeemed the living.

units.la: Sed vel inprimis Michaël[?] ille Servetus, Hispanus, hæresiarcha, et sacra Triadis, h. e. omnis vera deitatis hostis, adeoq; teterrimum illud monstrum ex omnibus omnium temporum hæresibus conflatū, postquam aliquot annis hinc inde medicinam faciens oberrasset, tectus Michaelis Villanovani nomine, horrendas multas blasphemias sparsit. Cum Sabellio personas & essentiam confundebat: Cum Samosateno docebat, Filium ex Deo fuisse, non reipsa, sed figurative: quia in eo Deus futurum hominem geniturebat, mulierem exspectans, ex qua eum gigneret: Cum Ario, τὸν λόγον[?], tum cepisse existere, cum mundus creatus est, ac etiam ideam quandam fuisse ex tribus increatis Elementis compositam: Cum Eutyche, conceptum fuisse Filium in utero virginis ex ipsa verbi essentia, in carne transeunte, qua postea in deitatem fuerit absorpta: Cum Marcione etiam, non verum, sed imaginarium corpus Christo tribuebat, cum illud negaret ex femine Abrahae simpliciter fuisse genitum, sed partim etiam ex tribus illis Elementis conflatum, & substantiali quadam Dei facie, qua ab initio sanctis Patribus visa fuisset: Et cum Apollinari, animam Christi sane reipsa exinaniebat, cum illam diceret par[?]im ex humano partim ex divino spiritu fuisse compositam.
units.tr: But above all that Spaniard Michael[?] Servetus, the heresiarch, the enemy of the sacred Trinity, that is, of all true deity, and that most hideous monster compounded of all the heresies of all times, after he had wandered here and there for some years practising medicine, spread many horrible blasphemies under the name of Michael Villanovanus. With Sabellius he confused the persons and the essence; with Samosatenus he taught that the Son was from God not in reality but figuratively, because God was going to beget in him a man, waiting for a woman from whom he would bring him forth; with Arius, he held that the Word (τὸν λόγον[?]) began to exist when the world was created, and also that there was a certain idea composed of three uncreated elements; with Eutyches, that the Son was conceived in the womb of the virgin from the very essence of the Word, changed into flesh, which was afterwards absorbed into the deity; with Marcion too, he attributed to Christ not a true but an imaginary body, while denying that it was simply born of the seed of Abraham, but partly also compounded of those three elements, and of a certain substantial form of God, which had been seen by the holy Fathers from the beginning; and with Apollinaris he indeed emptied out the soul of Christ in reality, saying that it was partly composed of a human spirit and partly of a divine spirit.

units.la: Summatim ut universa comprehendam, foedissime homo improbus de tota Trinitate, de Christi humana natura, de puerorum Baptismo, de fide, de justitia, de tota denique religione senti-re, loqui, scribere. Servetus iste, homo sceleratus, qui Dei substantiam mutabilem fecit, & rerum omnium partem esse docuit: qui Filii Dei æternitatem negavit: qui personam æternam Fi-lii Diabolicam ideam & fabulosam chimæram appellare non erubuit: qui unionem naturarum hypo-staticam sustulit: qui Spiritus sancti hypo-stasin ac divinitatem esse inficiatus: qui Patrem, Filium, Spiritum Sanctum triceps monstrum, & Cerberum quendam tricipitem seu tripartitum, {horrifico referens} deniq; imaginarios Deos, illusiones, ac tres Spiritus dæmoniorum, toties appellitavit, æternam Dei Majestatem nefandè & horribiliter blasphemando: qui animam mortalitatem asseruit: qui veterem Israelitarum Ecclesiam in haram porcorum transformavit: qui Mosen ridiculum impostorem fuisse scripsit; qui Catabaptismum defendit: qui deniq; Deo viven-ti maledixit.
units.tr: To sum up the whole matter: that wicked man thought, spoke and wrote most foully about the whole Trinity, about the human nature of Christ, about the baptism of infants, about faith, about justice, and in short about the whole of religion. This Servetus, a criminal man, who made the substance of God mutable and taught that he is a part of all things; who denied the eternity of the Son of God; who did not hesitate to call the eternal person of the Son a diabolical idea and a fabulous chimera; who abolished the hypostatic union of the natures; who denied that the Holy Spirit is a hypostasis and divine; who, describing the Father, Son and Holy Spirit as a three-headed monster and a certain three-headed or tripartite Cerberus, (horrible to relate), and finally as imaginary gods, illusions, and three spirits of demons, so often gave them names, blaspheming the eternal majesty of God in an unspeakable and dreadful manner; who asserted that the soul is mortal; who transformed the ancient Church of the Israelites into a sty of pigs; who wrote that Moses was a ridiculous impostor; who defended Catabaptism; and who finally cursed the living God.

units.la: Quin tantum fuit incarnati ipsius Diaboli furor, ut non dubitarit dicere, Diabolus inesse divinitatem, Imo singulis plures inesse Deos: quia deitas substantialiter tam illis quam ligno & lapidi communicata fuerit. Parum ratus, ista publice sparsisse. sparsisse, ni etiam abominandas Judaeorum bla-sphemias in Christianam religionem effusas, excusaret; et foeda Mahometis verba: Tres in Tri-nitate personas, velut ipse ait, tres Deos, Patribus fuisse incognitas, et esse filios Beelzebub, approbaret. Equidem bonus iste vir in Africam trajiciens, (qua hodie Barbariam vocant) et inter Turcas agens, cum horum Doctoribus de doctrina & religione contulit; neque eo contentus, in Judaeorum quoque Synagogis sese volutavit. Ex utraque igitur illa, Mahometica & Judaica Schola tantum profecit Servetus, ut in tam egregium Doctorem evaderet scilicet.
units.tr: Indeed the fury of this very incarnate Devil was so great that he did not hesitate to say that the divinity dwells in the Devil, and moreover that several gods dwell in each thing, because deity had been communicated in substance to them just as to wood and stone. He thought it too little to have spread these things publicly, unless he also excused the abominable blasphemies of the Jews poured out against the Christian religion, and approved the foul words of Mahomet: that there are three persons in the Trinity, as he himself says, three gods, unknown to the Fathers, and that they are sons of Beelzebub. Indeed this good man, crossing over into Africa (which today they call Barbary), and living among the Turks, conferred with their teachers about doctrine and religion; and not content with this, he also wallowed in the synagogues of the Jews. Thus it was from that Mahometan and Jewish school together that Servetus profited so much that he turned out to be such an outstanding teacher, as one might expect.

units.la: Ob quas triginta annorum blasphemias execrabiles atque ab ipsis inferis revocatas, quibus tum voce tum scripto caelum ac terram infecerat, & ob incredibilem contumaciam, quod religione Christianam universam contumeliosissime proscinderet, conspueret, conculcaret, neque ulla emendationis spes affulgendo appareret, ex Magnifici Se-natus Genevensis sententia perditus atque scelveratus, supplicio, quod homo pestilentissimus merebatur, affectus, & ustulata blasphema lingua, crematus est vivus.
units.tr: For these execrable blasphemies, carried on for thirty years and dragged back, as it were, from the very depths of hell, with which he had polluted heaven and earth by voice and by writing, and on account of his incredible obstinacy, since he most abusively tore apart, spat upon and trampled underfoot the whole Christian religion, and since no hope of amendment appeared, he was condemned by the sentence of the Most Illustrious Senate of Geneva as lost and accursed. Subjected to the punishment which that most pestilential man deserved, and with his blasphemous tongue burned out, he was burned alive.

units.la: Longe tamen in hoc infelicior, quod adduci nullo modo potuit, ut, cum ad rogum deduceretur, edito poenitentiae signo aliquo, totidem verbis blasphemiae veniam peteret: Dn. Je-su, Fili Dei aeterne, miserere mei.
units.tr: He was, however, all the more unhappy in this, that he could by no means be brought, when he was led to the stake, to give some sign of repentance and to ask pardon for his blasphemy in these very words: "Lord Jesus, eternal Son of God, have mercy on me."

units.la: Plura de Serveto diximus, quam forsan putaris, Lector benevole. At hoc id consilio fa[?]Elum, quod ex hujus Magistri schola male feria-ti discipuli complures, ceu ex equo quodam Trojano, prodierint, qui si praeceptoris malitiam non superarint, at adaequarunt tamen. De his succin-ctior futura est nostra narratio.
units.tr: We have said more about Servetus, kind reader, than you perhaps think necessary. But we did so with this purpose: that several disciples, badly trained in this master's school, have come forth from it like men from a Trojan horse; and if they have not surpassed their teacher's malice, they have at least equalled it. Our account of them will be more concise.

units.la: Vix desierant calere infelicis Serveti cineres, cum domi illi pullulare ceperunt, exorta flamma, quae postea Ecclesias alias reformatas, Poloniam pri-mum, inde Transylvaniam & Hungariam corripuit.
units.tr: Scarcely had the ashes of the unhappy Servetus ceased to smoulder, when in his own homeland they began to sprout again; a flame broke out which afterwards seized other reformed Churches, first Poland, then from there Transylvania and Hungary.

units.la: Inter quos Johannes quidam Paulus Alciatus Mediolanensis Miles, recensetur loco primo, homo stolidi ac vesani ingenii, & plane atque ad rabiem usque phreneticus, qui Fargias Bernatum concessit; Inde in Poloniam devenit, ubi tandem ad Mahumetanos palam defecit, & Alcoranum impurissimum amplexatus.
units.tr: Among these, one Johannes Paulus Alciatus, a Milanese soldier, is listed in the first place: a man of foolish and frenzied mind, and wholly mad, even to the point of raging, who withdrew to Fargias in Bern. From there he came to Poland, where at last he openly defected to the Mahometans, embracing the most impure Alcoran.

units.la: Strenuus hujus commilito Valentinus extitit Gentilis Consentinus, teterrima Tritheitarum[?] haereseos[?] astipulator. Qui Italica, quatum[?] Geneva erat, Ecclesia Minister, venenum, ꝗ ex lacu-nis Servetanis hauserat, de Deitate Filii secunda-ria, quae ab illâ unicâ Patris ꝑfluxisset, tam atro-cibus contumeliis evomere nō dubitavit, ut nihil unquam magis impurum & detestandum Solis iste conspexerit.
units.tr: Valentinus Gentilis of Consenza, a vigorous soldier of this same army, was the most dreadful supporter of the Tritheist heresy. As minister of the Italian church at Geneva, he drew the poison he had taken from the Servetan pools and spewed out, without hesitation, such savage insults about the secondary Deity of the Son, supposedly flowing from the one Father, that this man never looked upon anything more impure or detestable than what he said.

units.la: Hic simulata poenitentia, et execrandis illis dogmatibꝰ abjuratis, à Senatu Amplissimo Genevensi è carcere dimissus, postquam jurejurando se astrinxisset, sine venia se urbe non egressurum: at mox neglecta data fidei religione, aderrores abiuratos postliminio rediens, clam & perfidus ad Gribaldum vicinū in Sabaudia profugit, & longum hinc inde iter emensus, in Poloniam ab Alciato & Blandrata evocatus, ac biennio exacto inde ejectus Moraviam, &Anaba-ptistis scatertim[?], mox etiam Viennam adiit, tandem de reditu in Sabaudiam cepit cogitare, & hac occasione Bernam Helvetiorum perductus, quòd sacrosanctam Trinitatem sceleratè impugnasset, mysterium istud adorandum nominando commentum merè humanum, atq; idolum, & quòd scripta in Filium Dei edidissset contumeliosa, ut plura prætereàm[?] lubens, (illa enim recense-re singula religio mihi fuerit) capite truncatus est.
units.tr: Feigning repentance and abjuring those execrable doctrines, he was released from the prison by the most distinguished Senate of Geneva, after binding himself with an oath not to leave the city without permission. But soon, neglecting the sanctity of his pledged faith, he returned to his former errors, which he had abjured, and fled secretly and treacherously to his neighbour Gribaldus in Savoy. After a long journey hither and thither, he was summoned to Poland by Alciatus and Blandrata. When he had spent two years there, he was expelled and went to Moravia, where he mingled with the Anabaptists in great numbers, and soon afterwards he went to Vienna. Finally he began to think of returning to Savoy, but on this occasion he was brought to Bern in Switzerland, because he had wickedly attacked the most holy Trinity, calling that adorable mystery an entirely human invention and an idol, and because he had published abusive writings against the Son of God. I pass over many other things willingly, for it would be tedious for me to list each one. He was beheaded.

units.la: Infelix ille Gentilis, qui Monarchia ad unicam Patris personam translata, quem solum & unicum αὐτόθεον esse volebat, Essentiam, id est, Essentia propagationem, tres numero, ut personas, sic etiam essentias, id est, tres numero Deos, aperte ꝓ-fiteri[?] non erubuit.
units.tr: That unhappy Gentilis did not blush to declare openly that, the monarchy having been transferred to the single person of the Father, whom he alone wished to be the one and only God, there are three essences, that is, three essences in number just as there are three persons, that is, three Gods.

units.la: Socios, praeter Alciatum, habuit Valentinus Gentilis, primarios, Georgium Blandratam Sa-lutiensem, profession Medicum, & Matthaum Gribaldum non incelebrem jurisconsultum. Horum ille, homo impudens & sceleratus Genevae negotium Trinitatis cepit convellere, at graviter à magno illo Johanne Calvino, viro beatae recordationis, refutatus, & ab eo sibi satisfactum simulans, male sibi conscius, et metuens, ne à Magistratu quaereretur, in ditionem vicinam, adpa[cum]? Fargiarum (ubi & Alciatus tum substitê-rat) refugit, & quia Medicinam diu in Poloniâ primum, deinde in Transylvania apud Reginae fecerat, eò reversus, facile ibi locum invenit, (insinuante illum in Illustrissimi cujusdam Principis gratiam Lismanino quodam Corcyrensi, magnatum Polonicae Ecclesiae autoritatis viro,) et vero nemo isto abominando non paucos infecit, unà cum Gentili, palàm factus Arianus, adeò ut cum discipulis suis nomen & doctrinam Arii sine pudore tueretur. Usus is ipse inibi est collega, Francisco Davidis, et hoc Antitrinitario, cujus blasphemia in Sacrosanctam Trinitatem, & nominatim in Filii Dei, atq; Spiritus S. Deitate, scripta, publicè praestant,at ab Orthodoxis plurib. solidè refutata.
units.tr: Besides Alciatus, Valentinus Gentilis had as his leading associates Giorgio Blandrata of Saluzzo, a physician by profession, and Matthaeus Gribaldus, a jurist of no little renown. Of these, the first, a shameless and wicked man, undertook at Geneva to overthrow the doctrine of the Trinity, but he was sharply refuted by the great John Calvin, a man of blessed memory. Pretending to be satisfied by him, but conscious of his guilt and fearing that the magistrate would call him to account, he fled into the neighbouring territory of Fargiae (where Alciatus had then also settled). Since he had practised medicine for a long time first in Poland and then in Transylvania at the court of the queen, he returned there, and easily found a place (Lismanino, a certain Corcyrean, a man of authority among the magnates of the Polish Church, introduced him into the favour of a certain most illustrious prince). And indeed this detestable man infected not a few, together with Gentilis, openly becoming an Arian, so that with his disciples he defended the name and doctrine of Arius without shame. He had as his colleague there Francis David, and this Antitrinitarian, whose blasphemy against the most holy Trinity, and especially against the deity of the Son of God and of the Holy Spirit, is set out in writings published in public, has been solidly refuted by many orthodox writers.

units.la: Hic verò, (Gribaldum dico) Fargiarū Dominus, (pagus is est in Genevâ & Bernati vicinia) blasphemiis Serveti non obscurè favere deprehensus est, nullo postea loco ullis admonitionib. vel argumentis relicto. Dei is quoq; essentiam lacerabat, & Christum fingebat novitium Deum, à Patre diversum, & cui non eadem esset cum Patre essentia. Hic postquam Vergerii favore Tubingâ introductus, at mox profugus, Bernae captus, simulataq; abnegatione, liberatus esset, ad ingenium redit, Gentilis fautor & hospes existens, & tandem divino judicio è medio sublatus, paratum sibi in terris supplicium antevertit.
units.tr: But this man (I mean Gribaldus), lord of Fargiae (a village near Geneva and in the neighbourhood of Bern), was caught clearly favouring the blasphemies of Servetus, and afterwards no admonitions or arguments were left for him in any place. He also tore apart the essence of God, and feigned that Christ was a new God, different from the Father, and not of the same essence as the Father. After he had been introduced at Tübingen through the favour of Vergerius, but soon fled, was captured at Bern, and was set free after a feigned renunciation, he returned to his former disposition, being a supporter and host of Gentilis. Finally, by divine judgment, he was removed from the world, and anticipated the punishment prepared for him on earth.

units.la: BERNHARDINUS OCHINUS Senensis, impurissimus hypocrita, & Veterator nocentissitissimus, Basileæ quid non tentavit? Arianorum iste clandestinus fautor, polygamiæ oppugnator, omnium Christianæ religionis dogmatum irrisor, Pelagianismi imprimis strenuus defensor. At nimirum is fere detectus, quando deprehensus, Dialogos illum edidisse triginta, Italica quidem lingua, at in Latina a Sebast. Castellione conversos. Et hi sane Dialogi loquuntur de hominis calliditate, qui dubitare de singulis, Academicorum more, videatur malle, quam quicquam definire. Semina certè fœdissimarū hæreseon non obscurè in illis spargū-tur. Cum hanc ob causam, & quod edito scripto publico sententiam suam de quæstionib. tum ambi-guis, tum etiam erroneis diserte & orthodoxè declarare renueret, urbe et agro Tigurino excedere iuberetur; neq; etiam Basilea aliter ferri posset, in Polonia devenit, & palàm illic hypostasin Spiritū S. oppugnavit, neq; tamen ibi diutius eisubsistere licuit. Quamobrem in Moravia ad Anabaptista-rū conventicula se recepit, et illic obiit veterator.
units.tr: BERNARDINO OCHINO of Siena, a most impure hypocrite and a most harmful old deceiver, what did he not attempt at Basel? This secret supporter of the Arians, opponent of polygamy, mocker of all the doctrines of the Christian religion, was above all a vigorous defender of Pelagianism. But he was almost certainly exposed when he was caught; he had published thirty dialogues in Italian, but they were translated into Latin by Sebastian Castellio. Indeed these dialogues speak of the cunning of a man who seems to prefer doubting every point, in the manner of the Academics, to defining anything. Surely the seeds of the most foul heresies are sown in them quite openly. For this reason, and because he refused, after publishing a public writing, to declare his opinion plainly and orthodoxly on questions that were both ambiguous and even erroneous, he was ordered to leave the city and territory of Zurich. Since he could not be tolerated at Basel either, he went to Poland, and there openly attacked the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit, yet he was not allowed to remain there any longer. Therefore he retired to the conventicles of the Anabaptists in Moravia, and there died, an old deceiver.

units.la: Sed & Sebast. Castellio Allobrox, Gracarum literarum in Academia Basileensi Professor, ex iis, quos commemoravimus, non parum contagii contraxit. Probant hoc Dialogi, quos germa-nissimus frater Lelius sub Felicis Turpionis Urbevetani nomine edidit; in quibus multorum fœdissimorum errorum fundamenta jaciuntur, & ea continentur, quæ adversarios in tuendis blasphemiis hominis istis abominandis plurimum juvare, ex horum temporum controversiis, luce meridia-na, quod nâ, quod dicere consuevimus, clarius apparet.
units.tr: But Sebastian Castellio, a Savoyard, professor of Greek literature at the Academy of Basel, also contracted no small contagion from those we have mentioned. The dialogues which his most German brother Lelius published under the name of Felix Turpio of Urbevetum prove this. In them the foundations of many most foul errors are laid, and there are contained those things which greatly help the opponents in defending the blasphemies of these abominable men, as is clearer than the noonday light, to use our usual saying, from the controversies of our own times.

units.la: Neque in exercenda ista militia, & virulenta lingua atq; stylí tela in Dn. Iesum, aeterni Patris Filium aeternum, dirigendo, postremus fuit La-lius Socinus Senensis, Mariani Iurisconsulti F. Tiguri diu versatus, ac ibidem tandem etiam mortuus, homo ingenii plane Academici, & incredibiliter ad contradicendum ac varios nectendum [illegible, ~5 letters] comparatus, nec non egregius dissimulator, ita quidem, ut quid is animo meditaretur suo, quod, inquam, perditissimus Samosatenianus & Arianus esset, haeresibus hoc genus aliis pernitiosissimis laboraret, nonnisi post illius mortem cognosceretur, postquam in Ecclesiis Evangelicis peragrandis Melanchthoni, Calvino, Camerario turpiter imposuisset, insignis & astutissimus hypocrita. Nam & sub Martini Bellii nomine fictitio, ὀρθοδοξίαν[?] insidiose oppugnavit, eumque Serveti, Castellionis, Ochini deniq; furoribus fuisse, compertum est. In Samosateni partes clam eum transiisse, argumento est, quod verbum Dei, ac praesertim primum Evangelii Johannis caput adeo veteratorie & plane versute depravavit, ut videatur omnium ejus corruptorum impietatem longe superasse.
units.tr: Nor was Lelius Socinus of Siena the last to take up this warfare and to aim the weapons of a virulent tongue and pen at the Lord Jesus, the eternal Son of the eternal Father. Son of the jurist Marianus, he long lived at Zurich and at last died there. He was a man of a thoroughly academic talent, incredibly prepared for contradicting and for weaving various [illegible], and also an outstanding dissembler. So much so that what he privately intended, namely that he was a most desperate Samosatenian and Arian, and was troubled by other most pernicious heresies of this kind, was known only after his death. Having toured the Evangelical churches, he shamefully deceived Melanchthon, Calvin and Camerarius, being a notable and most cunning hypocrite. For under the fictitious name of Martin Bellius he insidiously attacked orthodoxy [ὀρθοδοξίαν], and it has been established that he was of the same fury as Servetus, Castellio and finally Ochino. That he secretly passed over to the side of Samosatenus is evident from the fact that he so corrupted the word of God, and especially the first chapter of the Gospel of John, with such deceitful and utterly crafty skill, that he seems to have far surpassed the impiety of all these corrupters.

units.la: Iisdem annis Franciscus Stancarus (Mantuanus, homo pestilentissimus, virulentis dogmatibus Poloniam inficere cepit, asserendo, Christum non esse, nisi secundum humanam naturam, Mediatorem; Arianismi insimulans, quotcunque illi dicerent,
units.tr: In the same years Francis Stancarus of Mantua, a most pestilential man, began to infect Poland with virulent doctrines, asserting that Christ is a Mediator only according to his human nature, and charging with Arianism as many as said otherwise,

units.la: AD LECTOREM.
units.tr: TO THE READER.

units.la: dicerent, quatenus etiam Deus sit, Mediatorem esse, quasi facerent Filium Patre minorem. Ex istius hominis importunitate scissa Polonica Ecclesia, atque hinc evenit, ut nonnulli imperitiores, Stancari refutandi studio, in errorem Tritheitarum inciderent, cum Blandrata, & aliis complicibus, sic afferentes Christum esse secundum utramque naturam Mediatorem, ut Deitatem, inaequalitate induta, multiplicarent. Proinde volentes illi vitare Nestorii praecipitium, in Arii vel Tritheitarum abyssum irruerunt imprudentes. Hinc res eo deducta, ut incendium, quod jam ante quoq; exortum fuerat, postmodum tota vastata Polonia, in Transylvaniam quoq; pervaserit, Gregorio quodam Paulo impurissimis libellis suis pestilentissimos errores spargente, & eo insania progrediente, ut & receptos in Ecclesia orthodoxa loquendi modos, de una Dei essentia, & de uno Deo in tribus personis, Diaboli stratagemata indigitare homo improbus non verereatur: Et Petro quodam Statorio operam suam fucandis Blandrata barbarissimi Scriptoris commentis navante, etsi illi ipsi Antitrinitarii in sectas tres diversas, Tritheitas, Arianos, & Samosatenianos scinderentur.
units.tr: they said, insofar as God is also a mediator, as if they made the Son less than the Father. Through this man's importunity the Polish Church was torn apart, and from this it came about that some less experienced men, in their eagerness to refute Stancarus, fell into the error of the Tritheites, along with Blandrata and other accomplices. They so asserted that Christ is mediator according to both natures that, by introducing inequality, they multiplied the Deity. Therefore those men, wishing to avoid the precipice of Nestorius, rashly plunged into the abyss of Arius or of the Tritheites. From there matters went so far that the fire, which had already broken out earlier, after all of Poland had been laid waste, spread also into Transylvania. Gregorius Paulus, a certain man, scattered the most pestilent errors in his most impure pamphlets, and his madness advanced so far that this wicked man did not hesitate to call the accepted modes of speaking in the orthodox Church, concerning the one essence of God and the one God in three persons, stratagems of the Devil. Petrus Statorius, a certain man, lent his efforts to dressing up these errors with the fabrications of Blandrata, a most barbarous writer, although those same Antitrinitarians were split into three different sects: Tritheites, Arians and Samosatenes.

units.la: Quæ reliqua adhuc sunt, brevissimè pertexā, Heidelbergæ publicè in Ecclesia docuêre, Johan-nes Sylvanus et Adamus Neüserus, quos par haereticorum perditissimum vere dixerus. Uterque Arianismum in sinu fovit. Sylvanus scelerata blasphemia convictus capitis supplicium subivit.
units.tr: What remains I shall go through briefly. At Heidelberg, Johannes Sylvanus and Adamus Neuserus, whom one may rightly call a pair of most ruinous heretics, taught publicly in the Church. Both nursed Arianism in their bosom. Sylvanus, convicted of wicked blasphemy, underwent capital punishment.

units.la: Friderico III. Electore Palatino, at quanto Princi-pe! gravissimis de caussis hoc jubente, Neuse-rus è vinculis, haudscio, quâ ratione evasit, & ad Turcas sese protripuit, ubi ejurata religione Christianâ, Alcoranum esse professus, ac miserrimè perüt.
units.tr: Under Frederick III, Elector Palatine, but what a prince! who ordered this for the gravest reasons, Neuserus, I know not by what means, escaped from his chains and fled to the Turks, where, having renounced the Christian religion, he professed the Koran and perished most wretchedly.

units.la: Et bonos tamen Ubiquetarios totics recoctam crambem de Arianismo, cui doctrina nostra Orthodoxa favet & viam aperiat, reponere non pudet. Quam atrocem calumniam tot nostrorum scripta solidè refutarunt; quam supplicia, de Serveto, Gentili & Sylvano sumta, refutarunt: quorum mortem & supplicium isti ipsi Aristarcha sibi valde displicere, in suis scriptis, cum magno stomacho ostendunt.
units.tr: And yet the good Ubiquitarians are not ashamed to serve up again the crambe repetita about Arianism, to which our orthodox doctrine is favourable and opens the way. Many of our writings have solidly refuted this atrocious calumny; they have refuted the punishments taken against Servetus, Gentilis and Sylvanus, whose death and punishment those very Aristarchs show in their writings, with great spleen, to be deeply displeasing to them.

units.la: Restat Faustus Socinus, Lælii F., qui universum doctrinam Christianam corpus in suis scriptis, præsertim iis, quæ in Covetum edidit, convellere, & religione novam introducere homo haereticissimus non veretur. At quem Lubbertus Sibrandus, Orthodoxorum ocellus, solidè & graviter refutavit. Astipulatores habet Socinus, etsi inter se in nonnullis non parum dissentientes, Johanne Erasmi Soldwedelensem, olim Lipsiensis Academiae discipulum, Johannem Sommerum Pirnen-sem Misnicū, Christophorum Osiorodum Goslariensem Saxonē, Valentinum Smalzium Gothanum Thuringum, quendam Eniedinum, & Antitrinitarios alios quamplurimos, qui Photinianos se profitentur, à Photino Syrmiensis Ecclesiae Presbytero, Bytero[?], cuius hae fuerunt blasphemiae, quae sequun-tur. Negavit Trinitatem: Christum purum hominem esse docuit: At illi communicatam realiter omnipotentiam: (quod ipsum hodie Ubiquetarii tradunt de reali Idiomatum effusione) prorsinde esse Deum creatum, sanctum, & tem-poralem: & Filium Dei aeterni, non tamen aeter-num: nec Sp. Sanctum, Deum. Ob quos tetros errores in Synodo Syrmiensi est condemnatus.
units.tr: There remains Faustus Socinus, son of Laelius, who, a most heretical man, does not hesitate to overthrow the whole body of Christian doctrine in his writings, especially those he published at Covetum, and to introduce a new religion. But Lubbertus Sibrandus, the eye of the orthodox, refuted him solidly and gravely. Socinus has supporters, though not a little at odds among themselves on some points: Johannes Erasmi of Soldwedel, formerly a pupil of the Academy of Leipzig; Johannes Sommer of Pirna in Meissen; Christophorus Osiorodus of Goslar in Saxony; Valentinus Smalzius of Gotha in Thuringia; a certain Eniedinus; and many other Antitrinitarians who profess themselves Photinians, after Photinus, presbyter of the Church of Sirmium, whose blasphemies were these that follow. He denied the Trinity; he taught that Christ was a mere man, to whom omnipotence was really communicated (which the Ubiquitarians today also teach concerning the real effusion of the properties); that he is therefore a created, holy and temporal God, and the Son of the eternal God but not eternal; and that the Holy Spirit is not God. For these foul errors he was condemned in the Synod of Sirmium.

units.la: Huic Socino & affectis grave scriptum oppo-suit Otto Casmanus p. m. fidelis Ecclesiae Staden-sis Ministri, quod tecum, benevole Lector, communicamus, neq; hoc sine gravissimis causis, scilicet quod in media, prob dolor! Germania, ea[?] in ipso Ecclesiae gremio, Socinianismi femina repullulare, & radices agere altas, obscurum amplius non sit.
units.tr: Against this Socinus and his adherents, Otto Casmann, of blessed memory, minister of the faithful Church of Stade, set forth a weighty writing, which we share with you, kind reader, and not without the gravest reasons: namely, that in the midst of Germany, alas, the seeds of Socinianism are sprouting again in the very bosom of the Church and striking deep roots, and this is no longer obscure.

units.la: Vt vero, quoties de superioris atq; etiam nostri seculi haeresibus cogitamus, nos cohorrescere par est, ob Diabolo odium & malitiam, quae hominum mentes fascinare & dementare non desinit, ut illos in exitium praecipit et sempiternum: ita deplorandum est hominum infirmitas, quae tanta est, ut Diaboli potentia resistere illi nequeant, nisi a Deo regantur. Itaque Deus orandus est, ut furoribus Satanae resistat, & fanaticorum conatus reprimat, Ecclesiam vero tueatur, & nos omnes in veritate sanctificet, denique benignum[?] efficiat, ut omnes in Christo Iesu simus unum. Amen. Vale, pie Lector, & nobis fave. E nostro eremo[?]: Die XVI. Aug. ex natali Friderici V. Electoris Palatini, ut quam chari nobis capitis! nobilitate, Anno MDCXII.
units.tr: But just as, whenever we think of the heresies of the former century and of our own, we ought to shudder at the hatred and malice of the Devil, which does not cease to bewitch and drive mad men's minds, so as to hurl them headlong into eternal destruction, so we must lament human weakness, which is so great that men cannot resist the power of the Devil unless they are ruled by God. Therefore God must be prayed to, that he may resist the furies of Satan and restrain the attempts of the fanatics, that he may protect the Church and sanctify us all in the truth, and finally make us kind, so that we may all be one in Christ Jesus. Amen. Farewell, pious reader, and favour us. From our hermitage, on the 16th day of August, the birthday of Frederick V, Elector Palatine, how dear to us is the nobility of our head! In the year 1612.

units.la: CAPUT I. DE FIDE CHRISTIANA CHRISTIANISMI. SECTIO I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I. OF THE CHRISTIAN FAITH OF CHRISTIANITY. SECTION I.

units.la: FIDES CHRISTIANA respicit vel doctrinam credendorum Christiano ad salutem, vel hominem Christianum, in quo est, & per quam hic credens & fidelis est.
units.tr: The Christian faith looks either to the doctrine of things to be believed by a Christian for salvation, or to the Christian man, in whom it resides and through whom the believer is faithful.

units.la: I. FIDES respiciens doctrinam, tradit salutarem ex verbo Dei sapientiam credendorum Christiano ad salutem.
units.tr: I. Faith, looking to doctrine, delivers the saving wisdom from the Word of God concerning the things to be believed by a Christian for salvation.

units.la: Credenda haec breviter constringuntur Symbolo Apostolico, quod est breve quoddam rerum creditu ad salutem necessariarum compendium.
units.tr: These things to be believed are briefly comprised in the Apostles' Creed, which is a short compendium of the things necessary to be believed for salvation.

units.la: Partes Symboli huius duae sunt, una de Deo, altera de Ecclesia.
units.tr: The parts of this Creed are two: one concerning God, the other concerning the Church.

units.la: In Deo considerantur Essentia ejus & Personae. Essentia Dei est absoluta perfe&tiffimaq;[?] Dei Natura, per quam Deus revera esse & subsistere intelligitur. Exod.3.verf.14. Galat.4.verf.8. Apoc.1.ver.8. Estque haec una, & quidem Numero. Deut.4.v.35. Cap.6.v.4. Cap.32.v.39. Ief. 37.v.16. Cap.44.v.1. Cap.45.v.5. Cap.46. v.9. Rom.3.v.30. 1.Corinth.8.v.4. &c.
units.tr: In God we consider his essence and persons. The essence of God is the absolute and most perfect nature of God, by which God is understood to truly be and to subsist. Exod. 3, v. 14; Gal. 4, v. 8; Rev. 1, v. 8. And this essence is one, and indeed one in number. Deut. 4, v. 35; ch. 6, v. 4; ch. 32, v. 39; Isa. 37, v. 16; ch. 44, v. 1; ch. 45, v. 5; ch. 46, v. 9; Rom. 3, v. 30; 1 Cor. 8, v. 4; etc.

units.la: Hujus essentiae divinae quaedam descriptiones in scripturis ad nostrum ca-ptum fiunt per attributa, tum absoluta, qualia sunt Simplicitas, Immutabilitas, Aeternitas, Immensitas: tum relata, certum ad creaturas respectum includentia, ut sunt Omnipotentia, Omnisapientia, Bonitas, Justitia, Veritas, &c.
units.tr: Certain descriptions of this divine essence are given in the Scriptures, for our capacity, through attributes: some absolute, such as simplicity, immutability, eternity, immensity; others relative, including a definite respect to creatures, such as omnipotence, omniscience, goodness, justice, truth, etc.

units.la: Persona hoc loco est subsistentia in Essentia divina, quae ad alios relata proprietate incommunicabili distinguitur.
units.tr: Here "person" is a subsistence in the divine essence, which, related to others, is distinguished by an incommunicable property.

units.la: Personae Deitatis tres sunt: Pater, Filius, & Spiritus Sanctus.
units.tr: There are three persons of the Godhead: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Pater est prima Deitatis persona a nullo alio existens, filiumque ab aeter-no gignens, 1. Corinth.8.v.6. Psalm.2. v. 7. 2. Corinth.1.v.1.
units.tr: The Father is the first person of the Godhead, existing from no other, and begetting the Son from eternity. 1 Cor. 8, v. 6; Ps. 2, v. 7; 2 Cor. 1, v. 1.

units.la: Pater in Symbolo dicitur Omnipotens Creator Cœli & Terræ. Credendum itaque in Patrem Omnipotentem Creatorem omnium bonorum, Omnisapientem Gubernatorem Bonorum & Malorum, misericordem datorem Filii sui in Servatorem.
units.tr: In the Creed the Father is called the Almighty Creator of heaven and earth. Therefore we are to believe in God the Father Almighty, the Creator of all good things, the All-wise Governor of good and evil, and the merciful giver of his Son as Saviour.

units.la: 1. Deus enim in principio res omnes bonas, partim ex nihilo, partim ex materia ab ipso creata solo verbo potentiæ suæ fecit, Gen. cap.1. & 2. Psalm. 33. v.6. & 9. Hebr. 11. v. 3. 2. Pet. 3. v. 5.
units.tr: 1. For God in the beginning made all good things, partly out of nothing and partly out of matter created by himself, by the mere word of his power. Gen. chs. 1 and 2; Ps. 33, vv. 6 and 9; Heb. 11, v. 3; 2 Pet. 3, v. 5.

units.la: 2. Deus etiam res singulas à se conditas omnésque illarum actiones sapientissimè gubernat, mala etiam fieri permittit, iisq; justissimè uti novit ad electorum suorum salutem & impiorum pœnam. Exod. 21. v. 13. Devt. 9. v. 4. Poverb. 16. verf. 33. Matth. 10. verf. 29. 30. Luc. 12. v. 6. 7. &c.
units.tr: 2. God also governs each of the things he has created, and all their actions, most wisely; he permits even evil things to happen, and he knows how to use them most justly for the salvation of his elect and the punishment of the wicked. Exod. 21, v. 13; Deut. 9, v. 4; Prov. 16, v. 33; Matt. 10, vv. 29–30; Luke 12, vv. 6–7; etc.

units.la: 3. Sic verò Deus Pater dilexit Mundum, ut unigenitum filium suum dederit (in Salvatorem) ut omnis qui credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam, Johannis 3.
units.tr: 3. Indeed, God the Father so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son (as Saviour), so that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. John 3.

units.la: FILIUS est secunda Deitatis persona, à Patre per æternam & incomprehensibilem generationem exsistens, qui Redemtor noster est ad vitam æternam. Matth. 13. versic. 17. Johan. 1. v. 14. 18.34. Cap.3.v.16. Rom.1.v.4.Cap.8.v.32.&c.
units.tr: The SON is the second person of the Godhead, existing from the Father by an eternal and incomprehensible generation, who is our Redeemer to eternal life. Matt. 13, v. 17; John 1, vv. 14, 18; 3, 4; 3, v. 16; Rom. 1, v. 4; 8, v. 32; etc.

units.la: Hic in Symbolo dicitur 1. JESUS, quia Servator noster est Doctrinâ, merito & Efficaciâ. 2. CHRISTUS, quia ad nostram salutem est unctus in Doctorem, Sacerdotem & Regem, ut ita nobis adjudicemus Christū, ut Dei Patris donum, ad nos pertinens, eum toto corde apprehendamus; ut nostrū, & certò speremus, eum semper nos salutariter curaturum. 3. Dominus noster, quia nos creavit & recreavit, redemit & ex omni potestate diaboli liberavit.
units.tr: In the Creed he is called: 1. JESUS, because he is our Saviour by his teaching, merit and efficacy. 2. CHRIST, because for our salvation he has been anointed as Teacher, Priest and King, so that we may appropriate Christ to ourselves, as the gift of God the Father pertaining to us, and apprehend him with our whole heart, and, as ours, surely hope that he will always care for us savingly. 3. Our Lord, because he created and re-created us, redeemed us, and set us free from all the power of the devil.

units.la: De Christo Jesu unigenito Filio Dei Patris Domino nostro, Symbolū proponit credenda, PRIMÒ Incarnationem & Nativitatem.
units.tr: Concerning Christ Jesus, the only-begotten Son of God the Father, our Lord, the Creed sets forth the things to be believed: FIRST, the Incarnation and Nativity.

units.la: INCARNATIO Filii Dei est, quâipse ex SS. Trinitatis decreto, tempore definito (1. Pet. 1. v. 20. Galat. 4. v. 4.) Natu-ram tam assumens humanam, in carne manifestatus est. 1. Timoth. 3. v. 16.
units.tr: The INCARNATION of the Son of God is that by which he himself, by the decree of the Holy Trinity, at a defined time (1 Pet. 1, v. 20; Gal. 4, v. 4), assuming human nature, was made manifest in the flesh. 1 Tim. 3, v. 16.

units.la: Hujus partes duę sunt, Conceptio Christi & personalis duarum naturarum Unitio.
units.tr: Its parts are two: the conception of Christ and the personal union of the two natures.

units.la: Conceptio Christi est, quâ Filius Dei ex virginis Mariæ fœmine per immediatâ ac miraculosam Spiritus S. operationem, factus est homo. Isa. 7. v. 14. Luc. 1. v. 31. 35. Gal. 4. v. 4. Matth. 1. v. 18. & 20.
units.tr: The conception of Christ is that by which the Son of God was made man from the woman, the virgin Mary, through the immediate and miraculous operation of the Holy Spirit. Isa. 7, v. 14; Luke 1, vv. 31, 35; Gal. 4, v. 4; Matt. 1, vv. 18, 20.

units.la: Personalis duarum naturarum unitio, est divinæ & humanæ naturæ in unam hypostasin seu personam copulatio, inconfuse, incommutabiliter, indivisè, & inseparabiliter facta.
units.tr: The personal union of the two natures is the joining of the divine and human natures into one hypostasis or person, effected unconfusedly, unchangeably, indivisibly and inseparably.

units.la: Nativitas est, quâ Filius Dei secundû humanam naturam, expleto mensium ordinariorum spatio, ex utero Mariæ Matris parientis, in lucem est editus. Luc. 2. v. 4. Matth. 2. &c.
units.tr: The nativity is that by which the Son of God, according to his human nature, when the ordinary span of months was complete, was brought into the light from the womb of his mother Mary as she gave birth. Luke 2, v. 4; Matt. 2, etc.

units.la: SECUNDO Credenda de Christo proponuntur hæc quinque.
units.tr: SECONDLY, the following five things are set forth as to be believed concerning Christ.

units.la: 1. Passio Christi, quâ Christus per omnem vitam suam, nunc in corpore, nunc in animâ, nunc in utroq; varios dolores ac ignominias sustinuit; in primis vero solennem illum, gravissimumque Passionis actum in vitæ extremo.
units.tr: 1. The passion of Christ, by which Christ, throughout his whole life, sometimes in body, sometimes in soul, sometimes in both, endured various sorrows and ignominies; above all, that solemn and most grievous act of the Passion at the end of his life.

units.la: 2. CRUCIFIXIO, qua Christus ligno Crucis ignominiosissimè tanquā execrabilis & maledictus affixus fuit.
units.tr: 2. The CRUCIFIXION, by which Christ was fixed to the wood of the cross most ignominiously, as one accursed and cursed.

units.la: 3. MORS Christi, quia vera facta est animæ Christi à corpore separatio: salva interim manente personali naturarum duarum, divinæ & humanæ, unione.
units.tr: 3. The DEATH of Christ, because there was a true separation of the soul of Christ from the body, while meanwhile the personal union of the two natures, divine and human, remained intact.

units.la: 4. SEPULTURA, qua corpus Christi jam mortui de cruce, & in sepulcro conditum est.
units.tr: 4. The BURIAL, by which the body of Christ, now dead, was taken down from the cross and laid in the sepulchre.

units.la: 5. DESCENSUS ad Inferos, qui aliis extremus exinanitionis Christi gradus, aliis vero primus exaltationis dicitur.
units.tr: 5. The DESCENT into Hell, which some call the last step of the humiliation of Christ, but others the first step of his exaltation.

units.la: TERTIO de Christo credenda traduntur hæc quatuor.
units.tr: THIRDLY, the following four things are handed down as to be believed concerning Christ.

units.la: 1. RESURRECTIO Christi, qua Christus secundum humanam naturam, virtute Deitatis revivisc[?]ens, tertio post mortem die è sepulcro gloriosè exivit.
units.tr: 1. The RESURRECTION of Christ, by which Christ, according to his human nature, reviving by the power of the Godhead, gloriously came out of the sepulchre on the third day after death.

units.la: 2. ASCENSIO in Cœlum, qua postquam à resurrectione per quadraginta dies subinde discipulis suis apparuisset, tandem in monte Oliveti eis benedixit, atqj valedixit, statimqj spectantib[?] eis corpore suo sursum libratus, & nube interveniente e discipulorum conspectu ablatus, & in Coelum translatus est, Act. 1.[?]
units.tr: 2. The ASCENSION into Heaven, by which, after he had appeared from time to time to his disciples for forty days after the resurrection, at last on the Mount of Olives he blessed them and took his leave, and immediately, while they watched, was lifted up by his body, and, a cloud intervening, was taken from the sight of the disciples and carried into Heaven. Acts 1.

units.la: 3. SESSIO ad dextrā Dei Patris, qua ipseChristus Regnū suum redemtione partum plenissime occupans, consedit ad dextram Majestatis Dei in excelsis, quave Pater gloriæ sedere fecit Jesum Christū ad dextram suam in cœlestib. supra omnem principatū, ac potestate, & virtutem, & dominium, & omne nomen, q; nominatur, non solum in hoc seculo, verū etiam in futuro, & omnia subiecit sub pedes illius, & dedit eum Caput ipsi Ecclesiæ, q est Corpus ipsi, complementum ejus, qui omnia in omnibus adimplet. Hebr. 1, Ephs. 1.
units.tr: 3. The SESSION at the right hand of God the Father, by which Christ himself, most fully occupying the kingdom won by his redemption, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty of God on high; and by which the Father of glory made Jesus Christ sit at his right hand in the heavenly places, above every principality and power and virtue and dominion and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the age to come; and he put all things under his feet, and gave him as head over all to the Church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all. Heb. 1; Eph. 1.

units.la: 4. REDITVS Christi ad Judicium, quo in novissimo mundi die, excitabit mortuos ut revivi scant, viventes oculi momento immutabit, & totum genus humanum in conspectum suum sistet, & in duo agmina divisum, alterum sibi ad dexteram, alterum ad leva collocabit, tandeq; sententiam feret, qua dextrū agmen vitæ, sinistrum vero igni & morti æternæ adjudicabitur. Matth 25.
units.tr: 4. The RETURN of Christ to Judgment, when on the last day of the world he will raise the dead to live again, will change the living in a moment, and will set the whole human race before his sight, and, divided into two companies, will place one at his right hand and the other at his left; and then he will pronounce sentence, by which the right-hand company will be adjudged to life, and the left-hand company to fire and eternal death. Matt. 25.

units.la: Hæc de Filio Dei credēda: SPIRI-TUS S. est tertia Deitatis persona, à Patre & Filio ab æterno & incomprehensibiliter procedens, qui Sanctificator noster est ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: These are the things to be believed concerning the Son of God. The HOLY SPIRIT is the third person of the Godhead, proceeding from the Father and the Son from eternity and incomprehensibly, who is our Sanctifier to eternal life.

units.la: Credendum itaq; , Spiritum S. esse verum Deum cum Patre & Filio, à Patre & Filio incomprehensibili modo procedentem, eum ut donum, morte & intercessione Christi nobis partum esse, & eum coepisse nos sanctificare, & in posterum magis magisq; sanctificaturum ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Therefore we are to believe that the Holy Spirit is true God with the Father and the Son, proceeding from the Father and the Son in an incomprehensible manner; that he has been given to us as a gift, procured for us by the death and intercession of Christ; and that he has begun to sanctify us, and will sanctify us more and more in time to come, to eternal life.

units.la: HACTENUS CREDENDA DE DEO IN SYMBOLO.
units.tr: HITHERTO THE THINGS TO BE BELIEVED CONCERNING GOD IN THE CREED.

units.la: Ecclesia sancta, est multitudo hominū per Evangelii prædicationem efficaciter vocatorū, ad Fidem, Spem, & Caritatem, adeoq; ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: The holy Church is the multitude of men effectually called through the preaching of the Gospel to faith, hope and love, and so to eternal life.

units.la: Ea est vel Catholica, vel particularis.
units.tr: It is either Catholic or particular.

units.la: Catholica est ex universis regionibus & populis collecta, & per universas regiones & populos sparsa. Particularis est quivis coetus unius gentis, aut civitatis, aut uniuscujusque particularis loci, Christum colens.
units.tr: The Catholic Church is gathered from all regions and peoples, and scattered through all regions and peoples. A particular Church is any assembly of one nation, or city, or of any particular place, that worships Christ.

units.la: Ecclesiæ Catholicæ bonum tum in Genere, tum in Specie, consideratur.
units.tr: The good of the Catholic Church is considered both in its genus and in its species.

units.la: Bonum ejus in genere, est Communio Sanctorum, quæ est eorundem communium bonorum participatio, ad quæ omnes & soli sancti jus habent.
units.tr: Its good in general is the communion of saints, which is the participation in those common goods, to which all the saints, and only the saints, have a right.

units.la: Estq; tum Sanctorum cum Deo, tum eorundem inter se.
units.tr: And this is both of the saints with God and of the saints among themselves.

units.la: Communio Sanctorum cum Deo, est gratiosa Dei in credentibus habitatio, omnia ipsis salutaria donafrueda dantis.
units.tr: The communion of the saints with God is the gracious indwelling of God in believers, God giving them all things salutary to be enjoyed.

units.la: Communio Sanctorum inter se, est unio omnium Christi membrorum in unum corpus, per Spiritum Sanctum omnib. inhabitantem facta, eorumq; obligatio ad bona accepta in commune cōmodum, in primis autē in capitis sui Christi gloriam promtē & alacriter conferenda.
units.tr: The communion of the saints among themselves is the union of all the members of Christ into one body, effected through the Holy Spirit dwelling in all of them, and their obligation to bring the goods they have received into common use for the benefit of all, but above all to contribute them readily and eagerly to the glory of their Head, Christ.

units.la: Bonum in specie consideratum est triplex.
units.tr: The good considered in its species is threefold.

units.la: I. REMISSIO Peccatorum, quâ Deus & culpam & pœnam peccatorum ex mera gratia credentibus remittit, eosque in filios adoptat, ob perfectissimam filii sui unigeniti satisfactionem.
units.tr: I. The REMISSION of sins, by which God, out of pure grace, remits to believers both the guilt and the punishment of their sins, and adopts them as sons, on account of the most perfect satisfaction of his only-begotten Son.

units.la: Hanc peccatorum remissione immediate sequitur Sanctificatio, quæ est Naturæ corruptæ ad imaginem Dei per Spiritum Sanctum renovatio.
units.tr: Immediately following this remission of sins is sanctification, which is the renewal of corrupt nature into the image of God through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Hujus partes duæ sunt: I. Mortificatio Carnis, per quam vitiosa naturæ nostræ inclinatio & dispositio paulatim aboletur & frangitur. II. Vivificatio Spiritus, per quem vitiosæ dispositioni sive inclinationi boni habitus & Christianæ virtutes succedunt.
units.tr: Its parts are two: I. the mortification of the flesh, by which the sinful inclination and disposition of our nature is gradually abolished and broken. II. the vivification of the spirit, by which good habits and Christian virtues take the place of the sinful disposition or inclination.

units.la: II. RESURRECTIO Carnis, qua corpora nostra virtute Dei excitata, & cum animis suis unita ad vitam immortalem & gloriosam glorificata resurgent.
units.tr: II. The RESURRECTION of the flesh, by which our bodies, raised by the power of God and united again with their souls, will rise glorified to immortal and glorious life.

units.la: III. VITA ÆTERNA est beatissimus noster status post hanc Vitam, cum nimirum in Cœlum translati, & ab omnibus miseriis liberati, perfecto gaudio & gloria, tam corpore, quàm anima in æternum fruemur.
units.tr: III. ETERNAL LIFE is our most blessed state after this life, when, namely, we are carried up into heaven and freed from all miseries, and we shall enjoy perfect joy and glory, both in body and in soul, forever.

units.la: CAPITIS II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: SECTIO II.
units.tr: SECTION II.

units.la: FIDES respiciens Christia-num credente, qua credens est, & quatenus est actus fidelis, qua fidelis est, quaque justificatur & servatur, est mirada quæ-dam vis & supernaturalis facultas, qua mens hominis Verbo Dei edocta & à Spiritu Sancto illuminata, Deum ejus-que promissiones bene novit ac intel-ligit, notis assensum præbet, & quod cognitum habet, approbat ut verum & bonum. Speciatim vero promissa illa vera ac bona sibi adjudicat, & ad se per-tinere statuit: quaq; Voluntas à Spiri-tu S. flexa, appetit & apprehendit id, quod ab intellectu illustrato, ut verum & bonum monstratum, ac ut suum pe-culium, est judicatum, adeoq; in eo fi-duciam suam collocans acquiescit.
units.tr: Faith, considered as the faith of the Christian believer, by which he believes, and insofar as it is a faithful act, by which he is faithful, and by which he is justified and kept, is a certain wonderful power and supernatural faculty. By it the human mind, taught by the Word of God and enlightened by the Holy Spirit, truly knows and understands God and his promises, gives assent to them, and approves as true and good what it has come to know. Especially, it claims for itself those true and good promises and determines that they pertain to it. The will, bent by the Holy Spirit, then desires and grasps what the enlightened intellect has judged to be shown as true and good and as its own possession, and so, placing its trust in it, rests there.

units.la: Fides hæc præcipue respicit Deum & Mediatorem suum.
units.tr: This faith chiefly regards God and its Mediator.

units.la: 1. Deum, quatenus se nobis in fœ-dere in Deum promisit. Ait enim
units.tr: 1. God, insofar as he has bound himself to us in covenant. For he says:

units.la: 1. Ego sum Schaddai, id est, Omnisufficiens Deus, quā voce & Unitatem, & Omnipotentiam, & Bonitatem, & omnem virtutem suam exponit Deus. 2. Ego sum Deus tuus & semini tui post te: quò pertinent quæcunque promissiones in scripturis ad felicitatem sempiternam ac temporariam referri possunt. Deum enim alicujus esse, est & creatorem & conservatorem esse. Quicquid itaque Deus est, id fides statuit sibi & suo bono esse. Audit Deum bonum esse, credit itaque Deum sibi quoque bonum esse & fore, & suam bonitatem secum communicare: eam in se efficiendo. Audit Deum Omnipotentem esse, statuit ipsum suo bono esse omnipotentem, adeoque omnipotentia Dei, quam sibi commodare novit, freta gaudet. Audit Deum esse Summe Sapientem, cōfidit eum sibi sapientem esse & manere, & Dei Sapientiam suis quoque rationibus prospecturam. Audit Deum esse Clementem & Misericordem, talem suo quoque bono eum esse non dubitat, nec unquam ab ejus Clementia & Misericordia vult esse exclusum. Audit Deum esse summè Justum, statim suum inde elicit commodum, & Deum suo etiam bono Justum credit. Audit Deum esse summè Veracem, confugit itaq; ad veritatem Dei, quam sibi quoq; applicat, & Deum in promis-sis suis sibi veracem nullus dubitat: & ita deinceps. Sic itaq; fides Deum respicit, ut suum & sibi promissum Deum. Omniaque Dei sua facit, & bono suo applicare studet.
units.tr: 1. I am Shaddai, that is, the All-sufficient God. By this word God sets forth his unity, his omnipotence, his goodness, and all his power. 2. I am your God and the God of your seed after you. To this belong all the promises in Scripture that can be referred to eternal and temporal happiness. For to be someone's God is to be both creator and preserver. Whatever God is, faith therefore holds to be for itself and for its own good. It hears that God is good, and so it believes that God is and will be good to it too, and that he shares his goodness with it by making it good. It hears that God is omnipotent, and holds that his omnipotence is for its own good; so it rejoices in the omnipotence of God, which it knows it can make its own. It hears that God is supremely wise, and trusts that he is and remains wise for it, and that the wisdom of God will also provide for its reasons. It hears that God is merciful and compassionate, and does not doubt that he is such for its good too, and never wishes to be shut out from his clemency and mercy. It hears that God is supremely just, and at once draws its own advantage from this, and believes God to be just for its good too. It hears that God is supremely truthful, and so it takes refuge in the truth of God, which it also applies to itself, and no one doubts that God is truthful to it in his promises; and so on. Thus faith regards God as its own God and his promise to it. It makes all of God's attributes its own and strives to apply them to its good.

units.la: II. Mediatorem proprie respicit Fides salvifica, quatenus est animi fiducia in Jesu Christo ejusq; merito penitus acquiescens. Fide enim fidelis credit in Jesum Christum, sibi, & in suum bonum ad salutem suam conceptum, natum, passum, crucifixum, mortuum, sepultum, redivivum, cœlos conscendentem, ad dextram Dei Patris sedentem, & novissimo die ad judicium reditūrum, Hunc Jesum totum fidelis per fidem sibi applicat, & pro suis peccatis satisfecisse, certò statuit.
units.tr: II. Saving faith regards the Mediator properly, insofar as it is a trust of the soul in Jesus Christ, resting wholly on his merit. For the faithful man believes in Jesus Christ, and believes that Jesus, conceived, born, suffered, crucified, dead, buried, risen again, ascended into the heavens, seated at the right hand of God the Father, and to return on the last day for judgment, was conceived for his salvation and is for his good. Through faith he applies the whole of this Jesus to himself, and firmly determines that Jesus has made satisfaction for his sins.

units.la: Ergò fides Christianorum salvifica versatur in Christo Jesu rectè cogno-icenfcendo ad vitam æternam, Joh, 17. v. 3. Hæc est autem vita æterna, ut cognoscant te illum solum verum Deum, & quem misisti Iesum Christum. Ecce vita æterna consistit in cognitione Dei, qua certo persuasi sumus, Deum verum esse unicum, eumque esse Patrem, Filium & Spiritum S. de quo supra. Et filium a Patre missum esse in hunc mundum, ut is assumta nostra natura esset Iesus Christus, id est, noster Servator, summus Propheta, summus Sacerdos & summus Rex, qui scilicet arcanum illud consilium Dei de æterna nostra salute nobis exposuerit: qui sese peccatis nostris in se susceptis, pro nobis Deo cum precibus obtulerit victimam expiatoriam, nosq; eo sacrificio reconciliarit Deo: qui sacrificio illo peracto, in Sanctuarium coeleste ingressus, coram facie Patris ꝑ nobis continenter appareat: deniq; qui in coelis ad dextram Patris regnans, nos Spiritu suo regat, & potentia sua contra hostes protegat; donec suo tempore hostibus plene abolitis nos ad se in Regnum suum coeleste recipiat. Agnoscit vero Iesum Christum, adjudicat, apprehendit & applicat fi-deli Fides, ut Suum Mediatorem inter se & Deum. Siquidem ipse dicat Johan. 14. Ego sum Via, Veritas & Vita, nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Et Paul. 1. Timoth. 2. Unus enim Deus; & unus Mediator Dei & hominum Iesus Christus. Heb. 7. In tantum melioris testamenti sponsor factus est Iesus; Unde & salvare in perpetuum potest accedentes per semetipsum ad Deum, semper vivens ad interpellandum pro nobis. Cap. 8. Nunc melius sortitus est ministerium, quanto & melioris foederis Mediator est, quod in melioribus repromissionibus sanctum est. Cap. 9. Ideo novi foederis Mediator est, ut morte intercedente, in redemtionem earum praevaricationum, quae erant sub priori testamento, repromissionem accipiant, qui vocati sunt, aeternae hereditatis.
units.tr: Therefore the saving faith of Christians is occupied with Christ Jesus, rightly known, leading to eternal life. John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent. Behold, eternal life consists in the knowledge of God, by which we are firmly persuaded that God is the one true God, and that he is Father, Son and Holy Spirit, as above. And that the Son was sent by the Father into this world, so that, having assumed our nature, he might be Jesus Christ, that is, our Saviour, the supreme Prophet, the supreme Priest and the supreme King: who indeed has laid open to us that hidden counsel of God concerning our eternal salvation; who, having taken our sins upon himself, offered himself to God for us with prayers as an expiatory victim, and reconciled us to God by that sacrifice; who, that sacrifice completed, entered the heavenly sanctuary and continually appears for us before the face of the Father; and finally, who, reigning in heaven at the right hand of the Father, rules us by his Spirit and protects us against our enemies by his power, until in due time, the enemies being wholly abolished, he receives us into his heavenly kingdom. Faith, however, recognizes, claims, grasps and applies Jesus Christ to the believer as his Mediator between himself and God. For he himself says, John 14: I am the Way, the Truth and the Life; no one comes to the Father except through me. And 1 Timothy 2: For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and men, Jesus Christ. Hebrews 7: By so much was Jesus made surety of a better covenant. Wherefore he is able also to save to the uttermost those who come to God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them. Chapter 8: But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by so much as he is also Mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. Chapter 9: For this reason he is the Mediator of a new covenant, so that, death having intervened for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the former covenant, those who are called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.

units.la: 2. Ut Suum REDEMTOREM, ut qui pro se dederit animam suam in redemtionem, Matth. 20. v. 28. adeoq; sibi a Deo factus sit redemtio, 1. Cor. 1. v. 30. Hic n. dedit semetipsum pro nobis in redemtione, ut nos redimeret ab omni iniquitate, & mundaret sibi populū acceptabile sectatorem bonorum operum, 1. Tim. 1.Timot.2.v.6.Tit.2.v.14. occisus est, & redemit nos Deo per sanguinem suum, Apoc.5.v.9.
units.tr: 2. Faith regards him as its REDEEMER, as one who gave his soul as a ransom for himself, Matthew 20:28, and so was made by God a redemption for us, 1 Corinthians 1:30. For he gave himself for us as a ransom, to redeem us from all iniquity, and to cleanse for himself a people acceptable and zealous for good works (1 Timothy 2:6; Titus 2:14). He was slain and redeemed us to God by his blood (Revelation 5:9).

units.la: 3. Ut suum SERVATOREM seu SALVATOREM, ut qui salvum faciat populum suum a peccatis ejus, Matth.1. v.21. Venit enim filius hominis servare, quod perierat. Matth.18.v.11. Non venit animas perditum, sed servatum, Luc.9.v.56. Non enim misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum. Johan.3.v.17. Fidelis igitur sermo, & omni acceptione dignus, quod Christus Jesus venit in hunc mundum, ut peccatores salvos faceret.
units.tr: 3. Faith regards him as its SAVIOUR, who will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). For the Son of Man came to save what was lost (Matthew 18:11). He did not come to destroy souls but to save them (Luke 9:56). For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him (John 3:17). Therefore this is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners (1 Timothy 1:15).

units.la: Hunc Iesum Mediatorem, Redemptorem, & Servatorem suum agnoscit Christianorum fides, tum quoad Personam, tum quoad Officium.
units.tr: This Jesus the Christian faith acknowledges as his Mediator, Redeemer and Saviour, both as to his Person and as to his Office.

units.la: I. Quoad PERSONAM, agnoscit Christum esse Verum Deum.
units.tr: I. As to his PERSON, he acknowledges that Christ is true God.

units.la: 2. Verum Hominem. 3. θεάνθρωπον, hoc est, Deum & Hominem simul in una Persona.
units.tr: 2. True man. 3. Theanthropos, that is, God and man together in one Person.

units.la: I. Christum verum Deum credit & profitetur Christianus, 1. Propter cla-ra enunra enunciata Scripturæ, quibus Christi divinitas asseritur: Jes. 9. v. 6. Hoc est nomen, quo vocabunt eum, (Messiam) sc. Deus Fortis, Pater futuri seculi. Jerem. 23. v. 6. Nomen, quo Germen Davidis vocabitur, erit Jehovah justitia nostra. Matth. 16. v. 16. Tu es Christus Filius Dei vivi. Johan. 1. In principio erat λό-γῳ, & λόγῳ[?] erat Deus. Rom. 9. v. 5. Christus ex Patribus secundum carnem, qui est Deus in secula. 1. Joh. 5. v. 20. Et sumus[?] in Filio ejus Jesu Christo, qui est verus Deus & vita aeterna.
units.tr: I. The Christian believes and professes that Christ is true God: 1. On account of the clear statements of Scripture by which the divinity of Christ is asserted: Isa. 9. v. 6. "This is the name by which they will call him (the Messiah), namely, Mighty God, Father of the age to come." Jer. 23. v. 6. "The name by which the Branch of David will be called is, Jehovah our righteousness." Matt. 16. v. 16. "You are Christ, the Son of the living God." John 1. "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was God." Rom. 9. v. 5. "Christ, who is God over all, blessed for ever, came from the Fathers according to the flesh." 1 John 5. v. 20. "We are in his Son Jesus Christ, who is the true God and eternal life."

units.la: 2. Propter opera soli Deo competentia, quæ ipsi tribuuntur, ut Creare & Conservare. Johan. 1. v. 3. C. 3. v. 17. Coloss. 1. v. 16. Heb. 1. v. 2. 3. Redimere, ut supra probatum est. Delere iniquitates. Matth. 9. v. 6. Scrutari corda. Marc. 2. v. 8. Cap. 14. v. 13. Exaudire. Johan. 14. v. 14. Vivificare. Johan. 5. v. 21. Judicare. Joh. 5. v. 22. Item opera miraculosa, quæ sua virtute edidit, juxta vaticinium Jes. 35. v. 5. 6. Ad quæ ipse quoq; Christus remittit, Joh. 10. v. 25. Matth. 11. v. 4. 5. Et quorum edendorum potestatem largitus est Apostolis. Matth. 10. v. 8. Item Epitheta, quæ soli divinæ naturæ conveniunt, ei tribuuntur, ut quòd dicitur Æternus, Mich. 5[?]. v. 2. s.v.2. Joh.1.v.1. Cap.17.v.5. Omnipotens, Joh.3.v.31. Phil.3.v.21, Immensus, Matth.18.v.20, Rex Regum, Apocal.19.verf.16. Servator, ut supra, &c.
units.tr: 2. On account of the works that belong to God alone, which are ascribed to him: such as creating and preserving (John 1. v. 3; ch. 3. v. 17; Col. 1. v. 16; Heb. 1. v. 2, 3); redeeming, as has been shown above; blotting out iniquities (Matt. 9. v. 6); searching hearts (Mark 2. v. 8; ch. 14. v. 13); hearing prayers (John 14. v. 14); quickening (John 5. v. 21); judging (John 5. v. 22). Likewise the miraculous works which he performed by his own power, according to the prophecy of Isa. 35. v. 5, 6, to which Christ himself also refers (John 10. v. 25; Matt. 11. v. 4, 5), and the power of performing which he granted to the Apostles (Matt. 10. v. 8). Likewise the titles which belong only to the divine nature are ascribed to him: as that he is called Eternal (Mic. 5. v. 2; John 1. v. 1; ch. 17. v. 5), Almighty (John 3. v. 31; Phil. 3. v. 21), Immense (Matt. 18. v. 20), King of kings (Rev. 19. v. 16), Saviour (as above, etc.).

units.la: 3. Propter cultum & honorem, qui à sanctis fidelibus & ab Angelis Christo tribuitur: ut Invocatio, Adoratio, Fides, Spes. Psal.12. v.11. Jes.11. v.10. Rom. 15.v.12. Psal.2. v.12. Joh.14. v.1. Act.7. v.59.
units.tr: 3. On account of the worship and honour which are given to Christ by the holy faithful and by the angels: such as invocation, adoration, faith, hope (Ps. 12. v. 11; Isa. 11. v. 10; Rom. 15. v. 12; Ps. 2. v. 12; John 14. v. 1; Acts 7. v. 59).

units.la: Credit autem Christianus hunc Christum Mediatorem & Servatorem suum oportuisse esse Deum.
units.tr: The Christian also believes that this Christ, as Mediator and Saviour, had to be God.

units.la: 1. Propter magnitudinem mali, quo genus humanum premebatur, quod à nulla creatura tolli potuit; Spectaturq; in Peccati Gravitate, in Irae Dei intolerabili Pondere, in Mortis imperio, & in Tyrannide Diaboli, quae tollere, abolere, placare, vincere nemo potuit, nisi Deus. 2. Propter magnitudinem boni, quod à nemine restitui potuit hominibus, nisi à Deo, qui solus vere bonus est: consistitq; in imaginis Dei restitutione. Ideo Christus factus est nobis Sapientia, Justitia, Sanctificatio & Redemtio, non illa docen-do tando tantum, sed præstando & restitu-endo.
units.tr: 1. On account of the magnitude of the evil by which the human race was oppressed, which no creature could remove. It is seen in the gravity of sin, in the intolerable weight of God's wrath, in the dominion of death, and in the tyranny of the devil; no one could remove, abolish, appease or overcome these except God. 2. On account of the magnitude of the good which no one could restore to men except God, who alone is truly good; and it consists in the restoration of the image of God. Therefore Christ was made for us wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption (1 Cor. 1. v. 30), not only by teaching and exhorting, but by bestowing and restoring.

units.la: II. Christum Verum Hominem credit & profitetur Christianus, quia dicitur Semen mulieris. Genes. 3. vers. 15. Semen Abrahæ, in quo benedicendæ sint omnes gentes. Genes. 22. vers. 18. Filius Davidis, qui sedere debeat super eius solio, & regnare in perpetuum, 2. Sam. 7. v. 12. & 16. Virginis filius, Ies. 7. v. 14. Deinde tota historia Evangelica demonstrat Christum hunc, conceptum, natum, circumcisum, habuisse corpus verum, & animam, esurivisse, sitivisse, effudisse sanguinem, mortuum esse, omnes q; proprietates & affectiones naturæ humanæ (sed absq; peccato) habuisse, &c.
units.tr: II. The Christian believes and professes that Christ is true man, because he is called the seed of the woman (Gen. 3. v. 15), the seed of Abraham in whom all nations are to be blessed (Gen. 22. v. 18), the son of David who is to sit on his throne and reign for ever (2 Sam. 7. v. 12, 16), the son of a virgin (Isa. 7. v. 14). Further, the whole Gospel history shows that this Christ, conceived, born, circumcised, had a true body and soul, hungered, thirsted, shed blood, died, and had all the properties and affections of human nature (but without sin), and so on.

units.la: Credit autem Christianus huc Servatorem oportuisse hominem esse.
units.tr: The Christian also believes that this Saviour had to be man.

units.la: 1. Quia justitia id requirebat, ut inobedientia in carne nostra commissa, in eadem sarciretur, in Epist. ad Romanos c. 5. v. 17. 18. 19. Heb. 2. v. 14. 2. Postulabat hoc adoptionis nostri ratio. Voluit enim Filius Dei Naturam humanam assumere, ut frater, adeoq; proximus & propinquus noster fieri, ut nos ipsius membra effecti, filii Dei efficere-mur, Galat. 3. v. 26. & ita jus haberet nos redimendi & vindicandi. 3. Requirebatur hoc ad resurrectionis nostræ certitudinem. Nam quia Christus carnem nostram assumsit, & suscitavit, eique immortalitatem dedit, & in cœlos evexit: nos quoq; communionis illius, quæ nobis cum illo est, vi & jure, excitabimur in extremo die, & corpus hoc nostrum vile glorioso corpori Christi conforme reddetur, Phil. 3. v. 21. 1. Corint. 15. vers. 21. 22.
units.tr: 1. Because justice required that the disobedience committed in our flesh should be atoned for in the same flesh (Epistle to the Romans, ch. 5. v. 17, 18, 19; Heb. 2. v. 14). 2. The reason of our adoption demanded this. For the Son of God willed to assume human nature, in order to become our brother, and thus our kinsman and near relation, so that, having been made his members, we might be made sons of God (Gal. 3. v. 26), and thus he might have the right to redeem and vindicate us. 3. This was required for the certainty of our resurrection. For since Christ took up our flesh and raised it, and gave it immortality, and carried it up into the heavens, we too, by the power and right of that communion which we have with him, shall be raised up on the last day, and this our vile body shall be made conformable to the glorious body of Christ (Phil. 3. v. 21; 1 Cor. 15. v. 21, 22).

units.la: III. Credit Christianus, hunc verum Deum & Hominem θεάνθρωπον, adeoq; unam personam esse.
units.tr: III. The Christian believes that this one is the true God and Man, the God-man [θεάνθρωπον], and therefore one person.

units.la: Siquidem persona τῷ λόγῳ ęterna, humanam naturam propriæ personalitatis expertem, mirando & imperscrutabili modo assumsit in unitatem suæ personæ, sibiq; propriam fecit, salvis utriusq; naturæ proprietatibus.
units.tr: For the eternal Person of the Word [τῷ λόγῳ] assumed human nature, which had no personality of its own, into the unity of his own person in a wonderful and inscrutable way, and made it his own, with the properties of each nature remaining intact.

units.la: II. Quoad Officium, Fides Christianorum agnoscit, sibi adjudicat, apprehen-
units.tr: II. As regards office, the Christian faith acknowledges, claims for itself, apprehends and applies Christ as its Redeemer,

units.la: prehendit, applicat Christum Redemtorem suum, ut Doctorem, Sacerdotem, & Regem suum, qui Christus, id est, unctus est, ut sit nobis Jesus, id est, Servator. Servator autem nobis DOCTRINA, ut Doctor. MERITO, ut Sacerdos. EFFICACIA, ut Rex.
