units.tr: as its Teacher, Priest and King. He is Christ, that is, the Anointed One, so that he may be Jesus to us, that is, our Saviour. He is our Saviour by his TEACHING, as Teacher; by his MERIT, as Priest; and by his EFFICACY, as King.

units.la: I. DOCTRINA Servator est Christus, quia ipse arcanam Dei de generis humani redemtione Voluntatem, immediate sibi monstrata, nobis perfecte patefecit: & sic immediate a Patre Verbū ejus, & in Verbo etiam omnia, quibus obtinetur salus, revelavit. Matth.4. v.17. Ca.11.v.5. Devt,18:v.18. Jef.61.v.1. Joh. 1.v.16. 17.18. Heb.1.v.1. Actor.3.v.22.
units.tr: I. Christ is our Saviour by TEACHING, because he himself has fully revealed to us the hidden will of God concerning the redemption of mankind, which was shown to him directly; and so he has revealed directly from the Father his Word, and in the Word all the things by which salvation is obtained. Matt. 4:17; 11:5; Deut. 18:18; Isa. 61:1; John 1:16, 17, 18; Heb. 1:1; Acts 3:22.

units.la: II. MERITO & satisfactione Servator noster est, quia Christus, ut Sacerdos, Deum Patrem peccatis nostris offensum, propitium nobis reddidit. Heb. 5.v.10. Et sic Christus apud Deum ea peregit, quibus perfecte obtineretur salus.
units.tr: II. Our Saviour is also our Saviour by MERIT and satisfaction, because Christ, as Priest, made the Father, who was offended by our sins, merciful toward us. Heb. 5:10. And so Christ accomplished before God those things by which salvation is fully obtained.

units.la: Primum enim Servator hic noster nostra expiavit peccata, dum pro peccatis nostris Deo Patri λύτρον & pretium suffisufficiens persoluit. Rom. 3. v. 24. 25. 1. Pet. 3. v. 18. Ief. 53. v. 12. Et sic est pro peccatis nostris plena propitiatio, 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. Hac de re postea fusius.
units.tr: For first, this our Saviour atoned for our sins, when he paid to God the Father a sufficient ransom [λύτρον] and price for our sins. Rom. 3:24, 25; 1 Pet. 3:18; Isa. 53:12. And so there is a full propitiation for our sins, 1 John 2:2. We shall speak of this matter more fully later.

units.la: Satisfecit autem Christus Deo offenso, pro parte offendente, scilicet humano genere, perfectam voluntati divinae obedientiam usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis praestando, & eidem plenae obedientiae dignitatem summam, nimirum Meritum coram Deo & Efficaciam tribuendo. Iohan. 17. v. 19. Act. 20. v. 28. 2. Corinth. 5. Nempe quia Deus erat in Christo Mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputando iis peccataipsorum[?].
units.tr: Christ satisfied God, who had been offended, on behalf of the offending party, namely the human race, by rendering perfect obedience to the divine will, even to death, indeed to the death of the cross, and by ascribing the highest worth to that full obedience, namely by bestowing on it merit and efficacy before God. John 17:19; Acts 20:28; 2 Cor. 5. Certainly, because God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not imputing their sins to them.

units.la: Expiavit itaque Christus peccata nostra Merito passionis & mortis suae, quo persolutis peccatorum poenis satisfecit Iustitiae Dei, Iramque ejus placavit.
units.tr: Christ therefore atoned for our sins by the merit of his passion and death, by which, having paid the punishments due for sins, he satisfied the justice of God and appeased his wrath.

units.la: Vide hic SACRIFICIUM illud (de quo paulo post disceptabitur) quo se Christus Servator offert Deo Patri ad persolvendum poenas peccatis nostris debitas. Heb. 9. v. 26.
units.tr: Here see that SACRIFICE (which will be discussed a little later), by which Christ our Saviour offers himself to God the Father to pay the penalties owed for our sins. Heb. 9:26.

units.la: Sed nunc semel inconsummatione seculorum ad abolendum peccatū per immolatione sui ipsius patefactus est.
units.tr: But now once, at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

units.la: In hoc sacrificio, Victima fuit Christus, qua Homo; Altare Christus, qua Deus; Sacerdos Christus & Deus & Homo.
units.tr: In this sacrifice, Christ was the victim as man; Christ was the altar as God; Christ was the priest both as God and as man.

units.la: 1. Vide etiam hic Acceptationem Dei Patris acquiescentis in eo sacrificio. Nisi enim approbasset Pater, inane su-isset. Matth. 3. v. 7. Hic est filius ille meus di-lectus, in quo εὐδόκησα [?], id est, Valde placatus sum & acquiesco. Ephes. 5. Christus dilexit nos, & tradidit seipsum pro nobis oblationem Deo in odorem bonae fragrantiae.
units.tr: 1. Here also see the acceptance of God the Father, who was pleased with that sacrifice. For unless the Father had approved, it would have been in vain. Matt. 3:17: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased [εὐδόκησα], that is, I am very well pleased and content. Eph. 5: Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering to God as a fragrant aroma.

units.la: Vide denique hic IMPUTATIONEM peccati, qua Christus æstimatus est a Patre, velut transgressor, peccatis omnium in eum translatis. Jes. 53. v. 4. 5. & 2. Corinth. 5. v. 21.
units.tr: Finally, here see the IMPUTATION of sin, by which Christ was reckoned by the Father as a transgressor, the sins of all having been transferred to him. Isa. 53:4, 5; 2 Cor. 5:21.

units.la: CHRISTUS Expiator peccatorum nostrorum, est etiam Advocatus & deprecator apud Deum pro nobis, Rom. 8. v. 34. Heb. 9. v. 24.
units.tr: Christ, the atoner for our sins, is also our Advocate and intercessor with God on our behalf. Rom. 8:34; Heb. 9:24.

units.la: III. EFFICACIA Christus Servator noster est, quia, ut Meriti & Satisfactionis adeoque Redemtionis suæ fiamus participes, salutarem suam gratiam efficaciter nobis distribuit, & omnia disponit ad nostram Salutè. Primò enim Ecclesiam suam per Evangelii praedicationem è mundo collectam, (adeoq; nos) Verbo & Spiritu suo vocat, dein-de vocatos ac venientes ad se guber-nat, ac contra omnes, tum Spirituales, tum Corporales hostes potentissimè defendit. Atq; sic nos suâ morte redemtos efficaciter vocat, & ad fidem vocatos & credentes justificat, & justificatos glorificat. Sic Christum Servatorem suum spectet: agnoscat, colat Christiana fides.
units.tr: III. Christ is our Saviour by EFFICACY, because, so that we may become partakers of his Merit and Satisfaction and therefore of his Redemption, he efficaciously distributes his saving grace to us and arranges everything for our salvation. First, he calls his Church, gathered from the world through the preaching of the Gospel (and so us), by his Word and Spirit; then he guides those called and coming to him, and powerfully defends them against all enemies, both spiritual and bodily. And so he efficaciously calls us, redeemed by his death, and justifies those called and believing to faith, and glorifies those justified. Thus the Christian faith should regard Christ as its Saviour, acknowledge him and worship him.

units.la: CAPUT III. DE HORRENDA FIDEI Mutilatione, quâ Caput Fidei & salutis hodie à nonnullis rejecatur, quæ hoc loco Christianismi prima est mutilatio.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. ON THE HORRIBLE MUTILATION OF THE FAITH, BY WHICH THE HEAD OF FAITH AND SALVATION IS TODAY REJECTED BY SOME; HERE THIS IS THE FIRST MUTILATION OF CHRISTIANITY.

units.la: CHRISTUS Matth. 24. Vi-dete, inquit, ne quis vos seducat. Multi enim venient in Nomine meo dicentes: Ego sum Christus, & multos seducent. Hoc nostro seculo, eheu, quàm divisus est Christus! quàm multi veniunt in Christi nomine, dicentes, se verum & genuinum Christum nosse, habere, docere! Quaevis hodie secta ex cerebro suo, contortis ad suum εἴδωλον scripturis suum sibi format, aliis proclamat, armis propugnat Christum, quod nullo negotio ex hodiernarum sectarum inductione, si opus esset, nec infirmos offenderet, demonstrari posset. Addit alius, demit alius, transmutat alius quidpiam in Christo, sibi ut suum effingat, aliis venditet. Varia de Christo fides, Varium in hominum variorum mentib. efformat Christum, Uno interim vero existente & permanente in saecula Christo.
units.tr: CHRIST says in Matthew 24: "Take heed that no one deceives you. For many will come in my name, saying, 'I am Christ,' and they will deceive many." In our age, alas, how divided Christ is! How many come in Christ's name, saying that they know, have, and teach the true and genuine Christ! Every sect today forms for itself, out of its own brain, a Christ, bending the Scriptures to its own idol [εἴδωλον]; it proclaims him to others and defends him with arms. This could be shown without any trouble, if it were necessary, from an induction of today's sects, and it would not even offend the weak. One sect adds to Christ, another takes away, another alters something in him so as to fashion him for itself and sell him to others. There is a variety of faith about Christ; there is a variety of Christs formed in the minds of different people, while the one Christ remains and abides for ever.

units.la: Tria praecipuè me, postquam ex tenebris ignorantiae meae emersi, in tentationibus meis, mirum quantum consolata sunt. 1. Ingens DONUM illud Patris coelestis, Ipse Dei unigenitus Filius, ab illo ab aeterno genitus, quem dedit meo mihi bono, qui factus homo, servi formâ assumtâ, frater & propinquus meus esse voluit, ut me credentem in fe, redemtu in Libertate & Gloriam riam filiorum Dei assereret[?]. Hoc me saepius erexit, quod ipse Christus admirabundus ait: Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut filium suum unigenitum dederit, ut quisquis credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Three things in particular have wonderfully comforted me in my temptations, since I emerged from the darkness of my ignorance. (1) That great GIFT of the heavenly Father, his only-begotten Son himself, begotten by him from eternity, whom he gave for my good, who, having become man and taken the form of a servant, willed to be my brother and kinsman, so that he might assert that I, believing in him, am redeemed into the liberty and glory of the sons of God. This has often lifted me up, because Christ himself says in wonder: God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

units.la: 2. SPONSOR meus Iesus Christus cum merito & satisfactio-nesuâ, Agnus ille Dei, cuius caro mactata est pro mundi vita, cuius sanguis effusus est in remissionem peccatorum meorum, tollens peccata mundi, in quem Deus Pater conjecit, seu fecit con-vel incurrere omnium nostrum iniquitates; qui mihi ab ipso Deo factus est Sapientia, Iustitia, Sanctificatio & Redemtio; quē Deus pro me etiam fecit Peccatū, ut nos in ipso essemus Iustitia, &c. Hic vas meus nō modò spopondit, sed etiam a me persolvit & satisfecit, dans animā suam pro me in redemtionem.
units.tr: (2) My surety Jesus Christ, with his merit and his satisfaction: that Lamb of God, whose flesh was slain for the life of the world, whose blood was poured out for the forgiveness of my sins, "taking away the sins of the world," on whom God the Father laid, or made to fall, the iniquities of us all. He, who was made by God himself to be wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption for me; whom God also made sin for me, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God, and so on. He not only promised this for me, but also himself paid and satisfied it on my behalf, giving his soul as a ransom for me.

units.la: 3. ADVOCATUS meus apud Patrem Iesus ille Christus in quotidianis meis lapsibus ac infirmitatibus carnis meae magno mihi fuit solatio. Cum enim ingenti cum animi dolore & maxima Spiritus molestia, mise-rum rum me in corpore mortis detentum quotidie, imò singulis horis, aliquoties etiam non leviter, sed graviter errare, labi, hallucinari deprehenderem, nec me ad eam perfectionem fidei & vitæ, quam tot gemitibus expeto, hîc aspirare posse viderem, suspirabam ad intercessorem meum Jesum Christum apud Patrem, juxta illud: Si quis peccaverit; Advocatum apud Patrem habemus Jesum Christum, qui est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris: ac credebam hunc Jesum Advocatum meum, me in gratia Patris conservare regendo meos lapsus quotidianos, infirmitates ac imperfectiones quotidiana applicatione meritorum suorum per fidem meam, licet infirmam facta, ut hac ratione persona mea justa maneat, lapsus mei non veniant sub judicii censuram, & opera mea (licet imperfecta) Deo meo propter Christum, (qui quod deest mihi, supplet) accepta sint. 1. Johan. 2. v.12. 1. Pet. 2. v.5.
units.tr: (3) My advocate with the Father, that same Jesus Christ, has been a great comfort to me in my daily falls and the infirmities of my flesh. For when, with great grief of mind and the greatest distress of spirit, I found myself, wretched man that I am, held in the body of death, daily, indeed hourly, and sometimes not lightly but grievously erring, slipping and going astray, and I saw that I could not aspire to that perfection of faith and life for which I long with so many groans, I sighed to my intercessor Jesus Christ with the Father, according to that saying: If anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ, who is the propitiation for our sins. And I believed that this Jesus, my advocate, keeps me in the grace of the Father, by governing my daily lapses, infirmities and imperfections through the daily application of his merits by my faith, weak though it be; so that by this means my person remains righteous, my lapses do not come under the censure of judgment, and my works, though imperfect, are accepted by my God for Christ's sake, who supplies what is lacking in me. 1 John 2:12. 1 Peter 2:5.

units.la: Hæc ubi ita mecum agitare solebam, nescio quis, ut forte fidem hanc meam subverteret, animu meum tentare coecoepit, oblatis libris nonullis; quos ubi perlegi, Mc Christe, aliquoties Obstupui, steterúntq; Coma, & vox faucibus hasit. Ingemui, suspiria ingeminans, cum viderem praecipua illa meae fidei & consolationis fundamenta labefactari & everti.
units.tr: When I was in the habit of turning these things over in my mind, someone, perhaps to overthrow this faith of mine, began to try my soul by offering me certain books. When I had read them through, I was struck dumb, and, as I recall, I was amazed, my hair stood on end, and my voice stuck in my throat. I groaned, heaping up sighs, when I saw the chief foundations of my faith and consolation shaken and overturned.

units.la: Mecum excuterem, testante Conscientia, nihil nisi peccata in me, lapsus, infirmitates, adeoque maledictionem, parum admodum boni, quod fecissem, idque multis conspurcatum sordibus, offendi.
units.tr: When I examined myself, my conscience bearing witness, I found in myself nothing but sins, lapses, infirmities, and therefore a curse, and very little good, even what I had done, and that stained with many filths.

units.la: Offensus itaque, mihi Medicum & Servatorem anhelans quaesivi, monstrabatur mihi istis in libris quidem Christus, sed non aeternus Dei Filius, verum tantum purus homo suo modo Deificatus.
units.tr: Offended, therefore, and longing for a physician and a Saviour, I sought him. In those books Christ was indeed shown to me, but not as the eternal Son of God; only as a mere man, deified in his own way.

units.la: O quantum decessit dignitati doni mei, quo multum laetabar!
units.tr: Oh, how much of the dignity of my gift has been lost, in which I rejoiced greatly!

units.la: Ostendebatur Christus Servator quidem, sed ut Doctor & Exemplar lingua & vita mihi viam vitæ monstras, & habens auctoritatem & potestatem omnibus in se credentibus, hoc est, sibi rectè obedientibus, & se in via vitæ sequentibus, vitam æternam dandi: non autem, ut Sponsor & Satisfactor, qui suâ Obedientiâ & merito à me satisfecerit, & sanguine suo ita peccata mea expiarit, Christus proponebatur mihi lapsibꝰ meis excruciato, ut Advocatus quidem, sed non talis, qui virtute meriti & satisfactionis suæ, pro me in gratia conservando, intercederet, & ita meas infirmitates ac imperfectiones tegeret; relegabar ad Sanctam Christi obedientiam in vita sectandam, siquidem verè renati carnem suam plane superare possint, ut Spiritus in ipsis nō reluctante carne, sed plane domitâ & subactâ, plenè dominetur, nec Paulus de se renato loquatur, adeoq; in hac vita perfectio fidei & vitæ non sit desperanda. Et hæc quidem scripturarum frequentissimâ allegatione, & mirâ subtiliq; contorsione confidentissimè afferebatur. Quid animi mihi fuerit, reputet secum Christianus, cui cordi est salus, & in his confusionibus salvificæ veritatis seria inquisitio. Quod ad primum meæ consolationis fundamentum attinet, video illud ita debere convelli, ut plenis libris adversus æternam Filii Dei divinitatem decertetur. Ita enim non horrent scribere: Dicimus unum esse æternum illum & altissimum Deum, nempe Patrem, non agnoscimus aliquem Dei Filium, qui non fit purus homo. Item, Quod Messias non sit finis Deus & Homo primum ex eo liquet, quod nunquam talis promissus sit. 2. Quia nunquam in scripturis Novi Testamenti Deus vocatur. 3. Quia in scripturis Novi Testamenti solus Pater Deus vocatur.
units.tr: Christ was indeed presented to me as Saviour, but as a teacher and example, who by word and life shows me the way of life, and who has the authority and power to give eternal life to all who believe in him, that is, who rightly obey him and follow him on the way of life. He was not presented to me, as Surety and Satisfier, who by his obedience and merit has made satisfaction for me and by his blood has thus expiated my sins. Christ was put before me, while I was tormented by my lapses, as an advocate, but not one who, by the virtue of his merit and satisfaction, intercedes for me to preserve me in grace, and so covers my infirmities and imperfections. I was sent back to the holy obedience of Christ to be pursued in life, provided that the truly reborn can wholly overcome their flesh, so that the Spirit may rule fully in them, the flesh not resisting but completely tamed and subdued; and that Paul does not speak of himself as reborn, and that perfection of faith and life is not to be despaired of in this life. These things were asserted most confidently, with very frequent citation of Scripture and a wonderful and subtle twisting of it. What my state of mind was, let the Christian reflect, for whom salvation is dear, and who in such confusions seeks earnestly after the saving truth. As for the first foundation of my consolation, I see that it must be uprooted, since whole books are written to contend against the eternal divinity of the Son of God. For they do not shrink from writing thus: We say that there is one eternal and most high God, namely the Father; we do not acknowledge any Son of God who is not a mere man. Likewise: That the Messiah is not God and man is clear first from the fact that such a one was never promised. (2) Because in the Scriptures of the New Testament God is never called God. (3) Because in the Scriptures of the New Testament only the Father is called God.

units.la: Verum enimvero, ut dono illo divino ac immensa, Filio Dei, dico, unigenito & proprio mihi dato gaudeam & triumphem cum omnibus Orthodoxis Christianis, vicit & fecit invicta Dei & Verbi ejus Veritas de æterna divinitate Filii Dei, quam adversus pestilentem ac blasphemum hunc errorem, ejusque Patronos Nearianos, Josias Simlerus, Hieronymus Zanchius, Franciscus Junius & alii acriter defenderunt, & quidem adhuc in ea afferenda plurimum desudant.
units.tr: But in truth, that I may rejoice and triumph with all Orthodox Christians in that divine and immense gift given to me, the only-begotten and own Son of God, I say, the invincible truth of God and of his Word has conquered and prevailed concerning the eternal divinity of the Son of God. Against this pestilent and blasphemous error, and its patrons the Arians, Josias Simler, Hieronymus Zanchius, Franciscus Junius and others have defended it vigorously, and indeed still labour greatly in asserting it.

units.la: Quod vero ad alterum fidei & Salutis meae caput, & consolationis basin attinet, iidem illi homines, Doctrinam de Merito & Satisfactione JESU CHRISTI expresse humanum commentum vocitare solent. Audent aperte disputare, Falsam esse sententiam istam, quod Christum morte sua Deo, sive ejus justitiae pro peccatis nostris satisfecerit: quia in Deo satis sit misericordiae ad nos absque ulla satisfactione salvandos: imo Deum jure potuisse nobis condonare peccata nostra, nulla vera pro ipsis satisfactione ab ulla persona, ullove modo accepta. Item contendunt constanter, Christum poenarum, quas nos subire, ex lege Dei, tenebamur, solutione divina justitia pro nobis satisfacere non potuisse: Nullo pacto Christi satisfactione per fidem nobis imputari: imo Christi justitiam nobis imputare, merum esse commentum.
units.tr: As for the second head of my faith and salvation, and the basis of my consolation, these same men are accustomed to call the doctrine of the merit and satisfaction of JESUS CHRIST expressly a human invention. They openly dare to dispute that this opinion is false, that Christ by his death satisfied God, or his justice, for our sins, because in God there is enough mercy to save us without any satisfaction; indeed, God could by right have forgiven us our sins, with no true satisfaction for them received from any person or in any way. Likewise they constantly contend that Christ could not satisfy for us by the divine payment of the penalties which we were bound to undergo under the law of God; in no way is Christ's satisfaction imputed to us through faith; indeed, to impute Christ's righteousness to us is a mere invention.

units.la: Deum quidem satis misericordem esse ad condonanda mihi peccata mea non ambigo; at interim si Christus Sponsor, si Sponsoris hujus Meritum & satisfactio mihi eripitur, profecto quantum ex Sacris Scripturis, & me ipso colligere possum, me miserrimum hominem fateor. Ideoque fas mihi sit, ut missis caeteris, in hoc, pro virili mea, totus nunc sim, ut, ad fidem meam tuendam & confirmandam, adversus varias tentationes MERITUM, SATISFACTIONEM & JUSTITIAM Sponsoris mei JESU CHRISTI contra acerbos ejus hostes, asseram, adeoque hac me consolatione destitui non permittam.
units.tr: I do not doubt that God is merciful enough to forgive me my sins; but if Christ, the Surety, and the merit and satisfaction of this Surety are taken from me, then, as far as I can gather from the Holy Scriptures and from my own self, I confess myself the most wretched of men. Therefore it is right for me, setting other matters aside, to devote myself entirely, as far as I can, to defending and confirming my faith against various temptations; and to assert the MERIT, SATISFACTION and JUSTICE of my Surety Jesus Christ against his bitter enemies, and so I will not allow myself to be deprived of this consolation.

units.la: Interim velim Lectorem observare, me in illorum librorum lectione observasse, istorum hominum, de quibus mihi sermo est, dogmata, in omnibus fere Christianae fidei articulis, ab orthodoxa nostra Ecclesia recedere, & multiformia haereticorum olim ab Ecclesia damnatorum commeta revocare magno conatu, & in unum quoddam, quasi novae Theologiae monstrum formandum, comportare.
units.tr: Meanwhile I would like the reader to note that, in my reading of those books, I have observed that the teachings of those men of whom I am speaking depart from our orthodox Church on almost all the articles of the Christian faith, and that with great effort they revive the many forms of errors of heretics long ago condemned by the Church, and gather them together to form a kind of monster of a new theology.

units.la: I. In Doctrina de Deo impugnant
units.tr: I. On the doctrine of God, they attack

units.la: Personarum Divinarum Trinitatem: Filii Dei aeternam divinitatem, Spiritus Sancti hypostasin, & divinam essentiam pernegant. Christi Officium & virtutem lacerant & labefactant. stant. Ajunt loco nostro Christum nõ essepas-sum & mortuum: Christi sanguinem effusum non esse ullius efficacia: Christum nõ placasse no-bis Patrem. Negant Christifacerdotium consistere in oblatione corporis sui, in intercessione & satisfactione Christi pro nobis, sed in administratione Regni gloriæ, in quo tamen Regno Christum absq; carne & sanguine locant: somniant enim Christum absq; suo corpore naturali in cœlis esse, propterea quod caro & sanguis Regnum Dei possidere nequeant,& corpus ejus jam plane sit Spirituale. Scribunt Christum neq; fore Sacerdotem nostrum perpetuum, neq; regnaturum semper.
units.tr: They deny the Trinity of the Divine Persons: the eternal divinity of the Son of God, the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit, and the divine essence. They tear apart and weaken the office and power of Christ. They say that Christ was not a sufferer and dead in our place, that the shed blood of Christ was of no efficacy for anyone, and that Christ did not appease the Father for us. They deny that the priesthood of Christ consists in the offering of his body, in his intercession and satisfaction for us, but in the administration of the Kingdom of glory; yet in that Kingdom they place Christ without flesh and blood, for they dream that Christ is in heaven without his natural body, because flesh and blood cannot possess the Kingdom of God, and his body is now altogether spiritual. They write that Christ will be neither our everlasting Priest nor will he reign forever.

units.la: II. De lege docent, legem Moralè Mosis fuisse imperfeƈtam, à Christo autem nova accessione oportuisse compleri, (Matth. 5.) Præceptũ Christi de non temere jurando novum esse dicũt, atq; Mosi incognitum. Vindiƈtam non modò privatam, sed etiam publicam, quæ fit per Magistratum simpliciter à Christo esse prohibitam ajunt: ideo etiam putant, Christianis officium Magistratus minimè competere, si constet absq; cæde & bellis illud administrari nõ posse. Christianis quoq; non esse licitum bella gerere, aut vitam auferre hostibus: Sontes & maleficos non esse è [?] vita tollendos: Fures non esse suspendendos: Neminem ob hæ-resin ullam esse repudiandum aut damnandum: hæreticos etiam blasphe-mos & seditiosos non esse supplicio af-ficiendos. Docent in Veteri Testa-mento luxum ciborum & vestimento-rum non prohibitum; sed in Novo Te-ftameto omnes etiam ciborum delici-as & lautitias simpliciter interdictas es-se. Item nihil abundās aut superfluum esse quærendum, aut expetendū, quia avaritia sit studium abundantiæ, divi-tiasque in Novo Testamento homini Christiano nullo modo permissas esse opinantur.
units.tr: II. On the law they teach that the moral law of Moses was imperfect, and had to be completed by Christ through a new addition (Matt. 5). They say that the precept of Christ against swearing rashly is new and unknown to Moses. They say that revenge, not only private but also public, which is carried out by the magistrate, has been simply prohibited by Christ; therefore they also think that the office of the magistrate is in no way fitting for Christians, if it is agreed that it cannot be administered without slaughter and wars. Nor is it lawful for Christians to wage wars or take the lives of enemies; the guilty and wrongdoers are not to be removed from life; thieves are not to be hanged; no one is to be rejected or condemned on account of any heresy; heretics, even blasphemers and seditious persons, are not to be subjected to punishment. They teach that in the Old Testament luxury in food and clothing was not forbidden, but that in the New Testament all delicacies and sumptuous fare of every kind are simply forbidden. Likewise they think that nothing abundant or superfluous is to be sought or desired, because avarice is the pursuit of abundance, and that riches are in no way permitted to a Christian man in the New Testament.

units.la: III. De libero arbitrio & peccato,
units.tr: III. On Free Will and Sin,

units.la: I. Negant primorum parentum lapsu libertatem voluntatis, mentisq; nostra lucem in spiritualibus amissam: negant item ex S. literis probari posse, primum hominem ad sanctitatem & immortalitatem conditum esse: Negant naturam hominis lapsu esse corruptam.
units.tr: I. They deny that the freedom of the will was lost through the fall of our first parents, and that the light of our mind in spiritual matters was lost: they also deny that it can be proved from the Holy Scriptures that the first man was created in holiness and immortality. They deny that the nature of man was corrupted by the fall.

units.la: 2. Ergo Peccatum originis docent esse commentum & figmentum, extra omnem scripturam: adeoq; existimant hominem suis viribus posse & velle, & facere bonum, & credere in Christum.
units.tr: 2. Therefore they teach that original sin is an invention and a fiction, without any warrant in Scripture: and they accordingly think that man by his own powers can both will and do good, and believe in Christ.

units.la: IV. De Fide sic docent: Fides in Christû duplicem habet significationem. Una est, cum significat credere, Iesum esse Christum Dei filium (at non æternum) Altera est, cum significat Confidere Christo eiq; totum se tradere, h.e. ut ipsi scribunt, Christi Præceptis obedire, spe futuræ immortalitatis, & hac ratione, dicunt, nos fide iustificari. Deridént fidei apprehensionem & applicationem, qua Christi meritum applicari dicitur. Summa, Fides iustificans ipsis est observatio & obedientia mandatorum Christi.
units.tr: IV. On faith they teach as follows: Faith in Christ has a twofold meaning. One is when it means to believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God (but not eternal). The other is when it means to trust in Christ and to surrender oneself wholly to him, that is, as they themselves write, to obey the precepts of Christ in the hope of future immortality; and on this account, they say, we are justified by faith. They mock the apprehension and application of faith, by which the merit of Christ is said to be applied. In short, for them justifying faith is the observance and obedience of the commandments of Christ.

units.la: V. In Iustificationis Doctrina, explodunt descriptionem Evangelicorum, nempe gratuitam hominis à peccatis absolutionem, & imputationem iustitiæ Christi per fidem. Imputationem iustitiæ esse merum commentum aiunt, negant Christum satisfecisse pro peccatis nostris: tantum, ajunt, servari eos, qui mandata Dei per Christum tradita observent: In nobis esse aliquid, cur iustificemur, nempe fidem, id est, observantiam mandatorum Christi, ne iota quidem exstare in S. literis de merito Christi.
units.tr: V. On the doctrine of justification they reject the description given by the Evangelicals, namely the free absolution of man from sins, and the imputation of the righteousness of Christ through faith. They say that the imputation of righteousness is pure invention, and they deny that Christ satisfied for our sins: they say only that those are saved who observe the commandments of God delivered through Christ: that there is something in us on account of which we are justified, namely faith, that is, the observance of the commandments of Christ; and that there is not even a jot in the Holy Scriptures about the merit of Christ.

units.la: VI. De S. Scriptura docent, illam non opus habere ulla expositione: nihil opus esse Symbolis, nec libris exegeticis, eam posse ab omnibus intelligi etiam citra Spiritus Sancti revelationem & gratiam. Vnde & fidem tantum dicunt esse Dei donum, quatenus nos nulla re illam promeriti simus, non ea ratione, qua nos docemus.
units.tr: VI. On Holy Scripture they teach that it needs no interpretation at all, that there is no need of creeds or of expository books, and that it can be understood by everyone even without the revelation and grace of the Holy Spirit. Hence they also say that faith is only a gift of God in so far as we have deserved it by nothing, not in the way that we teach.

units.la: VII. De Sacramentis ita scribunt.
units.tr: VII. On the sacraments they write as follows.

units.la: 1. Baptismum tantum nudam esse ceremoniam. Baptismum in aqua à Christo non esse institutū, idq; nullà ratione probari posse. Verbum baptizare, idem esse, quod docere: Christum loqui de baptismo pœnitentiæ; Pædobaptismum nec Apostolicum, nec necessarium esse: Citius fratrum liberos admitti posse, si fidei rationem teneant, &c.
units.tr: 1. Baptism is only a bare ceremony. Baptism in water was not instituted by Christ, and this cannot be proved by any argument. The word "to baptize" means the same as "to teach"; Christ spoke of the baptism of repentance; infant baptism is neither apostolic nor necessary; the children of the brethren may be admitted sooner, if they hold to the profession of faith, etc.

units.la: 2. Cœna Domini negant obsignari & confirmari fidem nostram: docent errare supra modum, qui credant in cœna sumi Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, cum ibi tantum exhibeatur nudus Panis & nudū Vinum, Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, neq; realiter, neque respectivè, neq; spiritualiter exhiberi; esse duntaxat figurā & nudam commemorationem mortis Christi, ideoq; posse unumquemq; sua manu, sine administro & Pastore Panem & Vinum, quantum libeat, sumere. Hic cogita, sublata Christi satisfactione, quis illis situsus cœnæ Dominicæ,
units.tr: 2. The Lord's Supper they deny to seal and confirm our faith: they teach that those who believe that the Body and Blood of Christ are received in the supper err beyond measure, since only bare bread and bare wine are exhibited there; that the Body and Blood of Christ are exhibited neither really, nor respectively, nor spiritually; that it is merely a figure and a bare remembrance of the death of Christ; and therefore that each person may take the bread and wine with his own hand, without a minister or pastor, as much as he pleases. Consider here, with Christ's satisfaction removed, what kind of situation of the Lord's Supper remains for them,

units.la: VIII. Non
units.tr: VIII. Not

units.la: VIII. Non videntur Praedestinationem credere vel Lutheranam vel Calvinianam, sed potius sese, ut alibi, ita & hic se aggregare Pelagianis. Resurrectionem Carnis sic interpretantur: Credo resurrectionem Carnis, id est, ejus, quod erat caro, jam vero non est caro. Ecclesiam quaerere & cognoscere non opus esse, in ea puritatem Doctrinae non quarendam, ad docendum in Ecclesia nulla opus esse vocatione vel ordinatione: Sacramenta posse etiam a non vocatis & Laicis administrari docent. Ex his & aliis animadvertere licet ingens confluvium variorum dogmatum & opinionum ab Ecclesia nostra discedentium.
units.tr: VIII. They do not seem to believe predestination either in the Lutheran or in the Calvinist sense, but rather, as elsewhere, so here too they range themselves with the Pelagians. They interpret the resurrection of the flesh thus: I believe the resurrection of the flesh, that is, of that which was flesh, but now is no longer flesh. They teach that it is not necessary to seek and recognise the Church, nor to look for purity of doctrine in it; that no calling or ordination is needed to teach in the Church; and that the sacraments can also be administered by those who are not called, and by laymen. From these and other things it is possible to perceive a huge flood of various doctrines and opinions departing from our Church.

units.la: CAPITIS II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: SECTIO II.
units.tr: SECTION II.

units.la: RE in lites, à quibus anima mea abhorret, cum quoquam nolim; tantummodo animus est, tentatam fidem, adversus virulentas Satanæ hujus tentationes, formare & firmare, & non committere, ut Sponsoris mei satisfactione & persolutione pro peccatisnostris
units.tr: I have no wish to enter into disputes, which my soul shrinks from. My only aim is to shape and strengthen the faith that has been tested against the venomous temptations of Satan, and not to allow it to be stripped of the satisfaction and payment made by my Surety for our sins;

units.la: Note: the first line of the body shows a Latin text; the initial "R" is a large woodcut initial, read as "RE" in the scan. stris facta dispolier; & si forte Leƈtori cuipiam Meriti Filii Dei cupidissimo pretium operæ fecero, æqui bonique quæso, mecum hanc assertionem qualemcunq; faciat.
units.tr: and if perhaps I have done something worthwhile for any reader eager for the merit of the Son of God, I ask him, in fairness and goodwill, to accept this assertion, whatever its worth, along with me.

units.la: QVÆSTIO IGITVR DISCEPTATVR hæc: AN JESUS CHRISTUS MERITO ET Satisfactione, ac sufficientis λύτρα pro peccatis nostris persolutione, tanquam Sponsor noster, salutem æternam nobis acquisierit?
units.tr: THE QUESTION TO BE DISPUTED IS THIS: WHETHER JESUS CHRIST, BY HIS MERIT AND SATISFACTION, AND BY PAYING A SUFFICIENT RANSOM [λύτρα] FOR OUR SINS, AS OUR SURETY, HAS OBTAINED ETERNAL SALVATION FOR US.

units.la: Adeóque,
units.tr: And so:

units.la: An Christianus teneatur ad salutem suam credere, confidere & obedire Iesu Christo, ut servatori suo, qui ipsi salutem æternam, merito suo, & præstita satisfactione Deo Patri pro peccatis ipsius pepererit?
units.tr: Whether the Christian is bound to believe, trust and obey Jesus Christ as his Saviour, who by his own merit, and by the satisfaction he rendered to God the Father for sins, has procured eternal salvation for him.

units.la: DECLARATIO QVÆSTIONIS.
units.tr: DECLARATION OF THE QUESTION.

units.la: Observandum vero hic, nos statuere: 1. JESUM CHRISTUM esse Dei vivétis Filium unigenitum. (Matth. 16. dicit hic Jesus Discipulis: Vos autem quem me dicitis esse? Respondens vero Simon Petrus dixit: Tu es Christus Filius ille Dei viventis. Tunc respondens Jesus, dixit ei: Beatus es Simo Bar-jona, quia caro & sanguis hoc non retexit tibi, sed Pater meus, qui est in cœlis. Sed & ego dico tibi: Tu es Petrus, & super hanc petrā adi-ficabo Ecclesiam meam, & porta inferorum non praevalebunt ei. Petri hanc confessionem amplexamur: quia Christus fide hanc Petri approbat effectu, scilicet beatitudine: Beatus es, inquit: & causa procreante, quam dicit esse Patrem coelestem. Proinde credimus. 1. Quod Christus nō solum sit Filius Hominis, sed etiam Filius ille Dei Viventis, ac proinde verus Deus & Homo in una persona 2. Quod hic filius hominis & Dei sit Christus, Unctus scilicet a Deo in Doctore, qui nos edoceat rationem consequendi salute æternam: in summum Sacerdote, qui sacrificio sui corporis peccata nostra expiet, suaq; intercessione Deum nobis reconciliet: & deniq; in Regem æternum, qui corda nostra gubernet per Verbum & Spiritum S. suaq; potentia nos defendat contra hostes, donec ad fruitionem plenam Regni coelestis nos ad se assumat. Sic Joannes (Johan. 1.) testatus est de Christo, & clamavit dicens: Hic est de quo dicebam, is qui me sequitur, antepositus est mihi: quia prior me erat. erat, & ex plenitudine omnes accepimus, & gra-tiam supra gratiam. Nam Lex per Mosen data est: Gratia & Veritas per Jesum Christum praestita est. Deum nemo vidit unquam: Unigenitus ille Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ille exposuit.
units.tr: Here we must observe that we maintain: 1. That JESUS CHRIST is the only-begotten Son of the living God. (Matthew 16 records Jesus asking his disciples: "But who do you say that I am?" Simon Peter answered: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." Then Jesus answered and said to him: "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jona, for flesh and blood have not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven." "And I say to you: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.") We embrace Peter's confession, because Christ approves Peter's faith by its effect, namely blessedness, saying "Blessed are you," and by its originating cause, which he names as the heavenly Father. Therefore we believe: 1. That Christ is not only the Son of Man, but also that Son of the living God, and so true God and Man in one person. 2. That this Son of God and Man is the Christ, that is, anointed by God as Teacher, to teach us the way of obtaining eternal salvation; as High Priest, to expiate our sins by the sacrifice of his body and to reconcile God to us by his intercession; and finally as eternal King, to govern our hearts through the Word and the Holy Spirit, to defend us by his power against our enemies, until he takes us to himself for the full enjoyment of the heavenly kingdom. Thus John (John 1) testified of Christ and cried out, saying: "This is he of whom I said, he who comes after me is preferred before me, for he was before me. And of his fullness we have all received, and grace upon grace. For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ. No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him."

units.la: Cum Joanne igitur credimus, Jesum esse Unigenitum illum Filium, qui est in sinu Patris, & novit arcana Patris in illius pe-ctore[?] quasi recondita, qui Johanne Baptista fuit prior, ut Deus, qui item hic Servator noster ostenditur, qui donorum omnium affluentiam in se continet, ita ut nulla salutis gutta aliunde petenda sit.
units.tr: Therefore with John we believe that Jesus is that only-begotten Son who is in the bosom of the Father, and who knows the secrets of the Father, as if they were hidden in his breast, who was before John the Baptist, as God; and who is likewise shown to be our Saviour, containing in himself the whole abundance of gifts, so that no drop of salvation is to be sought elsewhere.

units.la: In Lege adumbrata duntaxat su-it spiritualium bonorum imago: In Christo vero bona illa solide praestan-tur, nempe, Remissio peccatorum, cordis renovatio, & legis in eo inscriptio.
units.tr: In the Law there was only a shadow of spiritual goods; but in Christ those goods are truly bestowed: namely, the remission of sins, the renewal of the heart, and the inscription of the law in him.

units.la: III. Deinde credimus, hunc Unigenitus Viventis Dei Filium esse verū ac aeternum Deum, in saecula benedictum. Johan. 1. In principio erat λόγος ille (hoc est Christus, ut appareret ex v. 14.) & λόγος ille erat apud Deum, eratque ille λόγος Deus. Hic erat in principio a-pud Deum. Omnia per hunc facta sunt; & ab-sque eo factum est nihil, quod factum sit. Si fuit λόγος ille tum, cum res creatae esse in-cipeciperent, certè fuit ab æterno; cum ante res creatas nihil fuerit præter creatorem Deum. Erat autem λόγος[?] ille apud Deum, scilicet Patrem, imò erat Deus, nempe unius essentiæ cum Patre & Spiritu S. 1. Johan. 5[?]. v. 20. Scimus Filium Dei venisse, & dedisse nobis mentem, ut cognoscamus Verum illum, & simus in Vero illo (scilicet Deo Patre) & in filio ejus Jesu Christo; hic est Verus ille Deus, & vita illa æterna. Rom. 9. v. 5[?]. Ex Patribus est Christus, quod ad carnem attinet, qui est supra omnes Deus laudandus in secula. Hic Apostolus non ponit punctum post omnes, sed ubi mentionem facit originis Christi secundum carnem, vult simul indicare deitatem ipsius, idq; ad laudem Judæorum. Apocal. 1. v. 8. Ego (scilicet Jesus Christus, fidus ille testis, primogenitus ex mortuis, ac Princeps Regum terræ, qui vos a peccatis vestris lavo per sanguinem meum) sum A et Ω, hoc est, principium & finis, dicit Dominus, Qui est, et Qui erat, et qui venturus est ille Omnipotens.
units.tr: III. Next we believe that this only-begotten Son of the living God is the true and eternal God, blessed for ever. John 1: In the beginning was that Word (that is, Christ, as appears from verse 14), and that Word was with God, and that Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that was made. If that Word existed when created things began to exist, then certainly he existed from eternity, since before created things there was nothing but the Creator God. Now that Word was with God, namely the Father; indeed he was God, one in essence with the Father and the Holy Spirit. 1 John 5, verse 20: We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us understanding, that we may know him who is true, and may be in him who is true (namely God the Father), and in his Son Jesus Christ; this is the true God and eternal life. Romans 9, verse 5: Of the fathers is Christ, as concerning the flesh, who is God over all, blessed for ever. The Apostle does not put a full stop after all; rather, when he mentions the origin of Christ according to the flesh, he means at the same time to indicate his deity, and this to the praise of the Jews. Revelation 1, verse 8: I am (namely Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the Prince of the kings of the earth, who washes us from our sins by his blood) the Alpha and the Omega, that is, the beginning and the end, says the Lord, who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.

units.la: III. Hic unigenitus Dei viventis Filius, Deus laudandus in secula, est ille, qui in carne manifestatus. 1. Tim. 3. v. 16. ille qui pro nobis passus & mortuus est.
units.tr: III. This only-begotten Son of the living God, God blessed for ever, is he who was manifested in the flesh, 1 Timothy 3, verse 16, he who suffered and died for us.

units.la: 1. Pet. 3. v.18. Ille, qui purgatione peccatorum nostrorum per seipsum facta, consedit ad dextram Majestatis in excelsis, Heb. 1. v. 3. ille qui Mediator inter Deum & Homines est: 1. Tim. 2. v. 5. ille qui est caput Ecclesiæ, Ephes. 1. v. 22. ille denique qui est Sacerdos & Rex unicus. Hebræor. 2. v. 7. 24. 25. Apocal. 19. vers. 16.
units.tr: 1 Peter 3, verse 18: He who, having made purification of our sins by himself, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high. Hebrews 1, verse 3: he who is the Mediator between God and men, 1 Timothy 2, verse 5; he who is the head of the Church, Ephesians 1, verse 22; he, finally, who is the one Priest and King. Hebrews 2, verses 7, 24, 25; Revelation 19, verse 16.

units.la: IV. De hoc, inquam, Jesu Christo dicitur in quæstione, quod salutem æ-ternam a nobis acquisierit, adeoq; sit Servator noster, seu salutis æternæ Auctor, Princeps Vitæ talis, qui nos ab æterna damnatione & potestate tenebrarum, a servitute & reatu peccati liberavit: & contra beatam vitam ac immortalitatem nobis comparavit. Hebræor. 5. v. 9. Hic consecratus factus est AUCTOR SALUTIS ÆTERNÆ omnibus qui auscultant ipsi. Actor. 3. v. 15.
units.tr: IV. Of this Jesus Christ, I say, it is said in the question that he has obtained eternal salvation for us, and so is our Saviour, or the Author of eternal salvation, the Prince of Life, who has freed us from eternal damnation and the power of darkness, from the bondage and guilt of sin, and has won for us a blessed life and immortality in exchange. Hebrews 5, verse 9: Having been made perfect, he became the AUTHOR OF ETERNAL SALVATION to all who obey him. Acts 3, verse 15: You killed the Prince of Life, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.

units.la: Principem vitæ trucidastis, quem Deus excitavit a mortuis, cujus rei nos testes sumus. Hebræor. 2. v. 14. 15. Quoniam igitur pueri participes sunt carnis & sanguinis, ipse quoq; consimiliter particeps factus est eorundem, ut per mortem aboleret eum, qui mortis imperium habet, hoc est, Diabolu; & liberos redderet, quot quot metu mortis per omne vitam obnoxii erant servituti. 1. Pet. 1. v. 18. Sciatis vos non caducis rebus, argento & auro fuisse redemtos ex vana vestra conversatione, ex patrum traditionibus ac cepta: Sed pretioso sanguine, utpote agni immaculati, & incontaminati, nempe Christi, Gal. 3. v. 13. Christus nos redemit ab execratione legis, dum pro nobis factus est execratio; (scriptum est enim: Execrabilis quisquis pendet in ligno) ut in gentibus benedictio Abrahae exstet in Christo Jesu, utque promissum illum Spiritum accipiamus per fidem. 2. Timoth. 1. v. 10. Gratia patefacta nunc est per illustrem illum adventum Servatoris nostri Jesu Christi, qui & mortem abolevit, & Vitam in lucem produxit, ac immortalitatem per Evangelium. Hunc JESUM, hoc est, SERVATOREM dici declarat Angelus Gabriel, Matth. 1.
units.tr: Hebrews 2, verses 14-15: Since therefore the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he himself likewise took part in the same, that through death he might destroy him who has the power of death, that is, the devil, and deliver those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage. 1 Peter 1, verse 18: You know that you were redeemed not with corruptible things, silver and gold, from your vain conversation handed down from your fathers, but with the precious blood of a lamb without blemish and without spot, namely Christ. Galatians 3, verse 13: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us (for it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree), that the blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, and that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith. 2 Timothy 1, verse 10: The grace which has now been revealed through the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the Gospel. That this JESUS, that is, the SAVIOUR, is so called, the angel Gabriel declares, Matthew 1.

units.la: Quod servaturus sit populum suum a peccatis ipsorum, nempe, tum remissionem peccatorum nobis impetrando, tum ipsa peccata in nobis abolendo, denique loco aeterni supplicii beatam vitam nobis conferendo.
units.tr: That he will save his people from their sins: namely, by obtaining for us the forgiveness of sins, by abolishing sin itself in us, and finally by bestowing on us a blessed life in place of eternal punishment.

units.la: V. Servatorem hunc aeternam nobis salutem peperisse dicit Quaestio, Merito suo & satisfactione p̄stita Deo Patri pro peccatis nostris, non tantum doctrina & efficacia, sed etiam persolutione sufficientis λύτρῳ[?] ac pretii redē-tionis pro nobis; ut non tantum intel-ligatur Magister & Doctor noster Chri-stus, qui nobis viam salutis æternæ annuntiarit, & exemplo vitæ & mortis suæ ostenderit ac obsignarit; non tantum intelligatur Dominus & Princeps Vitæ, qui habeat potestatem plenam promittendi & conferendi vitam æternam omnibus verbo suo credentibus & præceptis vitæ obedientibus: sed etiam credatur SPONSOR NOSTER; q; & a nobis sposponderit, & a nobis per-solverit redemtionis nostræ pretium, Salutem promeruerit, se hostiam pro peccatis nostris obtulerit Deo Patri, il-lamq; apud eum valere cupiat pro nostri reconciliatione; ut paulo post hæc manifestis demo-strabitur argumen-tis.
units.tr: V. The Question says that this Saviour has won eternal salvation for us by his merit and by the satisfaction he made to God the Father for our sins, not only by his teaching and efficacy but also by paying a sufficient ransom [λύτρῳ] and the price of redemption on our behalf. Christ is therefore to be understood not only as our Master and Teacher, who announced to us the way of eternal salvation and showed and sealed it by the example of his life and death, nor only as the Lord and Prince of Life, who has full power to promise and bestow eternal life on all who believe his word and obey the precepts of life; he is also to be believed to be OUR SURETY, who stood surety in our place and paid the price of our redemption on our behalf, earned our salvation, offered himself as a sacrifice for our sins to God the Father, and desires that this offering should avail with him for our reconciliation. This will be shown shortly by clear arguments.

units.la: CAPUT III. ΣΩΤΗΡΙΑΝ[?] ET SALVANDI RATIONEM CHRISTI MERITO ET SATISFACTIONE truncatam vel destitutam, insufficientem esse asseritur.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. THE MANNER OF SALVATION AND THE SAVING OF CHRIST, ASSERTED TO BE TRUNCATED OR DEFECTIVE, AND INSUFFICIENT, AS REGARDS MERIT AND SATISFACTION.

units.la: PROPOSITAM quaestionem magno conatu negant infesti hostes Meriti et Satisfactionis Jesu Christi, ejusque affirmationem expresse audent falsam ac impiam appellare: Negant, inquam, Christum Jesum servare nos merito & efficacia, qualiter nos intelligimꝰ.
units.tr: The question proposed is denied with great effort by the hostile enemies of the merit and satisfaction of Jesus Christ, who dare to call its affirmation expressly false and impious. They deny, I say, that Christ Jesus saves us by merit and efficacy in the sense in which we understand it.

units.la: MERITO scilicet servat nos, ut Sacerdos, quia Sacrificio suo expiavit nostra peccata, atq; ita remissionem illorum & vitam aeternam nobis meruit.
units.tr: By merit, of course, he saves us as Priest, because by his sacrifice he expiated our sins and so merited for us their remission and eternal life.

units.la: EFFICACIA vero servat nos ut Rex, quatenus in nobis efficit per Verbū & Spi-ritum suum tum Fidem, qua testimonium Evangelii de remissione peccatorum apprehendi-mus: tum studium pietatis, quo nos gratos Deo pro tanto beneficio declaramus, eàq; viam ad vi-tam aeternam deducimur.
units.tr: By efficacy, however, he saves us as King, in so far as he works in us, through his Word and Spirit, both faith, by which we lay hold of the testimony of the Gospel concerning the remission of sins, and a zeal for godliness, by which we declare ourselves pleasing to God for so great a benefit, and by which we are led along the way to eternal life.

units.la: Ipsi autem Jesum Christum esse Servatorem nostrum contendunt.
units.tr: But they themselves contend that Jesus Christ is our Saviour in these ways:

units.la: I. DOCTRINA; quatenus aeterna sa-lutis viam ipse nobis annunciavit.
units.tr: I. By doctrine, in so far as he himself announced to us the way of eternal salvation.

units.la: II. EXEMPLO; quatenus annuntiatam salutis viam nobis in sua ipsius persona ostendit, & multis modis confirmavit.
units.tr: II. By example, in so far as he showed us in his own person the way of salvation that had been announced, and confirmed it in many ways.

units.la: III. COMMUNICATIONE; quatenus plenissimâ potestate in cœlo & terra acceptâ se vitam æternam nobis daturū satis præbavit.
units.tr: III. By communication, in so far as, having received full power in heaven and on earth, he showed that he would give eternal life to us.

units.la: CAPITIS III. SECTIO I.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. SECTION I.

units.la: CHRISTUS SERVATOR NOSTER EST ANNUNTIATIONE VOLUNTATIS PATERNÆ DE NOSTRI REDEMPTIONE.
units.tr: CHRIST OUR SAVIOUR IS SO BY ANNOUNCING THE FATHER'S WILL CONCERNING OUR REDEMPTION.

units.la: CHRISTUM JESUM, qui venit quærere & salvum facere, quod perierat, esse Mediatorem, Redemtorem & Servatorem nostrum agnosco: & ut Mediatoris ac Servatoris officio plenè defungeretur, ipsum esse à Deo patre nobis constitutū Doctorem, Sacerdotem & Regem credo, in quo ita omnes Mediationis gradus ac partes concur-rant. Mediationis dico gradus sex.
units.tr: I acknowledge Jesus Christ, who came to seek and to save that which was lost, to be our Mediator, Redeemer and Saviour. And so that he might fully discharge the office of Mediator and Saviour, I believe that he has been appointed by God the Father to be our Teacher, Priest and King, and that in him all the degrees and parts of mediation meet. I say there are six degrees of mediation.

units.la: Primus est discretio & dijudicatio causæ inter partes diffidétes (sicut ar-bitri bitri interdum solet vocari Mediatores.)
units.tr: The first is the discerning and judging of a cause between disputing parties (just as an arbiter is sometimes also called a mediator).

units.la: Secund' est referre utrinq; pacta & conditiones utriusq; partis (quomodo internuncii solent Mediatores dici. Sicut Moses vocatur Mediator veteris Testamenti, Heb. 9, v. 12, internuncius referens ad populum mandata Dei. Sic & Filius Dei annuntiavit humano generi arcana voluntate aeterni Patris.) Tertius est intercessio & supplicatio pro ea parte, quae laesit & offendit. Quartus est, persolvere & satisfacere uni parti pro altera. Quintus gradus est, satisfactionem illam efficaciter applicare. Deniq; Sextus est eos, pro quibus satisfactum est, contra hostes tueri, & in parta salute conservare.
units.tr: The second is to carry the terms and conditions of each party to the other (go-betweens are commonly called mediators in this sense. Thus Moses is called the Mediator of the Old Testament, Heb. 9, v. 12, a go-between who carried God's commands to the people. So too the Son of God announced to the human race the hidden will of the eternal Father). The third is intercession and supplication on behalf of the party that has been wronged and offended. The fourth is to pay and make satisfaction to one party on behalf of the other. The fifth degree is to apply that satisfaction effectively. Finally, the sixth is to defend those for whom satisfaction has been made against their enemies, and to keep them in the salvation obtained.

units.la: Tres priores gradus sunt suo modo communes, nam & Moses Mediator fuit per modum Arbitrii, Internuncii, & Intercessionis. Tres vero posteriores sunt Christo nostro Mediatori proprii. Ipse n. solus est nostre Mediator per modum Satisfactionis, Applicationis & Conservationis. Atq; ita primus & secundus respicit Munus Christi Propheticum; tertius & quartus munus Sacerdotale; quintus denique & sextus officium Re-gium.
units.tr: The first three degrees are in their own way common to others, for Moses too was a mediator by way of arbiter, go-between and intercessor. The last three, however, belong properly to Christ our Mediator, for he alone is our Mediator by way of satisfaction, application and preservation. Thus the first and second relate to Christ's prophetic office, the third and fourth to his priestly office, and the fifth and sixth finally to his kingly office.

units.la: Agnosco itaq; Christum Jesum esse Servatorem nostrum, primo quatenus ipse nobis æternæ salutis viam annuntiavit, & voluntatem Patris de redemtione generis humani plane & plenè nobis patefecit.
units.tr: I acknowledge, therefore, that Jesus Christ is our Saviour, first insofar as he has announced to us the way of eternal salvation and has plainly and fully revealed to us the Father's will concerning the redemption of the human race.

units.la: Ait enim ipse Jes. 61. Luc. 4. Actor.
units.tr: For Jesus himself says (Isa. 61; Luke 4; Acts):

units.la: 16. Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me Dominus, ad annunciandum mansuetis sive Evangelizandum pauperibus misit me, ut mederer contritis corde, & prædicarem captivis indulgentiam, & clausis apertionem. Et Psal. 2. v. 6. Ego autem constitutus sum Rex ab eo super montem sanctum ejus, prædicans præceptum ejus. Et Psal. 22. v. 23. Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis, in medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te. Joh. 1. v. 18. Deum nemo vidit unquam: Unigenitus Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarravit. Johan. 15. v. 15. Vos autem dixi amicos, quia omnia, quæ audivi à Patre meo, nota feci vobis. Matth. 11. v. 27. Omnia mihi tradita sunt à Patre meo: & nemo novit Filium nisi Pater, neque quisquam Patrem novit nisi Filius, & cuicunq; voluerit filius revelare. Coloss. 2. v. 3. In Christo sunt omnes thesauri sapientiæ & cognitionis abscondit, Ephes. 2. v. 17. Christus veniens Evangelizavit pacem vobis, qui procul eratis, & iis qui prope erant.
units.tr: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to preach good tidings to the meek, or to evangelize the poor, to heal the broken-hearted, and to proclaim liberty to the captives and opening to those who are shut in. And Psalm 2, v. 6: Yet I have been set up as king by him upon his holy hill, declaring his decree. And Psalm 22, v. 23: I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you. John 1, v. 18: No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him. John 15, v. 15: But I have called you friends, because all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you. Matt. 11, v. 27: All things have been delivered to me by my Father; and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wills to reveal him. Col. 2, v. 3: In Christ are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden. Eph. 2, v. 17: Christ came and preached peace to you who were far off, and to those who were near.

units.la: Agnosco proinde me debere hunc Magistrum & Doctorem mihi viam vitæ annuntiantem, tanquam immediatum divinæ veritatis testem (de quo Jesa. 55. v. 4. Ecce testem populis dedi eum, Ducem ac Præceptorem gentib⁹) reverenter audire, Matth. 17. v. 5. Adhuc eo loquente ecce nubes lucida obumbravit eos, & ecce vox e nube dicens: Hic est Filius ille meus dilectus, in quo acquiesco; ipsum audite. Hinc Apostolus Petrus Cap. 1. posterioris Epistolæ ita testatur: Non arte compositas fabulas secuti, notam vobis fecimus Domini nostri Jesu Christi potentiam & adventum; sed qui oculis nostris conspeximus ipsius Majestatem. Acceperat enim a Deo Patre Honorem & Gloriam, Voce ad illum delata hujusmodi a magnifica Gloria: Hic est ille Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi complacui. Et hanc vocem nos audivimus de cœlo delatam, cum essemus cum illo in monte Sancto.
units.tr: I acknowledge, then, that I ought to hear reverently this Teacher and Master, who announces to me the way of life, as the immediate witness of divine truth (of whom Isa. 55, v. 4: Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the nations), Matt. 17, v. 5: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him. Hence the Apostle Peter in the first chapter of his second Epistle bears witness thus: We did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty. For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when such a voice was borne to him from the magnificent glory: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. And we heard this voice borne from heaven, when we were with him on the holy mountain.

units.la: Prædixit etiam hoc Moses Deut. 18. ut & est Actor. 3. Quoniam Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus Deus vester, de fratribus vestris, tanquam me; ipsum audietis juxta omnia, quæcunque locutus fuerit vobis. Merito hunc Jesum dantem nobis sermone Dei Patris (Joh.17.) audio, qp-pe in quo tanquam viva & perfecta imagine Pater se totum nobis conspiciendum exhibet, Johan. 14. v.9. Philippe, qui vidit me, vidit Patrem: quomodo igitur tu dicis: Ostende nobis Patrem? Non credis, me in Patre, & Patrem in me esse? Verba, quae ego loquor vobis, a me ipso non loquor, sed Pater, qui in me manet, ipse facit opera illa. Credite mihi, me in Patre, & Patrem in me esse. (Hic inhabitationem ineffabilem Patris in se, probat Christus, ex doctrina sua & Miraculis, & Majestatem Dei se in sua Doctrina & factis plane conspicuam praebere ait) Sic 2. Corinth. 4. v. 4. Lumen Evangelii Gloriae Christi, hominis dicitur irradiare, qui Christus est, imago Dei. Christus missus est, ut in ipso tanquam illius imagine inaspectabilem Deum intueri & cognoscere possimus. Et ad Col. 1. v. 15. Christus est imago Dei invisibilis, primogenitus omnis creaturae. Nam per eum condita sunt omnia, & quae in terra visibilia & invisibilia sunt. Heb. 1. vers. 3. Qui cum sit splendor gloriae & character personae illius, sustinetque omnia verbo suae potentiae, etc.
units.tr: Moses also foretold this in Deut. 18, as is also cited in Acts 3: The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; you shall hear him in all that he shall speak to you. Rightly, then, I hear this Jesus, who gives us the word of God the Father (John 17), for in him, as in a living and perfect image, the Father presents himself to be seen by us entirely; John 14, v. 9: Philip, whoever has seen me has seen the Father; how then do you say, Show us the Father? Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak on my own authority, but the Father who dwells in me does his works. Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father in me. (Here Christ proves the ineffable indwelling of the Father in himself from his teaching and his miracles, and says that the majesty of God is plainly seen in his teaching and deeds.) So too 2 Cor. 4, v. 4: The light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, shines forth. Christ was sent so that in him, as in that image, we might behold and know the invisible God. And Col. 1, v. 15: Christ is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature. For by him were all things created, both in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible. Heb. 1, v. 3: Who, being the brightness of his glory and the express image of his person, upholds all things by the word of his power, etc.

units.la: Quod si igitur Apostoli & alii, eo, quod salutis viam suis auditoribus annunciarunt nuntiarunt, dicuntur seruasse illos, adeoq; Seruatores illorum; Paulus enim Rom. 11. v. 14. scribit: Si quo modo ad aemulandum provocem carnem meam, & seruem aliquot ex illis. 1. Corinth. 9. v. 22. Omnibus factus sum omnia, ut omnino aliquos seruem. 1. Tim. 4. Attende tibi ipsi & doctrinae; perfiste in his. Hoc enim faciens, & te ipsum seruabis, & eos qui te audiunt. Jacobus in fine Epistolae suae sic ait: Qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viae suae, seruabit animam a morte: Multo igitur magis unigenitus Dei Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, & ab initio ad hoc docendi munus obeundum a Patre (qui etiam per eum loquutus est) delectus, viam salutis annuntiavit, atq; in cuius nomine Apostoli ab ipso missi Evangelium praedicarunt, Seruator noster dicitur.
units.tr: If, then, the Apostles and others are said to have saved their hearers because they announced to them the way of salvation, and so are called saviours of them, (for Paul writes in Rom. 11, v. 14: If by any means I may provoke my flesh to emulation and save some of them; 1 Cor. 9, v. 22: I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some; 1 Tim. 4: Take heed to yourself and to the teaching; persist in these things. For in doing so you will save both yourself and those who hear you), and James at the end of his Epistle says: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death, then how much more is the only-begotten Son of God, who is in the bosom of the Father, and who was chosen by the Father from the beginning for the office of teaching (and who also spoke through him), said to be our Saviour: he who announced the way of salvation, and in whose name the Apostles, sent by him, preached the gospel.

units.la: Insufficientem autē dico hunc Seruandi modum; si seorsim accipiatur, ut qui Mediatoris, Conciliatoris & Seruatoris (qui partes scilicet diffidentes reconciliat seipsum interponendo Medium, satisfaciendo pro offensa, pròq; ea deprecando) Naturam & officium <bl>ἀλλ</bl> constituat neutiquam. Soli quippe fi-bi hoc sicut. bi hoc servatoris munus vendicat Filius Dei, ut qui gloriam hanc suam alteri non tribuat, Ies. 48. v. 11. Nec ullum homine in ejus societatem admittit. Actor. 4. v. 12. Nec enim est in alio quoquam salus, nec aliud nomen est sub caelo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos servari. Hoc itaque modo nullus alius Servator esse potest praeter JESUM CHRISTUM.
units.tr: I say, however, that this manner of saving is insufficient if it is taken on its own, as if it alone constituted the nature and office of the Mediator, Reconciler and Saviour (who, that is, reconciles the disagreeing parties by placing himself between them, makes satisfaction for the offence, and intercedes for it). The Son of God claims this office of Saviour for himself alone, and does not give this glory of his to another (Isa. 48, v. 11), nor admits any human being into partnership in it (Acts 4, v. 12): Nor is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved. In this way, therefore, no other Saviour can exist apart from JESUS CHRIST.

units.la: Viam autem hanc salutis & Prophetae olim praemonstrarunt, & Apostoli a Christo ablegati in nomine ejus annunciarunt, uti ancilla habens Spiritum Pythonis, (Actor. 16. v. 17.) Apostolos subsecuta, clamabat, dicens: Isti homines servi sunt Dei illius Summi, qui annuntiant vobis viam salutis.
units.tr: The Prophets of old also pointed out this way of salvation, and the Apostles, sent by Christ, proclaimed it in his name, just as the slave girl possessed by a spirit of Python (Acts 16:17) followed the Apostles, crying out, "These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to you the way of salvation."

units.la: Esto vero (nec enim nego hoc) ꝙ Prophetę non nisi de ventura hac salutis via, & quidem obscurius prophetarint; Christus vero de praesenti, & quidem manifestius praedicarit, ut illud asseritur. 1. Pet. 1. v. 10, 11, 12. Ubi dicuntur veteres illi Prophetae de salute hac diligenter inquisivisse, esse scrutati,
units.tr: Granted, though I do not deny this, that the Prophets only spoke of this way of salvation as something to come, and that they spoke rather obscurely, whereas Christ preached it as present and did so more plainly, as 1 Peter 1:10, 11, 12 asserts. There it is said that those ancient prophets searched diligently and inquired into this salvation,

units.la: & de gratiâ Evangelii nobis obventu- râ vaticinati, scrutantes scilicet, quo- nam, aut quali tempore Spiritus ille Christi, qui in ipsis agebat, gratiam il- lam Evangelii exstituram esse declara- bat, qui jam tum pronunciabat, ac te- stimonio suo comprobabat, C H R I- STUM pro nostra salute multa suo tem- pore passurum, & postea exacto humi- liationis circulo ad summam gloriam evehendum esse..
units.tr: and prophesied about the grace of the Gospel that was to come to us, inquiring, that is, at what time or in what manner the grace of the Gospel would come forth, which the Spirit of Christ, who was working in them, declared. That Spirit already announced and by his testimony confirmed that CHRIST would suffer much for our salvation in his own time, and that afterwards, once the cycle of humiliation was complete, he would be raised to the highest glory.

units.la: Dicitur etiam ibi, Prophetis à Deo patefactum esse, quod quæ futura præ- dicabant, non sibi ipsis, neque ipsis, qui ipsorum tempore vivebant, sed nobis, quorum scilicet tempore C H R I S T U S fuit exhibitus, reipsa eventura esse, de- nuntiârút, quæ omnia nobis nunc an- nuntiata sunt per Apostolos J E S U C H R I S T I, qui nimirum Evangelium nobis prædicarunt virtute Spiritus S. quem D E U S è cœlo copiosè effudit ad tanti mysterii obsignationem, &c.
units.tr: There it is also said that it was revealed by God to the Prophets that what they foretold was not for themselves, nor for those who lived in their own time, but for us, in whose time CHRIST was manifested; they announced that these things would in fact come to pass, and all of them have now been announced to us through the Apostles of JESUS CHRIST, who preached the Gospel to us by the power of the Holy Spirit, whom GOD poured out abundantly from heaven as the seal of so great a mystery, etc.

units.la: Esto etiam, quod prædictio & promissio sit rerum futurarum, annuntiatio vero rerum præsentium & pertinētium[?] ad eos, quibus illæ res annunti-arent. Esto deniq; q; Apostoli nomine Christi Domini sui, & tanquà Ministri & Legati Evangelium prædicarint.
units.tr: Grant also that prediction and promise concern things to come, while announcement concerns things present and pertaining to those to whom they were announced. Grant finally that the Apostles preached the Gospel in the name of Christ their Lord, and as ministers and envoys.

units.la: Quid tum? Satis mihi est, utrósq; eandem salutis viam prædicasse, & mū-do revelasse, nempe, Christum cruci-fixum. Actor. 10. vers. 42. & 43. Præcepit autem nobis, ut prædicaremus populo, ac testificaremur, eum esse qui definitus sit à Deo, Iudex vivorum & mortuorum. Huic enim omnes Prophetæ testimonium dant, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen ejus quemvis, qui crediderit in eum. Actor. 26. v. 22. ait Paulus: Auxilium à Deo nactus perstitit in hunc usque diem, testificans ista tum parvis tum magnis, nec quicquam dicens extra ea, quæ Prophetæ ac Moses futura prædixerunt: nempe Christum esse passurum, &c. 1. Cor. 2. v. 2. Non decreveram quicquam scire inter vos, nisi Jesum Christum, eumq; crucifixum. Novi & ipsum filium Dei Jesum Christum Ministrum ac legatum æterni sui Patris fuisse, in annunciando nobis salutis Doctrina. Jel. 53. v.11. Cognitione sui justificabit multos justus Servus meus, quorum iniquitates ipse bajulaverit.
units.tr: What then? It is enough for me that both preached the same way of salvation and revealed it to the world, namely, Christ crucified. Acts 10:42, 43: "He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God to be judge of the living and the dead. To him all the Prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name." Acts 26:22, Paul says: "Having obtained help from God, I have stood firm to this day, testifying both to small and to great, saying nothing beyond what the Prophets and Moses foretold would come: namely, that Christ would suffer," etc. 1 Cor. 2:2: "I determined to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. I also know that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was the Minister and envoy of his eternal Father in announcing to us the doctrine of salvation." Isa. 53:11: "By his knowledge my righteous Servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities."

units.la: Ideo dicit hic Servus Dei Patris Joh. 7. v. 16. Mea Doctrina, non est mea, sed ejus, qui misit me. Et cap. 14. v.10. Non credis me in Patre & Patrem in me esse? Verba, quae ego loquor vobis, à me ipso non loquor, sed Pater, qui in me manet, ipse facit opera. Heb. 1. Deus ultimis hisce diebus locutus est nobis per filium.
units.tr: Therefore this Servant of God the Father says in John 7:16: "My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me." And in chapter 14:10: "Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak on my own; but the Father, who dwells in me, does his works." Hebrews 1: "In these last days God has spoken to us by the Son."

units.la: Patris itaq; voluntatem de redemtione nostri, & viam aeternae salutis annuntiare hominibus, non est sufficiens servandi ratio, quod jam utrinq; est concessum,
units.tr: Therefore, to announce to men the will of the Father concerning our redemption and the way of eternal salvation is not a sufficient means of salvation, a point which is already conceded on both sides.

units.la: CAPITIS III. SECTIO II.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. SECTION II.

units.la: CHRISTUS EST SERVATOR NOSTER EXEMPLO VITÆ, PASSIONIS MORTIS ET GLORIOSÆ RESURRECTIONIS SUÆ.
units.tr: CHRIST IS OUR SAVIOUR BY THE EXAMPLE OF HIS LIFE, HIS PASSION, HIS DEATH AND HIS GLORIOUS RESURRECTION.

units.la: Hactenus de Salutis aeternae Via an-nuntiata. Jam de ejusdem Via ab eodem Christo confirmata videamus. Ut enim Christus dixit, se idcirco missum esse & venisse, ut praedicaret & Re-gnum Dei annuntiaret. Matth. 1. v 38. Luc. 4. v. 18.19. & 43. sic deinde affirmavit se in eum finem natum & in mundum venisse, ut testimonium redderet Veritati. Johan. 18. verf. 37. Unde testis fidelis appellatus est. Apoc. 1. verf. 5. & Cap. 3. v. 14. Et fuisse eum testimonium temporibus suis, inquit Paulus 1.Ti-moth. 2. v. 6. quia scilicet, plenam Dei erga nos benevolentiae fidem fecerit.
units.tr: So far, the way of eternal salvation has been announced. Now let us see how that same way was confirmed by Christ himself. Christ said that he had therefore been sent and had come, that he might preach and proclaim the Kingdom of God, Matt. 1. v. 38. Luke 4. v. 18, 19, & 43. Then he affirmed that he was born and had come into the world for this end, that he might bear witness to the truth, John 18. v. 37. Hence he is called the faithful witness, Rev. 1. v. 5. and ch. 3. v. 14. Paul also says that he was a testimony in his own times, 1 Tim. 2. v. 6. namely because he gave full proof of God's good will toward us.

units.la: Jam vero si is qui salutem annuntiat, Servator dicitur; multo magis SER-VATOR dicendus erit, si eandem salutis viam, veram esse, aperte probet & confirmet. CONFIRMARE autem dicitur Christus viam aeternae Salutis; 1. Exemplo vitae suae. 2. Editis Miraculis. 3. Profusione sanguinis sui. 4. Gloriosa sui ipsius Exaltatione.
units.tr: Now if he who announces salvation is called Saviour, he will be called Saviour all the more if he plainly proves and confirms that this same way of salvation is true. Christ is said to confirm the way of eternal salvation: (1) by the example of his life; (2) by the miracles he performed; (3) by the outpouring of his blood; (4) by his glorious exaltation.

units.la: I. Agnosco Christum nobis vivendi Exemplum reliquisse, & nos Christianos ad imitandum Christum nostrum in vita & morte incitari passim. Lego enim Matth. 16. v. 24. Tunc Iesus dixit discipulis suis: Si quis vult pone me venire, abneget sese, et tollat crucem suam, ac sequatur me. Rom. 6. v. 4. & 5. Sepulti igitur sumus una cum Christo per baptismum in mortem, ut sicut Christus excitatus est ex mortuis in gloriam Patris, ita & nos in nova vita ambulemus. Nam si cum eo plantati coaluimus conformatione mortis ejus, nimirum etiam resurrectionis conformatione coalescemus.
units.tr: I. I acknowledge that Christ left us an example of how to live, and that we Christians are urged everywhere to imitate our Christ in life and in death. For I read, Matt. 16. v. 24: Then Jesus said to his disciples: If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. And Rom. 6. v. 4 & 5: Therefore we were buried with Christ through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead to the glory of the Father, so we too should walk in newness of life. For if we have grown together with him in the likeness of his death, we shall surely also grow together in the likeness of his resurrection.

units.la: Video hic nos Christianos duplicē cum Christo habere conformitatem & communionem; Unam in Morte, alteram in Resurrectione. Prior huc spectat, ut sciamus nos peccatis esse mortuos: Posterior partim ad resurrectio-nem nostri ad spiritualem vitam, partim ad futuram corporum resuscitatio-nem ad vitam æternam referri potest.
units.tr: Here I see that we Christians have a twofold conformity and communion with Christ: one in his death, the other in his resurrection. The former points to this, that we know we are dead to sins. The latter may be referred partly to our rising to spiritual life, and partly to the future resurrection of our bodies to eternal life.

units.la: Quemadmodum enim Christus peccatis semel mortuus, deinceps immortale vitam in cœlo degit, ita quicunq; peccatis in hac vitâ mortui iustitiæ student, illi tandé æternâ vitâ cum Christo in cœlo fruentur. Christus autem peccatis mortuus dicitur, partim pro peccatis nostris moriēdo, partim ipsis miseriis atque infirmitatibus suæ vitæ defungendo. Ita etiam Ephes. 4. v. 20. &c. lego: Vos autem non ita didicistis Christum (seu Christi Doctrinam) si modo eum audistis (eam recte intellexistis) & ab ipso edocti estis, quanam sit veritas in Christo Iesu, seu quisnam sit verus Christianismus. Nempe, ut deponatis veterem illum hominem (qui nihil aliud est, quam pristina vestra in peccatis conversatio) qui fallacibus cupiditatibus addictus & ipse perit; & nos una perdit.
