Contra vero re-novemini spiritu mentis vestrae, & novum illum hominem induatis, qui secundum Deum conditus est, ad justitiam veramq; Sanctimoniam: Col. 3[?]. Si resurrexistis cum Christo, superna quarite, ubi Christus est, ad dextram Dei sedens: superna curate, non terrestria. Nam mortui estis, & vita vestra abscondita est, cum Christo, in Deo. Quando Christus, Vita illa nostra, patefactus fuerit, cum & vos cum eo patefietis gloriosi. Mortificate igitur membra vestra terrestria, &c. 1. Pet. 2. v. 21. Nam ad hoc vocati estis, quoniam Christus passus est pro vobis, relinquens vobis exemplar, ut insequeremini vestigia ipsius.
units.tr: For just as Christ, once dead to sin, now lives an immortal life in heaven, so all who in this life are dead to sins and strive after righteousness will at last enjoy eternal life with Christ in heaven. Christ is said to have been dead to sins partly by dying for our sins, and partly by undergoing the very miseries and infirmities of his life. So also I read, Eph. 4. v. 20 etc.: But you have not so learned Christ (or the doctrine of Christ), if indeed you have heard him (rightly understood him) and have been taught by him what is the truth in Jesus Christ, or what true Christianity is. Namely, that you put off the old man (who is nothing other than your former way of life in sins), who, given over to deceitful lusts, is himself perishing, and destroys us along with him. But on the contrary, be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who is created according to God, in righteousness and true holiness. Col. 3[?]: If you have risen with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is, sitting at the right hand of God. Mind the things above, not the things on earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ, who is our life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory. Therefore mortify your earthly members, etc. 1 Pet. 2. v. 21: For to this you were called, since Christ suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in his steps.

units.la: Hoc est, Hoc requirit vestra profes-sio, ad quam pridem vocati estis, ut propter Dei gloriam, hominum injurias perferatis, atque ita Christo in hac vita conformes reddamini. Nam ipse quoque nullo suo merito, multa admodum dura & dira propter nostram salutem perpessus est, atque ita vobis omnibus exemplum reliquit, ut vestigiis ipsius insisteretis. 1. Johan. 2. ver. 3. Per hoc scimus, nos eum nosse, si mandata ipsius observamus: & verf. 6. Qui dicit, se in eo habitare, debet sicut ipse ambulavit, ita & ipse ambulare. Hoc est, cum Deus Jesum dederit propropitiationem pro peccatis nostris, æquum est eum viciflim a nobis diligi, & mandata ejus seruari. Hinc enim constare nobis debet, nos verâ ipsius cognitione præditos esse, fi præcepta ipsius studiosè observemus.
units.tr: That is to say, your profession, to which you were called long ago, requires that for the glory of God you bear the injuries of men, and so be made conformed to Christ in this life. For he too, without any merit of his own, suffered many very hard and dreadful things for our salvation, and so left all of you an example, that you should tread in his footsteps. 1 John 2. v. 3: By this we know that we know him, if we keep his commandments; and v. 6: Whoever says that he abides in him ought himself also to walk just as he walked. That is, since God has given Jesus as the propitiation for our sins, it is fitting that in turn he be loved by us and his commandments be kept. For from this we ought to be assured that we have true knowledge of him, if we diligently observe his precepts.

units.la: Oportet eos, qui fe Christianos esse, & in Christo habitare profitentur, vitam hanc similiter ad Dei voluntatē conformare, quemadmodum Christus suam conformavit. Nemo enim verè ad Christum pertinet, quin eodem Spiritu Dilectionis & Obedientiæ agatur, cum non nuda Professio, sed Imitatio Christianum faciat. Cap. 3. v. 16. Per hoc, inquit, cognovimus caritatem, quia ille animam suam pro nobis posuit: nos igitur debemus pro fratribus animas ponere. Cap. 4. v. 17. Per hoc expleta est caritas in nobis, ut fiduciam habeamus in die judicii, quod qualis ille est, tales & nos sumus in hoc mundo, h. e. cum proximum ex animo diligimus, inde colligimus ingenium, noftrū, q; quidem ex regeneratione habemus, conformes esse Patri nostro cœlesti: Et scimus, nos in die judicii à Deo nō iri damnatū, si qualis ipse est, & nos tales sumus in hoc mundo. Hæc ita quidem esse debere prolixè largior; sed modum hunc exemplarem servandi, vel cum primo sufficientem, vel præcipuum esse, inficior.
units.tr: Those who profess that they are Christians and dwell in Christ ought likewise to conform this life to God's will, just as Christ conformed his. For no one truly belongs to Christ unless he is moved by the same Spirit of love and obedience, since it is not bare profession but imitation that makes a Christian. Ch. 3. v. 16: By this, he says, we have known love, because he laid down his life for us; so we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. Ch. 4. v. 17: By this love is made perfect in us, that we may have confidence in the day of judgment, because as he is, so are we in this world. That is, when we love our neighbour from the heart, we thereby infer that our disposition, which we indeed have from regeneration, is conformed to our heavenly Father; and we know that on the day of judgment we shall not be condemned by God, if we are such as he is in this world. I freely grant at length that these things ought to be so; but I deny that this exemplary way of keeping (the law) is either sufficient in the first place or the chief one.

units.la: I. Si enim illi, qui nobis imitandi proponuntur, sunt servatores, certè Sancti homines quoq; dicentur Servatores. Nam & Sanctorum hominum exempla nobis imitanda proponit Sacra Scriptura, 1. Corinth. 11. Paulus ait:
units.tr: I. For if those who are set before us to imitate are saviours, then holy men too will surely be called saviours. For Holy Scripture also sets before us the examples of holy men to imitate. In 1 Cor. 11, Paul says:

units.la: Imitatores mei estote, sicut ego Christi, 1. Thes. 1. v. 6. Et vos imitatores nostri facti fuistis, & Domini, recepto sermone cum oppressione multa, cum gaudio Spiritus S. adeo, ut fueritis exemplaria omnibus credentibus in Macedonia & Achaia. Philip. 3. v. 17. Estote simul imitatores mei, fratres, & eos considerate, qui ita incedunt, sicut habetis nos pro exemplari. Hebr. 13. v. 8. Memores estote ducum vestrorum, qui locuti sunt vobis sermonem Dei; quorum imitamini fidem, considerantes, qui fuerit exitus conversationis ipsorum.
units.tr: Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ. 1 Thess. 1. v. 6: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with the joy of the Holy Spirit, so that you became an example to all who believe in Macedonia and Achaia. Phil. 3. v. 17: Be imitators of me together, brothers, and consider those who walk so as you have us for a pattern. Heb. 13. v. 8: Remember your leaders, who spoke to you the word of God; whose faith imitate, considering the outcome of their conduct.

units.la: II. Si Christus sic nobis vitæ suæ exemplo viam salutis ostendit, ut imitatione ejus vitam nostram componentes, ad salutem adspiremus, frustra nobis videri queat æternæ Salutis via o-stensa, stensa, cum nostra obedientia etiam cum ad summum gradum pervenit, lō-gissimè absit à perfectione Christi. Ipse Paulus, Philip. 3. v. 12, fatetur, se nondum metam apprehendisse, aut jam nondum perfectù esse: sed se experiendo persequi, an quoq; apprehendit, cujus etiàm rei causa apprehensus sit à Christo Jesu. Jac. 3. v. 2. In multis labimur omnes.
units.tr: II. If Christ thus showed the way of salvation to us by the example of his life, so that by shaping our life in imitation of him we aspire to salvation, the way of eternal salvation might seem to be shown to us in vain, since our obedience, even when it reaches the highest degree, is very far from the perfection of Christ. Paul himself, Phil. 3. v. 12, confesses that he had not yet laid hold of the goal, or was not yet already perfect; but he presses on, if indeed he may lay hold of that for which he was also laid hold of by Christ Jesus. James 3. v. 2: We all stumble in many things.

units.la: Etsi alioqui qualitates, Christi qualitatibus similes, in omnibus salvandis requirimus. Rom. 8. ver. 9. Quod si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, is non est ejus. Gal. 5. v. 24. Qui Christi sunt, carnem crucifixerunt, cum affectibus & concupiscentiis. Phil. 2. v. 5. Is sit affectus in vobis, qui fuit & in Christo Jesu. 1. Johan. 3. Quisquis habet hanc spem in eo sit tam, purificat se, sicut & ille purus est. Item, Quisquis in eo manet, non peccat: quisquis peccat, non vidit eum, neque novit eum. Mox plura.
units.tr: Yet otherwise we require qualities like Christ's qualities in all who are to be saved. Rom. 8. v. 9: But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his. Gal. 5. v. 24: Those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. Phil. 2. v. 5: Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus. 1 John 3: Everyone who has this hope in him purifies himself, just as he is pure. Likewise: Everyone who abides in him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen him nor known him. More follow shortly.

units.la: II. Christum etiam viam Salutis ac Doctrinam suam Miraculis multis cō-firmasse, nullus dubito. Siquidem ipse inquit, Johan. 5. ver. 36. Ego testimonium habeo, majus testimonio Joannis: Opera enim, quae dedit mihi Pater, ut ea perficerem, ipsa, in-quam, Opera, quae ego facio, testantur de me, quod Pater miserit me. Johan. 10. v. 37. Si non facio Opera Patris mei, noli mihi credere: Sin vero facio, etiamsi mihi non credatis, operibus credite, ut cognoscatis & credatis, Patrem in me esse, & me in eo. Joh. 10. v. 30[?]. Multa etiam alia signa edidit Iesus in discipulorum (quorum-[?] conspectu, quae non sunt scripta in hoc libro. Haec autem scripta sunt, ut credatis, Iesum esse Christum, Filium Dei, & ut credentes, vitam habeatis per nomen ejus.
units.tr: I do not doubt that Christ also confirmed the way of salvation and his teaching by many miracles. He himself says, John 5:36: "I have a witness greater than John's witness: for the works which the Father has given me to accomplish, the very works which I do, bear witness of me, that the Father has sent me." John 10:37: "If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me. But if I do them, even though you do not believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in me and I in him." John 20:30: "Jesus also did many other signs in the sight of his disciples, which are not written in this book. But these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life through his name."

units.la: Verum haec confirmatio non argu- it solida nostri Soterian: constat enim plurima a Prophetis & Apostolis Miracula ad doctrinae ipsorum confirmationem edita fuisse. Sic Moses Exod. 7. suorum dictorum Veritatem multis prodigiis & miraculis coram Pharaone confirmat. Sic Elias 1. Reg. 18. suam Doctrinam Miraculo insigni cum Prophetis Baalis spondet, & convictos jugulat. Sic Acta Apostolorum testantur de variis miraculis, quibus in Christi nomine editis Christi doctrinam asseruerunt. Cap. 3. v. 6. Petrus claudo dicit: Argentum & aurum non habeo: quod autem habeo, hoc tibi do: In nomine Iesu Christi Nazareni surge & ambula. Et prehensa manu ejus dextera, erexit eum, illico vero confirmati sunt pedes ejus ac malleoli. Cap. 5. verf. 12. Per manus Apostolorum edebantur signa & miracula multa in populo, adeo ut in plain plateas efferrent ægros, & ponerent in lectis ac grabbatis, ut venientis Petri vel umbra umbra-ret aliquem eorum.
units.tr: But this confirmation does not establish our salvation, for it is plain that the Prophets and Apostles also performed many miracles to confirm their teaching. Thus Moses, Exod. 7, confirmed the truth of his words before Pharaoh by many portents and miracles. Thus Elijah, 1 Kings 18, vouched for his teaching by a notable miracle against the prophets of Baal, and slew them when they were convicted. Thus the Acts of the Apostles bear witness to the various miracles by which they vindicated the teaching of Christ, performed in the name of Christ. Ch. 3, v. 6: Peter says to the lame man: "Silver and gold I do not have; but what I have, that I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk." And taking him by the right hand, he raised him up, and at once his feet and ankles were made strong. Ch. 5, v. 12: "By the hands of the Apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people, so that they carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, so that when Peter came by, at least his shadow might fall on one of them."

units.la: Verum hæc miracula quis enarrabit omnia? Neq; tamen hi Servatores generis humani sunt vocandi. Neq; obstat, quod à Christo miracula faciendi & doctrinam ipsius confirmandi potestatem acceperint, modò ipsi quoque Miraculis viam salutis, quam & Christus docuit & confirmavit, nobis hominibus confirmarint.
units.tr: But who could recount all these miracles? Yet these men are not to be called saviours of the human race. Nor does it stand in the way that they received from Christ the power of working miracles and of confirming his teaching, provided that they too, by their miracles, confirmed for us men the way of salvation which Christ also taught and confirmed.

units.la: III. FATEOR etiam, Christum sanguinem suum profundere voluisse, in hunc finem, ut obsignaret fœdus illud gratiæ, quod nomine Dei nobis annu-tiavit. Ideò enim in S. literis nomina-tur: Sanguis novi Fœderis seu Testamenti, ut patet Marc. 14. v. 24. Heb. 12. v. 24. & cap. 13. v. 20. Verum hic fructu[?] effusi sangui-nis nec solus est, nec præcipuus: Scio eum effusum esse in remissione peccatorum, & per eum sanguinem in cruce cum sensu iræ Dei effusum, tanquam per λύτρον & pretium redemtionis, factam esse nostri ex potestate Satanæ liberatione. In Christo enim habemus redemtionem per sanguinem ipsius, redemtionem scilicet peccatorum. 1. Timoth. 2. v. 6. Hic per proprium sangui-nem ingressus est semel in sacrarium æternam redemtionem nactus. Hebr. 9. Proinde dignus est, qui accipiat librum & aperiat sigilla ejus: quoniam macta-tus est, & redemit nos Deo per sanguinem suum. Apoc. 5. [?] v. 9. Deinde manifestum est, Sanctos Martyres suo etiam sanguine profuso veritatem cœlestem obsignasse, & hac ratione Ecclesiæ sa-lutem non parum promovisse, qui tamen hominum Servatores dici nō meruerunt. Sanctus Paulus 2. Corinth. 1. v. 5. 6. ait: Sicut abundant perpessiones Christi in nobis: Ita per Christum etiam abundat consolatio nostra: sive enim premimur, id fit pro vestra consolatione ac salute, qua efficitur in tolerantia earundem perpessionum, quibus & nos afficimur: sive consolationem accipimus, id fit pro vestra consolatione ac salute: & spes nostra firma est de vobis, quod sciamus vos, sicut socii estis perpessionum: Ita etiam socios fore consolationis. Coloss. 1. v. 14. Nunc gaudeo de iis quae patior pro vobis, & reliquias afflictionum Christi vicissim [?] expleo in carne mea pro corpore
units.tr: III. I grant also that Christ was willing to pour out his blood for this purpose, that he might seal that covenant of grace which he announced to us in the name of God. For this reason he is named in the Holy Scriptures: "the blood of the new covenant or testament," as is clear from Mark 14:24, Heb. 12:24 and ch. 13:20. But this fruit of the blood poured out is neither the only nor the chief one. I know that it was poured out for the forgiveness of sins, and that through that blood, shed on the cross with the sense of God's wrath, as a ransom [λύτρον] and price of redemption, our deliverance from the power of Satan was accomplished. For in Christ we have redemption through his blood, that is, the redemption of sins: 1 Tim. 2:6. He entered once for all into the sanctuary through his own blood, having obtained eternal redemption: Heb. 9. Therefore he is worthy to take the book and open its seals, for he was slain and has redeemed us to God by his blood: Rev. 5:9. Further, it is plain that the holy martyrs, by shedding their blood, also sealed the heavenly truth, and in this way promoted the salvation of the Church not a little; yet they have not deserved to be called saviours of men. Saint Paul, 2 Cor. 1:5-6, says: "As the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so also through Christ our consolation abounds. For whether we are afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effective in the endurance of the same sufferings which we also undergo; or whether we receive consolation, it is for your consolation and salvation; and our hope for you is firm, knowing that as you are partners in the sufferings, so you will also be partners in the consolation." Col. 1:24: "Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ for his body

units.la: ipsius, id est Ecclesia. 2. Timot. 2, v. 10. Omnia haec sustineo propter Electos, ut & ipsi salutem consequantur, quae est in Christo Iesu cum gloria aeterna.
units.tr: that is, the Church." 2 Tim. 2:10: "I endure all things for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory."

units.la: Etsi igitur sanguine Martyrum novum foedus ac aeternum non dicatur proprie stabiliri & confirmari. Etsi veritatis testimonium Martyres dederint; Etsi ideo passi sint, ut magis Deo quam hominibus obedirent, dicanturq; Christi Martyres: tamen expresse dicuntur premi aut pati pro Ecclesia, pro salute & consolatione piorum, nec propterea Servatores proprie dicuntur.
units.tr: Although, therefore, a new and eternal covenant is not properly said to be established and confirmed by the blood of the martyrs; although the martyrs gave testimony to the truth; although they suffered so that they might obey God rather than men, and are called martyrs of Christ: nevertheless they are expressly said to suffer or be afflicted for the Church, for the salvation and consolation of the godly; and yet they are not for that reason properly called saviours.

units.la: IV. Non diffiteor, Christū gloriosa Resurrectione & sui ipsius exaltatione nos regenerare in spem vitae aeternae, ut in Principem illum vitae perpetuo respicientes, in via salutis animose decurrendâ confirmemur. Sed cum Apostolo dico, 1. Pet. 1. Benedictus Deus, & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui secundum misericordiam suam magnam, regeneravit nos in spem vivam, per resurrectionem Iesu Christi ex mortuis, in hereditatem incorruptibilem, incontaminatam & immarcescibilem, conservatam in coelis, in vos, qui in virtute Dei custodimini per fidem in salutem, paratam revelari in tempore novissimo. Rom. 10.v.9. Quod si confessus su-eris ore Dominum Jesum, & crediderit in corde tuo, quod Deus eum excitavit a mortuis, serva-beris. Actor. 5. v.30. Deus Patrum nostrorum excitavit Jesum, quem vos interfecistis suspen-sum in ligno. Hunc Deus dextera sua evectum constituit Principem ac Salvatorem, ut det Resi-piscentiam Israeli & Remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: IV. I do not deny that Christ, by his glorious resurrection and his own exaltation, has begotten us again to a hope of eternal life, so that, looking always to him as the Prince of life, we may be strengthened to run the way of salvation with courage. But with the Apostle I say, 1 Pet. 1: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has begotten us again to a living hope, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled and unfading, reserved in heaven for you who by the power of God are kept through faith unto salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time." Rom. 10:9: "If you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved." Acts 5:30: "The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree. Him God has exalted at his right hand as Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins."

units.la: Non itaq; inficior, Christi Resurre-ctionem & Exaltationem magnæ esse efficacitatis, ad confirmanda ea omnia, quæ Christus nobis annunciavit, & ad salutis viam nobis manifeste ostende-dam. Fateor, hanc Christi glorifica-tionem, magnam esse fidei nostræ cau-sam, ut jam ex eo, quod Jesum Domi-num & Caput nostrum à Deo ex mor-tuis excitatum credimus, unde Deus nos quoque ex mortuis excitasse, & in cœlestibus unà cum Christo collocas-se, Ephes. 2. v. 6. à Paulo dictus est, opti-mam fidei nostræ in Deo collocandæ causam habeamus.
units.tr: Therefore I do not deny that the resurrection and exaltation of Christ are of great efficacy, both for confirming all those things which Christ announced to us and for showing us clearly the way of salvation. I grant that this glorification of Christ is a great ground of our faith; so that, since we believe that Jesus our Lord and Head was raised from the dead by God, whence God, as Paul says, Eph. 2:6, has also raised us up from the dead and made us sit together with Christ in the heavenly places, we have the best ground for placing our faith in God.

units.la: Didici per Resurrectionem Jesum Christum declaratū esse potenter Dei filium. Rom. 1. v. 4. ut qui Jesum
units.tr: Through the resurrection I have learned that Jesus Christ was declared mightily to be the Son of God, Rom. 1:4, so that whoever

units.la: Christum Filium Dei unigenitum ac dilectū excitatum, & omni in cœlo ac in terra potestate prædituм esse agnoscit, & omnia vera esse credit, quæ ille dixit, simul & salutis suæ Spem in declarato hoc Dei Filio Servatore suo, collocet, Vitam suam emendet, & cœlestem Beatitudinem adipiscatur.
units.tr: acknowledges that Christ, the only-begotten and beloved Son of God, has been raised up and is set over all power in heaven and on earth, and believes everything that he said to be true, and at the same time places the hope of his salvation in this Son of God declared as his Saviour, amends his life, and obtains heavenly blessedness.

units.la: Verum & hoc scio (quod hîc defi-dero) Christi etiam resurrectione probare peractæ redemtionis certitudine, adeoq; evidentissimè testatum facere, quod morte suâ omnia nostra peccata, quæ ut Sponsor in se susceperat, expiaverit, próq; illis judicio Dei satisfecerit. 1. Corinth. 15. verf. 17. Si Christus non est excitatus, inanis est fides vestra: adhuc estis in peccatis vestris. Ergo, quia Christus est excitatus, sequitur credentes non amplius esse in peccatis suis, nec fidem ipsorum inanem esse, nempe fidem, qua credunt, peccata sua per mortem Christi esse expiata.
units.tr: Yet I also know (and this is what I am missing here) that the resurrection of Christ also proves the certainty of the redemption accomplished, and most clearly testifies that by his death he expiated all our sins, which as our Surety he had taken upon himself, and satisfied the judgment of God for them. 1 Cor. 15:17: "If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins." Therefore, because Christ has been raised, it follows that believers are no longer in their sins, nor is their faith vain, namely the faith by which they believe that their sins have been expiated through the death of Christ.

units.la: Huc pertinet illud Roman. 4.v. ult. Christus traditus est ppter [?] lapsus nostros (scilicet expiandos suâ morte) & excitatus est propter justificationem nostri scilicet testificandam, quod nimirum illa facta sit per sanguinem ipsius, (vel, ut alii: Christus dicitur propter justificationē nostris excitatus & exaltatus, quia per Resurrectionem Christi Fides potissimū generatur, quæ deinde ad Justitiam nobis imputatur) Idē Apostolus, Act. 13. ubi cum ex Psal. 16. ostendisset, Jesum esse Christum, ut qui incorruptus excitatus sit à mortuis, subjungit v. 38. Notum ergo sit vobis, fratres, quod per hunc vobis remissio peccatorum annuntiatur. 1. Pet. 3. ver. 2. ait Petrus, quod baptisma nos servet, non quo carnis sordes abjiciuntur, sed quo fit, ut bona conscientia Deum interroget per Resurrectionem Jesu Christi.
units.tr: To this belongs the saying of Romans 4:25: Christ was delivered up for our trespasses (namely, to be expiated by his death) and was raised for our justification, that is, to be attested, namely that justification was made through his blood. (Or, as others read it: Christ is said to have been raised and exalted for our justification, because faith is chiefly generated through the resurrection of Christ, and this faith is then imputed to us for righteousness.) The same Apostle, in Acts 13, after showing from Psalm 16 that Jesus is the Christ, since he was raised incorruptible from the dead, adds in verse 38: Be it known to you therefore, brethren, that through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you. In 1 Peter 3, verse 2, Peter says: that baptism saves us, not because the filth of the flesh is put away, but because a good conscience appeals to God through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Explicatio.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: Hoc vult dicere, Credentes in Christum habere bonam conscientiam, quâ illa purgata est à peccatis (Heb. 9. v. 14.) hoc est, quatenus credentes sibi conscii sunt, quod habeant remissionem peccatorum per sanguinem Christi, in cruce oblati.
units.tr: His meaning is this: believers have a good conscience, by which it is cleansed from sins (Heb. 9:14), that is, insofar as believers are conscious to themselves that they have the forgiveness of sins through the blood of Christ, offered on the cross.

units.la: Talem autem conscientiam, quod habeant credentes, probat Petrus ex effectu, videlicet, quod Deum aussint interrogare, Quidnam? Nempe hoc ipsum, An non ita sit, ut credunt, nempe, quod Deus ipsis remiserit peccata propter oblationem Christi. Hoc autem ipsum ut confirment, proferunt loco infallibilis argumenti, Resurrectionem Christi Sponsoris, qui nimirum nisi peccata ipsorum sacrificio suo expiasset, resurgere a mortuis non potuisset.
units.tr: Peter proves that believers have such a conscience from its effect, namely that they dare to appeal to God. To what? Namely this very thing: whether it is not so, as they believe, that God has forgiven them their sins on account of the offering of Christ. To confirm this very thing, they put forward, as an infallible argument, the resurrection of Christ their Surety, who, unless he had expiated their sins by his sacrifice, could not have risen from the dead.

units.la: Sunt tamen, qui interrogationem hanc bonæ conscientiæ putant gigni in nobis per resurrectionem Christi, quatenus consideramus, hanc esse certissimam totius novi fœderis, quod Deus nobiscum pepigit per Christum, confirmationem: Nam qui credit, Jesum a mortuis excitatum, ac suprema potestate ac gloria donatum esse, non potest non eum pro Christo agnoscere: unde fit, ut Christo sub Spe promissæ salutis confidat atq; obtemperet, quæ jam est illa bonæ conscientiæ erga Deum stipulatio. Sed hæc explicatio non favet huic proposito.
units.tr: There are, however, some who think that this appeal of a good conscience is begotten in us through the resurrection of Christ, insofar as we consider it the most certain confirmation of the whole new covenant which God made with us through Christ. For whoever believes that Jesus has been raised from the dead and endowed with supreme power and glory cannot but acknowledge him as Christ; whence it follows that one trusts in Christ and obeys him in hope of the promised salvation, and this is now that pledge of a good conscience toward God. But this explanation does not favour the present thesis.

units.la: CAPITIS III. SECTIO III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III, SECTION III.

units.la: CHRISTUS EST SERVATOR CREDENTIUM PER PLENISSIMAM ACCEPTAM POTESTATEM DONATIONEM VITAE AC SALUTIS AETERNAE.
units.tr: CHRIST IS THE SAVIOUR OF BELIEVERS THROUGH THE FULLEST POWER ACCEPTED AND THE GIFT OF ETERNAL LIFE AND SALVATION.

units.la: Statuo, Jesum Christum Mediatorem nostrum plenissimam à Patre accepisse potestatem in coelo & in terra. Ipse n. excitatus ex morte, & jam coelum conscensurus dixit Matth. 28. Data est mihi omnis potestas in coelo & in terra. Ephes.1. v.20.21. &c. Efficacitate fortis roboris sui Deus exseruit in Christo, cum excitavit eum ex mortuis, & collocavit ad dextram suam in coelis, longe supra omne imperium ac potestatem, & potentiam, & dominium, et omne nomen, quod nominatur non solum in hoc seculo, verum etiam in futuro: & omnia subjecit ejus pedibus, cumq; constituit caput super omnia ipsi Ecclesiae, quae est corpus ipsius & complementum ejus, qui omnia implet in omnibus. Phil. 2. v.8. 9. &c. Ipse se submisit, factus obediens usq; ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Quapropter etiam Deus ipsum in summa exaltavit sublimitatem, ac donavit ei nomen, quod est supra omne nomen, ut ad nomen Jesu omne genu se flectat, coelestium, terrestrium & subterraneorum, omisq; omnisq; lingua confiteatur Dominum esse Iesum Christum ad gloriam Dei Patris. Joh. 5. v. 20. Pater diligit Filium, & omnia demonstrat ei, quæ ipse facit, & opera istis majora demonstrabit ei, ut vos miremini. Sicut enim Pater excitat mortuos & vivificat, ita et filius, quos vult vivificat. Neque enim Pater judicat quemquam, sed omne judicium dedit Filio, ut omnes honorent filium, prout honorant Patrem.
units.tr: I maintain that Jesus Christ our Mediator has received from the Father the fullest power in heaven and on earth. For he himself, raised from death and about to ascend into heaven, said (Matt. 28): All power is given to me in heaven and on earth. (Eph. 1:20–21, etc.): God put forth the working of his mighty strength in Christ, when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above all rule and authority and power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the age to come; and he put all things under his feet, and gave him as head over all things to the Church, which is his body and the fullness of him who fills all in all. (Phil. 2:8–9, etc.): He humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. Therefore God also highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, of things in heaven, on earth and under the earth, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. (John 5:20): The Father loves the Son and shows him all that he himself does, and he will show him greater works than these, so that you may marvel. For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wills. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honour the Son just as they honour the Father.

units.la: Quoniam igitur omnem Christus habet potestate in cœlo & in terra, utique potest etiam suis ovib' vitam æternam dare. Proinde agnosco hunc Regem, Dominū ac Servatorem meum, credentib, & obedientibus nobis in illo novissimo die donaturum esse vitam æternam, & abolita morte, omnibusq; hostibus sibi subjectis, nos ab omni miseria liberatos, in societatem cœlestis gloriæ adducturum.
units.tr: Since therefore Christ has all power in heaven and on earth, he can certainly also give eternal life to his sheep. Accordingly I acknowledge him as my King, Lord and Saviour, and I hold that he will give eternal life to us who believe and obey him on the last day, and that, death being abolished and all his enemies subjected to him, he will free us from every misery and bring us into the fellowship of heavenly glory.

units.la: Johan. 10. v. 27. &c. Oves mea, inquit Iesus Pastor ille bonus, vocem meam audiunt, & ego eas agnosco, & sequuntur me: & ego vitam æternam do eis, nec peribunt in æternum, neq; rapiet eas quisquam e manu mea, Pater meus, qui eas mihi dedit, major est omnibus, neque quisquam potest eas rapere e manu Patris mei. Ego et Pater unum sumus. Joh. 17. Pater, venit hora illa, glorifica Filium tuum, ut & Filius tuus te glorificet. Sic dedisti ei potestatem in omnem carnem, ut quotquot dedisti, dei eis vitam aeternam. 1.Corinth. 15.v.25. Nam oportet eum regnare, usque quo omnes inimicos subjecerit pedibus ejus. Vltimus autem hostis aboletur mors. Nam omnia subjecit sub pedes ejus. Quum autem dicit omnia esse subjecta, palam est hoc dici excepto eo, qui subjecit ei omnia. Phil. 3. v. 21. E coelis Servatorem expectamus Dominum Iesum Christum, qui transformabit corpus nostrum humile, ut conforme fiat corpori suo glorioso, pro efficacitate, qua potest etiam sibi subjicere omnia. Heb. 2. v. 8. Omnia subjecisti sub pedibus ejus. Enim vero per hoc, quod subjecit ei omnia, nihil omisit, quod non sit ei subjectum: at nunc nondum videmus ei omnia esse subjecta. Sed Iesum illum vernimus gloria & honore esse coronatum, qui paulisper fuit Angelis inferior factus, propter mortis perpessionem, ut beneficio Dei mortem pro omnibus gustaret.
units.tr: (John 10:27, etc.): My sheep, says Jesus, that good Shepherd, hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me; and I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand. My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch them out of my Father's hand. I and the Father are one. (John 17): Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, that the Son may glorify you. As you have given him authority over all flesh, so that to all whom you have given him he may give eternal life. (1 Cor. 15:25): For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy to be destroyed is death. For he has put all things under his feet. But when it says that all things are subjected, it is plain that this excludes him who subjected all things to him. (Phil. 3:21): We await from heaven a Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, by the power with which he is able to subject all things to himself. (Heb. 2:8): You have put all things under his feet. For in putting all things under him, he left nothing that is not subject to him; but at present we do not yet see all things subjected to him. But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honour because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.

units.la: Haec ita vera esse agnosco, sed nondum & hoc cum reliquis etiam conjunctum integrum illud Iesu Christi Servatoris officium exprimit.
units.tr: I acknowledge that these things are true, but they do not yet express the whole office of Jesus Christ the Saviour, which is joined with the rest.

units.la: 1. Etenim haec ipsa salvandi ratio, q; siue[?] donatione vitae aeternae, non est singularis & propria Mediatoris, distincta nimirum ab ea ratione, qua Deus Pater quoq; nos servat, qui etiam toties in V. T. dicitur Salvator seu Servator. Jesa. 12. Ecce Deus Salvator meus. 17. Oblitus es Dei Salvatoris tui. 43. Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus Sanctus Israelis, Salvator tuus. Oseę.13. v.4. Ego sum Jehovah Deus tuus, inde a terra Ægypti, & Deum praeter me non expertus es, ac Servator nullus est praeter me. Ipse etiam Deus Pater remittit peccata, & justificat, & dat vitam aeternam in Filio promissam.
units.tr: 1. For this very manner of saving, namely by the gift of eternal life, is not peculiar and proper to the Mediator, being distinct, of course, from that manner by which God the Father also saves us, who in the Old Testament is so often called Saviour. (Isa. 12): Behold, God is my Saviour. (17): You have forgotten God your Saviour. (43): I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Saviour. (Hos. 13:4): I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt, and you have known no God but me, and there is no saviour besides me. God the Father himself also forgives sins, justifies, and gives eternal life, which is promised in the Son.

units.la: 2. Mediatoris est non tantum conferre vel largiri salutem nomine alterius, verum etiam eam salutem impetrare, vel promereri, ut ita Servatorem Christum agnoscamus, quo Mediator existens inter Deum & nos, qui ab eo per peccata nostra disjuncti eramus, plene & perfectè, pro nobis moriens, & sic Dei justitiae pro nobis satisfaciens Deum nobis reconciliaverit. 1. Timoth. 2. v. 5. Unus enim est Deus, unus etiam Mediator Dei & Hominum, Homo Christus Jesus, qui seipsum dedit pretium redemtionis pro omnibus hominibus orandū. Ult enim Deus omnes servari, quia unus Deus omnium, quia unus Mediator pretium redemtionis seipsum dans pro omnibus. Mediatoris itaque ut nos omnes servet Mediando, est seipsum dare pretium redemptionis, seipsum in cruce pro nobis offerre, & sanguinem suum cum sensu irae Dei effundere.
units.tr: 2. It is the office of the Mediator not only to confer or bestow salvation in the name of another, but also to obtain or merit that salvation; so that we acknowledge Christ as Saviour in this sense: being the Mediator between God and us, we who were separated from him by our sins, he, dying for us fully and perfectly, and thus satisfying the justice of God on our behalf, has reconciled God to us. (1 Tim. 2:5): For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all men. For God wills that all be saved, since there is one God of all, and one mediator, giving himself as a ransom for all. Therefore, that he might save us all by mediating, it is necessary for him to give himself as the ransom, to offer himself for us on the cross, and to pour out his blood under the sense of God's wrath.

units.la: 3. Deniq; Christus non satis recte diceretur ista ratione jam nos servasse ac redemisse, vel in praesenti servare ac redimere: Sed potius olim servaturus ac redempturus: cum tamen de eo potissimum hic quaeratur, qua ratione Christus salutem aeternam jam nobis pepererit.
units.tr: 3. Finally, Christ could not rightly be said to have already saved and redeemed us in this way, or to save and redeem us in the present; rather he would save and redeem us in time to come. Yet it is chiefly of him that we are asking here, by what means Christ has already procured eternal salvation for us.

units.la: Sic Apostolus ait Actor. 20. verf. 28. Spiritus Sanctus vos constituit Episcopos ad pascendam Ecclesiam Dei, quam proprio illo SANGUINE ACQUISIVIT. 2. Timot. 1. v. 9. Qui servavit nos & vocavit vocatione sancta: non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito & gratia, quae data quidem est nobis in Christo Iesu ante tempora fecularia[?], sed patefacta nunc est per illustrem illum adventum Servatoris nostri IESU CHRISTI, qui & mortem abolevit, & vitam in lucem produxit, ac immortalitatem per Evangelium. 1. Pet. 1. verf. 18. Ut qui sciatis vos non caducis rebus, argento vel auro fuisse redemptos ex vana vestra conversatione ex Patrum traditionibus accepta: sed pretioso sanguianguine, utpote agni immaculati & incontaminati Christi.
units.tr: Thus the Apostle says (Acts 20:28): The Holy Spirit has made you overseers to feed the Church of God, which he acquired with his own blood. 2 Tim. 1:9: Who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before the ages of time, but has now been revealed through the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the Gospel. 1 Pet. 1:18: Knowing that you were redeemed from your empty way of life, inherited from your fathers, not with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish or spot.

units.la: Non igitur integra Servandi nos ratio consistit in eo, quod Christus Jesus veniens in mundum annuntiarit nobis salutis viam, eamq; in sua ipsius persona nobis ostenderit, sanctè scilicet Vivendo, Patiendo, Moriendo, & ex mortuis Resurgendo; quodq; olim in novissimo ille die sit venturus judicatum hominibus & credentibus sibiq; obedientibus datum vitam æternam: Proin-de hæc servandi ratio Christi MERITO ET SATISFACTIONE truncata, rectè insufficiens esse concluditur.
units.tr: Therefore the whole manner of our salvation does not consist in this, that Jesus Christ, coming into the world, announced to us the way of salvation and showed it to us in his own person, namely by living, suffering and dying holily, and rising from the dead; and that in the last day he will come to judge mankind and give eternal life to those who believe and obey him. Hence it is concluded that this manner of saving, stripped of the merit and satisfaction of Christ, is rightly held to be insufficient.

units.la: CAPUT IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: ASSERTIO ET DEMON-stratio Meriti & Satisfactionis Servatoris Christi, ex eo, quod ipse Mediator, Reconciliator et Redem-tor noster fit.
units.tr: The assertion and demonstration of the merit and satisfaction of the Saviour Christ, from the fact that he himself becomes our Mediator, Reconciler and Redeemer.

units.la: Q[?]uamobrē cum Catholica Christianorū orthodoxorū Ecclesia assero, arcteq; te-neo, integrā & primariam propripropriamque Servandi rationem, qua JesusChristus noster Servator Salutem aeterna nobis acquisierit, esse ejus SATISFACTIONEM ET MERITUM, adeoq; statuo & confido Christum, ut sanctum Pontificem & sanctam victimam, sua passione & morte pro nostris peccatis justo Dei judicio satisfecisse, & poenas nobis ob peccata debitas in se ut SPONSOREM nostrum derivasse, adeoq; amissam Dei Gratiam & Vitae Aeternae praemium nobis esse promeritum. Quod ut sic statuam his S. literarum testimoniis, indeq; deductis argumentis convincor & impellor.
units.tr: Therefore, with the Catholic Church of orthodox Christians, I maintain and firmly hold that the whole and primary, proper and peculiar way of salvation, by which Jesus Christ our Saviour has obtained eternal salvation for us, is his SATISFACTION and his MERIT. Accordingly I affirm and am confident that Christ, as the holy High Priest and holy Victim, satisfied the just judgment of God by his suffering and death for our sins, and as our SURETY took upon himself the punishments due to us for sins; and so the forfeited grace of God and the reward of eternal life have been merited for us. That I hold this view I am convinced and driven by these testimonies of Holy Scripture, and by the arguments drawn from them.

units.la: CAPITIS IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: SECTIO I.
units.tr: SECTION I.

units.la: Vi ejusmodi Mediator & Pacificator est Dei & Hominum, ut dissidentes partes (Deum dico & Homines) utrinq; in novum amicitiae foedus vere restituit, & non minus Dei, quam nostri respectu aeternum foedus gratia sua morte sancivit, & redemtionis pretium pro nobis se dedit, ita ut nos de placata Dei ira certo persuasi audeamus andeamus[?] ad Deum accedere cum fiducia : &[?] nobis & nostra parte satisfaciendo vitam & iustitiam promeruisse nobis merito dici potest. Expendantur omnes antecedetis, seu de-scriptionis partes, & consequens de illo antecedente rectèdici minime nega-bitur.
units.tr: By this power the Mediator and Pacificator of God and men truly restores the disagreeing parties (I mean God and men) to a new friendship on both sides. By his death he ratified an eternal covenant of grace, no less with respect to God than to us, and he gave himself as the price of redemption for us. So, being certainly persuaded that God's wrath is appeased, we may dare to approach God with confidence. And since he has satisfied on his own part and ours, it can rightly be said that he has merited life and righteousness for us. Let all the parts of the antecedent, or description, be weighed, and the consequent will by no means be denied to follow rightly from that antecedent.

units.la: Atqui Iesu Christus ejusmodi est Mediator ac Pacificator Dei & hominum. Non enim eo tantum modo dicitur & est MEDIATOR, quo Deus, ut internun-tio & interprete, ad foedera sua cum hominibus sancienda & pangenda u-titur, & per quem illi ad ipsum, ejus voluntatis cognitione instructi, accedere possint: Sicut Moses dicitur Mediator Deut. 5. v. 5. Gal. 3. v. 19. quod fuerit internuntius divinae voluntatis. Proprium enim ejus (dico Moses) officium non quidem Deum hominibus placandi fuit, sed ejus nomine cum populo Israelitico vetus illud foedus fan-ciendi, atq; is fuit, per quem populus ille quotidie divinae voluntatis admo-nebatur, & ad Deum accedere ea ratio-ne poterat. Non, inquam, eo tantum modo Christus Mediator est. {1}i.[?] Sed ideo cumprimis, quod dissidentes inter se partes utrinq; in novum amicitiae foedus vere restituit, & non minus Dei, quam nostri respectu aeternum foedus gratiae sua morte sancivit. Hoc ita probo: Hebræor. 8.v. 6. At nunc eo excellentius ministerium nactus est, quo praestantioris est foederis MEDIATOR, quod praestantioribus promissis sancitum est. Ecce Christus est Mediator ac Intercessor praestantioris foederis, nempe Gratiae seu Evangelii, quod sancitum dicitur praestantioribus promissis (ut statim ex Jeremia explicatur) nempe Remissione peccatorum gratuita propter satisfactionem Christi.
units.tr: But Jesus Christ is such a Mediator and Pacificator of God and men. For he is not called and is a MEDIATOR only in the way that God uses someone as go-between and interpreter to make and establish his covenants with men, and through whom they can come to him, instructed in knowledge of his will. So Moses is called Mediator, Deut. 5. v. 5; Gal. 3. v. 19, because he was the messenger of the divine will. For the proper office of that man (I mean Moses) was not to appease God for the people, but to establish in God's name that old covenant with the Israelite people. He was the one through whom that people was admonished daily of the divine will, and in this way they could approach God. Christ is not Mediator, I say, only in this way. Rather, chiefly, he is Mediator because he truly restores the disagreeing parties to a new friendship on both sides, and by his death he ratified an eternal covenant of grace, no less with respect to God than to us. I prove it thus: Hebr. 8. v. 6. But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is the MEDIATOR of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. Behold, Christ is the Mediator and Intercessor of a better covenant, namely of grace or of the Gospel, which is said to be established upon better promises (as is explained at once from Jeremiah), namely the free forgiveness of sins on account of Christ's satisfaction.

units.la: Deinde donatione Spiritus Sancti, qui primum illuminat mentes nostras cognitione gratiae Dei per satisfactionem CHRISTI acquisitae; deinde vero renovat voluntatem ad studium gratitudinis pro beneficio liberationis ac redemtionis per CHRISTUM.
units.tr: Then, by the donation of the Holy Spirit, who first enlightens our minds with the knowledge of God's grace acquired through Christ's satisfaction, and then renews the will to a zeal of gratitude for the benefit of liberation and redemption through CHRIST.

units.la: Est itaque Mediator foederis gratiæ, sed quomodo? Audi ex Cap. 9. v. 15. Obid novi Testamenti Mediator est, ut Mor-te intercedente ad Redem-tionem earum prævaricationum, quæ fuerant sub priore testamento, qui vocati erant, promissam æternam hereditatem acciperent.
units.tr: Therefore he is the Mediator of the covenant of grace, but how? Hear Heb. 9. v. 15: "And for this cause he is the Mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance."

units.la: Nam ubi testamentum est, Mors intercedat necesse est Testatoris. Hic postquā Apostolus affirmaverat, Christum oblatione sui ipsius, hoc est, sua morte acquisivisse remissionem peccatorum & vitam æternam; jam causas exponit cur ita fieri oportuerit. Una est, quod hoc modo necesse erat ratum fieri testamentum Dei, cujus Mediator ipse fuerit constitutus. Audio igitur hic, oportuisse intercedere Mortem Christi, ut hæreditatem illam æternam nobis promissam acciperemus.
units.tr: For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. Here, after the Apostle has affirmed that Christ, by the offering of himself, that is, by his death, obtained remission of sins and eternal life, he now sets out the reasons why it had to happen in this way. One reason is that in this way it was necessary for the testament of God, of which he was appointed Mediator, to be ratified. I hear, therefore, that the death of Christ had to intervene so that we might receive that eternal inheritance promised to us.

units.la: Christus itaque ut mediator sua morte nobis acquisivit, & Redemtionem, id est, remissionem transgressionum, & Vitam æternam, Heb. 12. v. 24. Mediator foederis novi conjungitur cum Sanguine aspersionis. Descriptioni n. Ecclesiæ clesiæ Novi Testamenti annectit commemorationem beneficii per Christū præstiti nobis, nimirum reconciliationis Dei per sanguine ipsius, quem Sanguinis Christi effectum illustrat oppositione Sanguinis Abel, qui sanguis a Caino effusus Vindicta Dei adversus illum postulabat, cum sanguis Christi pro nobis postulet Veniam & Gratiam.
units.tr: Christ, then, as Mediator, by his death obtained for us both redemption, that is, the remission of transgressions, and eternal life. Heb. 12. v. 24: "And to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel." The Apostle joins to the description of the Church of the New Testament a reminder of the benefit bestowed on us through Christ, namely the reconciliation of God through his blood. He illustrates the effect of the blood of Christ by contrast with the blood of Abel, which, shed by Cain, called for the vengeance of God against him, whereas the blood of Christ, shed for us, pleads for pardon and grace.

units.la: 2. Deinde ejusmodi est Mediator Christus, qui redemtionis pretium pro nobis sese dedit. 1. Timoth. 2. v. 5. & 6. Unus enim Deus, unus etiam Mediator Dei & hominum Homo Iesus Christus, qui seipse dedit redemptionis pretium pro omnibus. Syrus sic habet: Unus enim Deus, & unus Mediator Dei & filiorum hominis, Filius hominis Iesus Christus, qui dedit semetipsum redemtionem pro omni homine.
units.tr: 2. Next, Christ is such a Mediator that he gave himself as the price of redemption for us. 1 Tim. 2. v. 5 and 6: "For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom for all." The Syriac reads thus: "For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and the sons of men, the Son of man, Jesus Christ, who gave himself as redemption for every man."

units.la: Ecce hic audis, cur Homo Iesus Christus sit Mediator; quia semetipsum dedit redemtionem pro nobis. Licet vero hic probare velit Apostolus suam quæstionem pro omnibus orandum esse, & Deum velle omnes servari, quia Christus pro omnibus hominibus vitam suam impederit
units.tr: Here you hear why the man Jesus Christ is the Mediator: because he gave himself as redemption for us. Although the Apostle here wishes to prove his point, that prayer must be made for all and that God wills all to be saved, because Christ gave his life for all men, he at the same time sets out the reason for the mediation of Christ between God and men, namely that he gave himself as the price of redemption for all. The same argument confirms that, and this declares it.

units.la: {*} Dedit se ipsum pro nobis redemtionis pretium. Probatur hoc. derit: simul tamen exponit rationem Mediationis Christi inter Deum & homines, quia nimirum semetipsum dederit pretium redemtionis pro omnibus. Idem argumentum illud confirmat, hoc vero declarat.
units.tr: {*} He gave himself as the price of redemption for us. This is proved. [The text is damaged here:] he gave... Yet at the same time he sets out the reason for the mediation of Christ between God and men, because he gave himself as the price of redemption for all. The same argument confirms that point, and this declares it.

units.la: Et licet antea nihil dictum sit de ira Dei adversus hominū scelera, sed contra de Dei bonitate & clementia, qua genus humanū fuerat complex; nihil tamē vetat, quo min hic ratio Mediationis & pacificationis Jesu Christi declaretur; siquidē & donatio filii & missio ad Mediatoris officium; ipsaq; officii executio per λύτρα persolutionem facta commēdat Patris erga nos Bonitatem & Dilectionem. Commendat enim suam caritatem erga nos Deus, quod cum adhuc essemus peccatores, Christus pro nobis mortuus sit. Rom. 5. v. 8.
units.tr: And although nothing had been said earlier about the wrath of God against the sins of men, but rather about the goodness and mercy of God, by which he had embraced the human race, nothing prevents the reason for the mediation and reconciliation of Jesus Christ from being declared here. For both the gift of the Son, his sending to the office of Mediator, and the carrying out of that office by the payment of a ransom [λύτρα] commend the goodness and love of the Father towards us. For God commends his love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Rom. 5. v. 8.

units.la: 3. Deniq; ejusmodi Mediator est, ut per eum nos de placata Dei ira certo persuasi, audeamus ad Deum accedere cum fiducia. Hebr. 4. v. 16, Habentes igitur Pontificem magnū, &c. accedamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ, ut consequamur misericordiam,
units.tr: 3. Finally, such is the Mediator that, being certain through him that God's anger has been appeased, we may dare to approach God with confidence. Heb. 4. v. 16: "Seeing then that we have a great high priest, let us come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need."

units.la: * Complex: Per Christum nos de placata Dei ira persuasi ad Deum accedere cum fiducia audemus. sericordiam, & gratiam inveniamus ad opportunum auxilium. Nisi n, [?] hujus mediatoris nostri merito & intercessione niteremur, in conspectum Dei prodire non auderemus, quippe peccatores & inimici Dei (Rom.5.10.) cujus iram a nobis ablatā esse non possimus credere, priusquā intelligamus Christi sanguine ipsum placatū esse, tanquam hostia bonae fragrantiae, Eph. 5. 2. Christus dilexit nos, & tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem ac victimam Deo, in odorem bonae fragrantiae.
units.tr: * Summary: Through Christ, persuaded that God's anger has been appeased, we dare to draw near to God with confidence, that we may find mercy and grace for timely help. Unless we relied on the merit and intercession of this our Mediator, we would not dare to come before the presence of God, since we are sinners and enemies of God (Rom. 5. 10). We cannot believe that his anger has been taken away from us until we understand that he has been appeased by the blood of Christ, as a sacrifice of sweet fragrance. Eph. 5. 2: "Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour."

units.la: Ubi nota. 1. Caritate Dei & Christi præ-cipuè in morte Christi declarata fuisse, quum & Deus Pater unigenitum Filium suum pro nobis in morte [?] tradere, & Filius hanc ipsam execrabilem crucis mortem pro nobis obire non dubitavit, idque eo fine, ut per mortem Filii Deo Patri reconciliaremur, qui alioquin perditi eramus.
units.tr: Note here: 1. The love of God and of Christ was especially declared in the death of Christ, since God the Father did not hesitate to deliver his only begotten Son for us to death, and the Son did not hesitate to undergo for us this very detestable death on the cross, and this for the purpose that through the death of the Son we might be reconciled to God the Father, we who otherwise were lost.

units.la: 2. MORTEM CHRISTI, quam nostri amore pro nobis obiit, sacrificium fuisse Deo gratissimum, & suaviter coram ipso fragrans:per quam & credentes in ipsum Deo Patri sunt accepti.
units.tr: 2. The death of Christ, which he underwent for us out of love for us, was a sacrifice most acceptable to God and sweetly fragrant before him, through which believers in him are also accepted by God the Father.

units.la: Christum itaque ut Mediatorem nostrum, justitiæ divinæ pro peccatis nostris satisfecisse, & iram Dei nobis placasse, adhuc credimus.
units.tr: Therefore we still believe that Christ, as our Mediator, satisfied divine justice for our sins and appeased the wrath of God toward us.

units.la: CAPITIS IV. SECTIO II.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV, SECTION II.

units.la: QVi ejusmodi Reconciliator noster est, ut per eum simus Deo reconciliati, seu ut per eum Deus ipse nos sibi reconciliarit eatenus, quatenus Deus ipsum constituit placamentum per fidem in sanguine ejus, ut ita per quandam compensationis viam sublata sit inimicitia inter Deum & nos, & pacem jam erga Deum consequamur per fidem in eum, quem ideo Deus fecit pro nobis peccatum, ut per sanguinem crucis ejus nos sibi reconciliaret: is certè pro nobis satisfecisse & reconciliationem nostri apud Deum impetrasse & promeruisse jure dici potest.
units.tr: He who is our Reconciler in such a way that through him we are reconciled to God, or that God himself reconciles us to himself through him, to the extent that God has set him forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood, so that by a certain way of compensation enmity between God and us is removed, and we now obtain peace with God through faith in him, whom God therefore made sin for us, so that through the blood of his cross he might reconcile us to himself: he can rightly be said to have made satisfaction for us and to have obtained and merited our reconciliation with God.

units.la: Atqui Jesus Christus ejusmodi est Reconciliator, ut per eum, simus & dicamur Deo reconciliati, seu ut per eum Deus ipse nos sibi reconciliarit eatenus, quatenus Deus ipsum constituit placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius, ut ita per quandam compensationis viam sublata sit inimiinimicitia inter Deum & nos, & pacem jam erga Deum per fidem in ipsum, quae ideo Deus ipse pro nobis fecit peccatum, ut per sanguinem crucis ejus nos sibi reconciliaret.
units.tr: But Jesus Christ is such a Reconciler that through him we are and are called reconciled to God, or that God himself reconciles us to himself through him, to the extent that God has set him forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood, so that by a certain way of compensation enmity between God and us is removed, and we now have peace with God through faith in him, whom God himself therefore made sin for us, so that through the blood of his cross he might reconcile us to himself.

units.la: QUOD JAM PROBANDUM EST.
units.tr: WHAT IS NOW TO BE PROVED.

units.la: Per Christum nos reconciliatos esse Deo, dicit Apostolus ad Rom. 5. v. 10. Ubi Reconciliatio non tantum nos respicit, quasi Reconciliare, tantū sit, cordis nostri duritiem emollire, & nos amicos Dei facere, & Reconciliari tantum sit, ad Deum converti, & amicos Dei evadere: Sed primo ipsum quoq; respicit Deum, Deo enim Reconciliari dicimur, ut & amici Deo fieri intelligamur: & quidem, DEO RECONCILIARI dicimur per MORTEM FILII, & per eum assequi reconciliationem, ut sit sensus hic:
units.tr: The Apostle says that we are reconciled to God through Christ (Rom. 5:10). Here the reconciliation does not concern us alone, as though to reconcile meant only to soften the hardness of our heart and make us friends of God, and to be reconciled meant only to be converted to God and become his friends. It looks first to God himself, for we are said to be reconciled to God, so that we are understood also to become friends to God. And indeed we are said to be RECONCILED TO GOD through the DEATH OF THE SON, and to obtain reconciliation through him, so that the sense is this:

units.la: Cum Deus adeo nos dilexerit, ut pro nobis adhuc peccatoribus filium suum unigenitum mori voluerit, ut scilicet per mortem ejus Deo reconciliaremur: dubitandum non est, quin nos multo magis servaturus sit per Filium suum in coelesti gloria viventem, postquam justificati & ad eum jam conversi sumus. Sic habet textus: Nam si cum inimici essemus, reconciliati fuimus Deo per mortem Filii ejus, multo magis reconci-liati liati servabimur per vitam ipsius, hoc est, si e-nim cum ipsius inimici essemus adeo nos dilexit, ut Filium suum pro nobis in mortem daret, et nos ISTA RATIONE SIBI reconciliare voluerit; multo magis postquam ipsi reconciliati sumus per eundem filium suum in coelesti gloria viventem ab aeterna morte nos servabit.
units.tr: Since God loved us so much that, while we were still sinners, he willed his only-begotten Son to die for us, namely so that we might be reconciled to God through his death, there is no doubt that he will keep us much more through his Son, who lives in heavenly glory, now that we have been justified and have already been converted to him. So the text reads: For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life (Rom. 5:10). That is, if, while we were his enemies, he loved us so much that he gave his Son to death for us, and willed to reconcile us to himself in this way, much more, now that we have been reconciled to him through the same Son, who lives in heavenly glory, will he save us from eternal death.

units.la: Hic certè actualis illa reconciliatio nostri facta per nostri justificationem & conversionem, non excludit, sed includit seu præsupponit reconciliationem Dei nobiscum factam per mortem & sanguinē crucis Christi. Deinde Mortis & Vitæ Christi mentionem eo trahi non debere concedo, quasi illa minus, hæc magis efficax sit ad nos servandū, sed hoc tantum dici, justificatos per Christum viventem eo magis iri servatum, quia jam non necesse sit Christū amplius IPSORUM CAUSA MORI.
units.tr: Here, certainly, that actual reconciliation of ours, effected through our justification and conversion, does not exclude but includes, or presupposes, the reconciliation of God with us made through the death and blood of Christ's cross. Next, I grant that the mention of Christ's death and life should not be taken as though the one were less effective and the other more effective in saving us; rather it is said only that those justified through the living Christ will be saved all the more, because it is no longer necessary for Christ to die FOR THEIR SAKE again.

units.la: 2. Deum nos sibi per Christum recō- ciliasse legimus. 2. Corin. 5. Omnia haec, inquit Apostolus, pendent ab auctore Deo, qui per Iesum Christum omnia instauravit, nosque fideles per illius ministerium sibi reconciliavit: denique[?] nobis Apostolis huius reconciliationis administrationem commisit. Equidem ipse Deum in Christo Mediatore praesentem sese exhibebat, & mundum, quantum in se erat. Opera Christi Filii sibi reconciliabat, non imputando iis peccata ipsorum, sed gratis condonando. Atque huius reconciliationis sermonem sive annuntiationem nobis verbi ministris concredidit.
units.tr: 2. We read that God reconciled us to himself through Christ (2 Cor. 5). All these things, says the Apostle, depend on God the author, who through Jesus Christ restored all things and reconciled us faithful to himself through his ministry; and finally he committed to us apostles the administration of this reconciliation. Indeed God himself was present, showing himself in Christ the Mediator, and reconciling the world to himself, as far as lay in him. He reconciled himself to the works of Christ his Son, not imputing to men their sins, but forgiving them freely. And he entrusted to us, the ministers of the Word, the message or proclamation of this reconciliation.

units.la: Quemadmodum igitur Patris sui legatum egit Christus: ita nos pro Christo legatione obimus: et proinde velut ipso Deo per nos adhortante, idque nomine Christi, vos unicè rogamus, ut relictis peccatis Deo reconciliari velitis. Etenim ad hanc conditionem prastandam ipsius Dei & CHRISTI erga nos caritas excitare nos debet. Quandoquidem Deus ipsum Christum, licet innocentissimum & omnis peccati expertem, nostra causa, tanquam facinorosum peccatorem tractavit, & veluti peculiarem hostiam pro nobis maclari & mori voluit, ut nos ista ratione ex peccatis emergentes & Christo per veram fidem insiti, justi coram Deo haberemur.
units.tr: Just as Christ acted as the envoy of his Father, so we also serve as ambassadors for Christ; and therefore, as though God himself were exhorting you through us, and that in the name of Christ, we earnestly beg you to lay aside your sins and be willing to be reconciled to God. For the love of God and of Christ toward us ought to stir us to fulfil this condition. Since God treated Christ himself, though most innocent and free from all sin, for our sake as though he were a wicked sinner, and willed him to be slaughtered and to die for us as a special sacrifice, so that we, rising out of our sins in this way and grafted into Christ by true faith, might be held righteous before God.

units.la: Hic jam figere pedem paulisper mihi fas sit, ut ex hoc loco veram Reconciliationis doctrinam enucleem.
units.tr: Here it is permitted me to linger a little, so that I may bring out the true doctrine of reconciliation from this passage.

units.la: I. Principalis efficiens Reconciliationis nostri Deus ipse, qui pro sua Misericordia, licet à genere humano offensus, tamen hanc Reconciliationem ultro procurat, & per Christum, pérque CHRISTI ministros non modo veniam peccatoribus nobis offert, sed etiam ad præstandam fidei conditio-nem nos hortatur, imo ut eam præste-mus efficit. DEUS erat in CHRISTO reconcilians[?].
units.tr: I. The principal efficient cause of our reconciliation is God himself, who, out of his mercy, though offended by the human race, nevertheless freely procures this reconciliation, and through Christ, and through the ministers of Christ, not only offers pardon to sinners, but also exhorts us to fulfil the condition of faith, indeed brings it about that we fulfil it. God was in Christ reconciling the world.

units.la: 2. Altera efficiens est JESUS CHRI-STUS, quatenus Mediator DEI & Hominum, per quem DEUS Pater hanc Reconciliationem apparavit, quatenus eum licet innocentissimum, non secus ac facinorosum aliquem peccatorem pro nobis in Mortem crucis tradidit, ut nos ista ratione per fidem in Christum justi coram DEO ipso efficeremur. Eum enim qui non noverat peccatum, pro nobis fecit peccatum, ut nos efficeremur Justitia Dei in illo. CHRISTUS itaque Me-ritoria manet causa hujus reconcilia-tionis.
units.tr: 2. The second efficient cause is JESUS CHRIST, as Mediator between God and men, through whom God the Father prepared this reconciliation, in that he delivered him, though most innocent, to the death of the cross for us, just as though he were some wicked sinner, so that in this way we might be made righteous before God himself through faith in Christ. For he who knew no sin he made to be sin for us, so that we might become the righteousness of God in him. Christ therefore remains the meritorious cause of this reconciliation.

units.la: 3. Tertio utitur DEUS Opera mini-strorum Verbi, tanquam CHRISTI legatorum, qui nomine Dei & CHRISTI gratiam istam nobis annuntiant, nosq; ad conditionem prædi&a libenter præstandam cohortantur, atq; ita demum per clavium spiritualium potestatem nos à peccatis absolvant. Itaq; inquit Paulus, nomine CHRISTI legatione fungimur, velut DEO vos precamur per nos, oramus CHRISTI nomine: Reconciliamini Deo.
units.tr: 3. Third, God uses the work of the ministers of the Word, as the envoys of Christ, who in the name of God and Christ announce this grace to us, and urge us to fulfil the aforesaid condition willingly, and so at last, through the power of the spiritual keys, absolve us from sins. Therefore, says Paul, we act as ambassadors in the name of Christ; as though God were beseeching you through us, we pray in Christ's name: Be reconciled to God.

units.la: 4. Ultimo loco consequitur ipsa Fi-DES, qua oblatum illud reconciliationis beneficium consequimur, per quam solam Christo inserimur, atque ita in ipso justi censemur.
units.tr: 4. Last in order comes FAITH itself, by which we obtain that offered benefit of reconciliation, and through which alone we are grafted into Christ and so are counted righteous in him.

units.la: 5. Forma hujus Reconciliationis exprimitur per NON-IMPUTATIONEM PECCATORUM, cum dicit: Reconcili-ans sibi non imputando eis peccata ipsorum.
units.tr: 5. The form of this reconciliation is expressed by the NON-IMPUTATION OF SINS, when it says: reconciling them to himself, not imputing their sins to them.

units.la: 6. Subjectum Reconciliationis nostris recipiens, si Dei oblationem spectamus, est universus Mundus, sive totum genus humanum. Deus erat in Christo Mundum sibi reconcilians: si vero ad eventum & actualem reconciliationem nostri spectamus, sola est credentium Multitudo, quæ reipsa hujus beneficii fit particeps. Cum enim sub conditione fidei hæc reconciliatio toti mundo offeratur, certe qui conditionem illam recusant, sua ipsorū culpa, tanto beneficio sese privant. Sed hæc per occasionem declarandi gratia copiosius.
units.tr: 6. The subject receiving reconciliation, if we look at God's offer, is the whole world, or the entire human race. God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself. But if we look at the outcome and actual reconciliation of ourselves, it is the multitude of believers alone who in fact become partakers of this benefit. For since this reconciliation is offered to the whole world under the condition of faith, certainly those who refuse that condition deprive themselves of so great a benefit through their own fault. But these matters will be declared more fully as occasion arises.

units.la: 3. Pergamus: Per Christum Deo re-conciliati sumus, quatenus Deus ipsum constituit placamentum per fidem in sanguine ejus, Rom. 3. v.25. Justificantur autem gratis, id est, ejus gratia, per redemptionem factam in Christo Jesu: quem proposuit Deus, ut esset placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius ad declarandam justitiam suam per remissionem praecedentium peccatorum. Hoc est, Justificantur gratis, quotquot justificantur, nempe ex pura Dei misericordia & gratia, quatenus ab omni peccato liberantur, ea liberatione, quæ nobis in Christo Jesu exhibita est: quippe quem Deus Pater nobis proposuit expiatorem seu propitiatorem peccatorum, vera animi fiducia amplectendum, interveniente fusione sanguinis ipsius, nempe ut hac ratione æquitatem seu justitiam suam omnibus demonstraret, eo quod peccata jam ante commissa gratiose nobis condonavit.
units.tr: 3. Let us go on: through Christ we are reconciled to God, in that God set him forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood (Rom. 3:25). They are justified freely, that is, by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness through the remission of sins previously committed. That is: They are justified freely, all who are justified, namely out of pure mercy and grace of God, in that they are freed from all sin by that deliverance which is offered to us in Christ Jesus, since God the Father set him forth to us as the expiator or propitiator of sins, to be embraced with a true trust of the heart, through the shedding of his blood, namely so that in this way he might show his equity or righteousness to all, in that he has graciously forgiven us the sins committed before.

units.la: 4. Ita per quandam compensationis viam sublata est inimicitia inter Deum & nos, Ephes. 2. v. 16. Pacem faciens, utrósque in uno corpore reconciliavit Deo per Crucem, peremtis inimicitiis per eam. Sustulit enim Christus autor pacis nostræ insignem illud inimicitiæ, nempe legem ceremonialem in variis placitis sive constitutionibus sitam, per sui corporis sacrificium, ut in sese ex duobus populis unum novum hominem conderet, & pacem inter utrosq; constitueret; ambos illos velut in unum opus coactos inter se invicem reconciliaret, IDQUE PER CRUCEM SEU MORTEM CRUCIS, UTROSQUE DEO RECONCILIANDO, PEREMTIS INIMICITIIS IN IPSA MORTE CRUCIS, Deo dico, quia sciendum, reconciliationem generis humani per Christum factam tripliciter in S. literis declarari: 1. Quatenus immediatè Deum respicit. 2. Quatenus per eum homines & Angeli velut in unam concordiam redacti sunt. 3. Quatenus per eandem simul Judæi & Gentes in unum Ecclesiæ corpus coaluerunt.
units.tr: 4. In this way, by a certain course of compensation, the enmity between God and us was removed, Ephesians 2:16: "Making peace, he reconciled both in one body to God through the cross, having slain the enmity by it." For Christ, the author of our peace, took away that notable enmity, namely the ceremonial law, which consisted in various decrees or ordinances, through the sacrifice of his body, so that in himself he might make of the two peoples one new man and establish peace between both; he reconciled both, as if gathered into one work, to each other; AND THIS THROUGH THE CROSS OR THE DEATH OF THE CROSS, RECONCILING BOTH TO GOD, HAVING SLAIN THE ENMITIES IN THE VERY DEATH OF THE CROSS. To God, I say; for it should be known that the reconciliation of the human race made through Christ is declared in Holy Scripture in three ways: (1) insofar as it looks immediately to God; (2) insofar as through him men and angels have been brought, as it were, into one harmony; (3) insofar as through the same Jews and Gentiles have grown together into one body of the Church.

units.la: Coloss. 1. 20. Et pacem per sanguinem crucis ejus facta placuit Patri per eum reconciliare sibi omnia, tum quae in terra, tum quae in coelis. Itaque vos quondam abalienatos & hostes, mente operibus malis intenta, nunc sane reconciliavit, in corpore illo carnis suae per mortem, &c. hoc est, Quandoquidem Deo Patri visum est per illum Filium suum, totam creaturarum universitatem inhabitare, ac plenitudinem omnium suorum in illo residere: Itaque placuit eidem Patri per sanguinem CHRISTI in cruce effusum, universalem pacem, inter Angelos & Homines sancire, & utrosque inter se reconciliare, hoc est, tum eos, qui in terra, tum eos qui in coelis sunt, ad suam ipsius gloriam.
units.tr: Colossians 1:20: "And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, it pleased the Father through him to reconcile all things to himself, whether things on earth or things in heaven. And you, who were once estranged and enemies in mind, intent on evil works, he has now indeed reconciled in that body of his flesh through death, etc." That is: Since it has seemed good to God the Father to dwell through that his Son in the whole universe of creatures, and to have the fullness of all his things abide in him, it has therefore pleased the same Father, through the blood of Christ poured out on the cross, to ratify a universal peace between angels and men and to reconcile both to each other; that is, both those who are on earth and those who are in heaven, to his own glory.

units.la: Ne verò putemus tantum hic agi de dissidio inter Gentes & Judaeos, interque Angelos & Homines: dicimur alibi Pacem erga Deum consequuti per fidem in CHRISTUM. Roman. 5. vers. 1, quia nimirum Pater in Christo, ut Sponsore nostro, acquiescit. Matth. 3. v. 17. Pater ipse dicit: Hic est filius meus ille dilectus, in quo acquiesce. Hic enim est, qui calcat lacum vini furoris & irae Dei. Apoçal, 5. v. 15.
units.tr: But lest we think that only the discord between Gentiles and Jews, and between angels and men, is treated here: elsewhere we are said to have obtained "peace toward God through faith in Christ," Romans 5:1, because surely the Father rests in Christ as our Surety. Matthew 3:17: the Father himself says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." For he is the one who treads the winepress of the wine of the fury and wrath of God, Revelation 15:19 (cf. 14:19-20).

units.la: Hinc propitiatio per Christum facta plerumque solet conjungi cum ejus intercessione; ut appareat, obedientia Christi pro nobis praestita, vere Deum factum esse nobis propitium. 1. Joh. 3. Filioli mei, haec scribo vobis, ne peccetis. Quod si quis peccaverit, Advocatum habemus apud Patrem, JESVM CHRISTVM justum: & ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris. En Christum & Propitiatorem & Advocatum: Et sensus est: Haec scribo vobis, carissimi, non ut fiducia misericordiae licentius peccetis, sed potius, ut memores summi illius beneficii per Christum allati, studiose a peccatis abstineatis. Si quis tamen (ut fit) ex infirmitate peccaverit, is ne propterea de gratia Dei desperet: Sed erigat se consideratione illius Patrocinii, quod ipse CHRISTUS Advocatus noster fidelissimus perpetuo nobis praestat apud Patrem nostrum. Quare consideret, Dominum JESUM esse propitiationem pro peccatis nostris, quippe quorum omnium plenissimam remissionem nobis comparavit.
units.tr: Hence the propitiation made through Christ is usually joined with his intercession, so that it appears that the obedience Christ rendered for us truly made God propitious to us. 1 John 2:1: "My little children, I write these things to you, that you may not sin. But if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; and he is the propitiation for our sins." Behold Christ both as Propitiator and as Advocate. And the sense is this: I write these things to you, dearly beloved, not so that you may sin the more freely from trust in mercy, but rather that, mindful of that supreme benefit brought through Christ, you may diligently abstain from sins. If anyone nevertheless (as happens) sins through weakness, let him not therefore despair of the grace of God; but let him raise himself by considering that patronage which Christ our most faithful Advocate continually provides for us before our Father. Let him therefore consider that the Lord Jesus is the propitiation for our sins, since he has procured for us the fullest remission of them all.

units.la: Hebr. 9. v. 22. &c. Postquam dixerat absq; sanguinis effusione non fieri remissionem, dicit Christum in coelum ingressum esse, ut appareat nunc in conspectu Dei pro nobis. Heb. 10. v. 12. Christus una pro peccatis oblata victima, in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei, &c. Deniq; ubi reconciliationis & pacificationis mentio fit, aperte indicatur, Deum nobis propitium factum esse Christi sacrificio: etsi hoc ipsum sacrificium ipse, qui prior dilexit nos, procuravit. 1. Joh. 4. v. 10. In hoc enim est caritas, non quod nos dilexerimus Deum, sed quod ipse dilexerit nos; et misit Filium suum, ut esset propitiatio pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: Hebrews 9:22 etc.: "Since he had said that without shedding of blood there is no remission," he says that Christ entered into heaven, "to appear now in the presence of God for us." Hebrews 10:12: "Christ, having offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sits at the right hand of God, etc." Finally, where mention is made of reconciliation and pacification, it is plainly indicated that God has been made propitious to us by the sacrifice of Christ, although he himself, who first loved us, procured this very sacrifice. 1 John 4:10: "In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins."
