units.la: Non autem (solum) docebunt amplius quisque amicum suum, & quisque[?] fratrem suum, dicendo: cognoscite Iehovam: Nam quotquot erunt, cognoscent me a minimo eorum, usque ad maximum eorum, dictum Iehova (nempe) me condonare iniquitatem ipsorum, & peccati ipsorum non recordari amplius. Et certe resipiscentia, ut effectus, fidem causam suam sequi solet.
units.tr: "They shall no longer teach each his neighbour and each his brother, saying, Know Jehovah; for all of them shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest of them, says Jehovah; for I will forgive their iniquity, and remember their sin no more." And certainly repentance, as an effect, is wont to follow its cause, faith.

units.la: Nam dolor ille, qui est secundum Deum, & efficit resipiscentiam, mentisque & consilii immutationem, item voluntatis & cordis conversionem, a malo & peccato commisso, ad bonum in posterum faciendum, fidei potius fœtus est.
units.tr: For that sorrow which is according to God, and which produces repentance, that is, a change of mind and purpose, and likewise a conversion of the will and heart from the evil and sin committed to doing good in future, is rather the fruit of faith.

units.la: CAPITIS I. SECTIO II.
units.tr: CHAPTER I. SECTION II.

units.la: HActenus prior Pars Assumti de absoluta DEI potestate, in iure suo remittendo, considerata & excussa est: sequitur iam posterior (quæ secundam objectionem parit) de benigna Dei voluntate, qua absq; satisfactione peccata remittere vult. Sic igitur argutantur:
units.tr: So far the first part of the assumption, concerning God's absolute power to remit his own right, has been considered and examined. Now follows the second part, which gives rise to the second objection, concerning God's gracious will, by which he wishes to forgive sins without satisfaction. They argue as follows:

units.la: Si DEus semper voluit, & vult adhuc, peccata absq; ulla præstita satisfactione nobis condonare, frustra laborantur[?] hominum animi Christi satisfactione & merito.
units.tr: If God has always willed, and still wills, to forgive us our sins without any satisfaction rendered, then men's minds labour in vain over Christ's satisfaction and merit.

units.la: At antecedens verum esse demon-stratur.
units.tr: But the antecedent is shown to be true.

units.la: Qui promisit, semper se benignitate usurum erga resipiscentes, ita ut non satisfactionem, sed tantum resipiscentiam & vitæ emendationem requirat, is etiam semper voluit, & vult, peccata nobis condonare, absq; ulla ullius satisfactione.
units.tr: He who promised that he would always deal in kindness with those who repent, so that he requires not satisfaction but only repentance and amendment of life, has also always willed, and still wills, to forgive us our sins, without any satisfaction from anyone.

units.la: At Deus promisit semper se benignitate usurum erga resipiscentes, ita ut non satisfactionem, sed tantum resipiscentiam et vitæ emendationem requirat.
units.tr: But God promised that he would always deal in kindness with those who repent, so that he requires not satisfaction but only repentance and amendment of life.

units.la: EXAMEN.
units.tr: EXAMINATION.

units.la: Fatemur Deum promisisse se beninitate usurum erga omnes resipiscentes. Magni enim facimus has Dei promissiones.
units.tr: We grant that God has promised to deal in kindness with all who repent. For we hold these promises of God in high esteem.

units.la: Ezech. 18. 21. &c. Cum autem improbus conversus ab omnibus peccatis suis, quae fecit, observabit omnia statuta mea, & exercebit ius & iustitiam, omnino vivet, non morietur. Omnes defectiones eius, quas commisit, non commemorabuntur ei; in sua iustitia, quam exercet, vivet. An nullo pacto delector Morte improbi? Dictum Domini Jehova: an non cum revertitur a viis suis, ut vivat? Sed cum averti se iustus a iustitia sua, & facit iniquitate, secundum omnes abominationes, quas fecerit improbus, facit, hucine viveret? Omnia iuste facta eius, quae fecerit, non commemorabuntur, propter praevaricationem ipsius, quam praevaricatus, & propter peccatum ipsius, quo peccat, propter hac morietur, &c.
units.tr: Ezek. 18. 21, etc. But if the wicked man turns from all his sins that he has committed, and keeps all my statutes, and does judgement and justice, he shall surely live, he shall not die. None of the transgressions that he has committed shall be remembered against him; in his righteousness that he has done he shall live. Have I any pleasure at all in the death of the wicked? says the Lord GOD: and not rather that he should return from his ways, and live? But when the righteous turns away from his righteousness, and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the wicked man does, shall he live? None of his righteous deeds that he has done shall be remembered, because of the trespass that he has trespassed, and because of the sin that he has sinned, for them he shall die, etc.

units.la: Ezech. 33. 11. &c. Dic eis, ne vivam ego, dictum Domini Jehovah, si delector morte impii, sed (delector) cum revertitur improbus a via sua, ut vivat. Revertimini, revertimini a viis vestris pessimis, cur enim moriemini domus Israel.
units.tr: Ezek. 33. 11, etc. Say to them: As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn, turn from your evil ways, for why will you die, O house of Israel?

units.la: Tu ergo, fili hominis, dic populari bus tuis: iustitia iusti non erit ereptura ipsum, tempore defectionis suae, & in sua improbitate improbus non corruet, quo tempore reversus fuerit ab improbitate sua: ut iustus non poterit vivere illa, quo tempore peccabit. Quum dixero iusto, omnino viveturus et, si ipse confessus iustitiae suae fecerit iniquitatem: omnia iuste facta ipsius non memorabuntur, sed in iniquitate illa sua, quam fecit, morietur; Et cum dixero improbo; omnino moriturus es; si reversus a peccato suo exercuerit iudicium & iustitiam, in statutis vita ambulaverit, non faciendo iniquitatem, omnino vivet, non morietur.
units.tr: Therefore, son of man, say to your people: the righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression; and as for the wickedness of the wicked, he shall not fall by it in the day that he turns from his wickedness; nor shall the righteous be able to live by his righteousness in the day that he sins. When I say to the righteous that he shall surely live, if he trusts in his righteousness and commits iniquity, none of his righteous deeds shall be remembered; but in the iniquity that he has committed he shall die. And when I say to the wicked, You shall surely die; if he turns from his sin and does judgement and justice, and walks in the statutes of life, not committing iniquity, he shall surely live, he shall not die.

units.la: Jerem. 3. v. 8. 9. Tantummodo agnosce iniquitatem tuam, te a Jehova Deo tuo defecisse: Nam sparsim univisti vias tuas ad extremos sub omni arbore virente, et voci meae non auscultasti, dictum Jehova. Revertimini filii aversantes, dictum Jehova, nam ego conjugio junctus sum vobis: & recipiam vos, &c.
units.tr: Jer. 3. 8, 9. Only acknowledge your iniquity, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God, for you have scattered your ways to strangers under every green tree, and you have not obeyed my voice, says the LORD. Return, you backsliding children, says the LORD, for I am married to you; and I will take you, etc.

units.la: Jerem. 18. Si convertatur gens illa a malo suo, contra quam locutus fuero, poenitebit me super malo eius, quod cogitaveram facere ei.
units.tr: Jer. 18. If that nation turns from its evil, against which I have spoken, I will repent of the evil that I had thought to do to them.

units.la: Baptista praedicans dixit Matth. 3. verf. 2. Resipiscite, appropinquavit enim regnum coelorum. Petrus inquit Actor. 3. 19. Resipiscite igitur et convertimini, ut deleantur peccata vestra. Et Actor. 5. v. 31. Deus Patrum nostrorum exitavit Jesum, quem vos interfecistis. Hunc ipsum Deus dextra sua evectum constituit Principem ac Servatorem, ut det resipiscentiam Israeli, & remissionem peccatorum. Paulus item Actor. 17. 30. Temporibus igitur istius ignorantiae dissimulatis Deus nunc denuntiat omnibus ubique hominibus, ut resipiscant, eo quod statuit diem, quo [illegible, ~3 letters] iudicaturus est orbem terrarum, per eum quem definiit, & cap.26.10. Annuntiavit Judaeis & Gentibus, ut resipiscerent & converterentur ad Deum, opera facientes digna iis qui resipuissent.
units.tr: John the Baptist, preaching, said (Matt. 3. 2): Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. Peter says (Acts 3. 19): Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out. And (Acts 5. 31): The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed, hanging him on a tree. Him God has exalted with his right hand to be Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. Paul likewise (Acts 17. 30): The times of this ignorance God overlooked, but now commands all men everywhere to repent, because he has appointed a day on which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained [illegible, about three letters]; and (ch. 26. 20): I declared to the Jews and the Gentiles that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

units.la: Hæc & similia agnoscimus, & inde concludimus, requiri à nobis veram conversionem & resipiscentiam ex parte nostra; At inde non efficitur, ex parte Dei nō requiri ullam satisfactionem pro peccatis nostris. Deus est, qui remittit peccata & justificat, qui se solum esse Servatorem nostrum affirmat, qui iniquitates nostras propter seipsum delet[?]. Iesa. 43. 11. Remittit seu condonat peccata ex gratuita bonitate, pura gratia & Misericordia sua, ex quâ & nobis datum est IESUS CHRI-STUS, Agnus ille Dei, tollens peccata Mundi, ex quâ & nobis conceditur Fides, per quam Christi participes fiamus.
units.tr: We acknowledge these and similar passages, and conclude from them that true conversion and repentance are required of us on our part. But it does not follow from this that no satisfaction for our sins is required on God's part. It is God who remits sins and justifies, who affirms that he alone is our Saviour, who blots out our iniquities for his own sake. Isa. 43. 11. He remits and forgives sins out of free goodness, by his pure grace and mercy, from which JESUS CHRIST, that Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, was also given to us, from which faith is also granted to us, through which we become partakers of Christ.

units.la: Hac gratiâ & liberalitate excludi quidem operum nostrorum merita dicimus, quibus scilicet justitiam ac salutem promereamur. Ex misericordia item hac nobis peccata condonari absq; jacturâ justitiæ Dei concedimus, quia Ita Deus judiciariæ justitiæ alligatus non est, ut pro suâ liberâ potestate misereri non possit, cujus velit: ipsiq; duplex est thronus, alter gratiæ, alter judicii. Sed quia subordinata se non tol-lunt, etsi Deus ex purâ suâ gratiâ ac liberalitate nobis peccata remittit, ex-cludi à condonatione peccatorum, ad-eoq; justificatione, Christi satisfactionem, neutiquam concedimus. Negamus igitur ita Deum benignitate suâ erga respicientes usurum promisisse, ut non satisfactione Christi, sed TAN-TUM vitæ emendationem requirat.
units.tr: By this grace and liberality we deny that the merits of our works are excluded, by which, of course, we might earn righteousness and salvation. Likewise we grant that by this mercy sins are forgiven us without loss to the justice of God, for God is not so bound to judicial justice that he cannot show mercy to whomever he wills by his free power; and he has a double throne, one of grace and one of judgement. But since subordinate things do not cancel each other out, even though God remits our sins out of his pure grace and liberality, we by no means grant that Christ's satisfaction is excluded from the forgiveness of sins, and so from justification. We deny, therefore, that God promised to deal in kindness with those who repent in such a way that he requires not Christ's satisfaction but only amendment of life.

units.la: Media enim adhibet Deus, quæ per misericordiam illam suam in nobis ad effectum producit: Horum unum ex-tra nos est, videlicet CHRISTUS ME-DIATOR, quem Deus nobis propositi propitiatore, interveniente ipsius sanguine. Et quidem hic, ubi de condo-natione peccatorum agitur, Christus consideratur, quatenus est Mediator, inter Deum & homines, ac proinde tanquam secundaria causa nostræ justitiæ, quam principalis non excludit. Unde passim illæ formulæ in S. li-teris exstant, Nos per Christum habere adi-tum seu accessum ad Deigratiam, adeoque per Christum ad Deum adduct. Rom. 5, 2. & 11. Ephes. 2.18. 1.Tim.2.5. 1.Pet.1.21. cap. 3.18. Heb. 7. 25. Mediator hic noster in statu humiliationis Deo Patri obedies factus in vitâ simul & morte, catenus justitiam & salutem nobis promeruit. Et quia nullum magis arduum opus nostrâ causâ suscepit, quàm cum mortem obivit, & sanguinem suum pro nobis effudit, idcirco passim sanguini & morti CHRISTI condonatio, justificatio & reconciliatio adscribitur. Gra-tia itaq; Dei & Meritum JESU CHRISTI non debent inter se opponi, cum istud potius illi subordinandū fit, quippe quod ex mero Dei beneplacito profluxit. Alterum medium intra nos si-tum est, nempe fides in JESUM CHRISTUM, qua misericordiam illam Dei in JESU CHRISTO exhibitam, adeoq; Christi meritis comparatam, ample-ctimur.
units.tr: For God employs means, which through that mercy of his he brings to effect in us. One of these is outside us, namely CHRIST THE MEDIATOR, whom God has set forth as a propitiation, through the intervention of his blood. And indeed here, where the forgiveness of sins is treated, Christ is considered as he is Mediator between God and men, and so as a secondary cause of our righteousness, which the principal cause does not exclude. Hence those formulas occur everywhere in the sacred letters: that we have access or approach to the grace of God through Christ, and are thus brought to God through Christ (Rom. 5. 2, 11; Eph. 2. 18; 1 Tim. 2. 5; 1 Pet. 1. 21; ch. 3. 18; Heb. 7. 25). This our Mediator, in the state of humiliation, made obedient to God the Father in life and in death, merited righteousness and salvation for us to that extent. And because he undertook no more arduous work on our behalf than when he underwent death and poured out his blood for us, therefore forgiveness, justification and reconciliation are everywhere ascribed to the blood and death of Christ. Grace of God and the merit of Jesus Christ therefore ought not to be set against each other, since the latter is rather subordinate to the former, as it flowed from God's mere good pleasure. The other means lies within us, namely faith in Jesus Christ, by which we embrace that mercy of God exhibited in Jesus Christ, and so obtained by the merits of Christ.

units.la: SED ILLI ANNITUNTUR probare subsumtum suum.
units.tr: BUT THEY STRIVE TO PROVE their minor premise.

units.la: Sacrae literae veteris & novi foederis non tantum docent, verum etiam persuadent, Deum nobis peccata nostra velle liberalissime condonare, absque satisfactione, ex sola gratia & benignitate sua.
units.tr: The sacred writings of the Old and New Covenant not only teach but also persuade that God wishes to forgive us our sins most freely, without satisfaction, from his grace and kindness alone.

units.la: I. Ex Veteri Testamento primum afferunt justum Abelem.
units.tr: I. From the Old Testament they first bring forward the righteous Abel.

units.la: Nemo, inquiunt, potest esse justus, cui delicta a Deo non condonantur.
units.tr: No one, they say, can be righteous whose sins are not forgiven by God.

units.la: Abel ab ipso Christo justus fuisse dicitur, Matth. 23.25. & Heb.11,4. Ergo ipsi peccata fuerunt condonata.
units.tr: Abel is said to have been righteous by Christ himself, Matth. 23.25, and Heb. 11.4. Therefore his sins were forgiven him.

units.la: Concedo de justitia fidei, quae consistit in gratuita condonatione peccatorum, propter Christum.
units.tr: I grant this concerning the righteousness of faith, which consists in the gratuitous forgiveness of sins for Christ's sake.

units.la: Perge. Si condonata illi fuerunt peccata, aut[?] ideo condonata sunt, quia credidit in promissum Semen & Messiam olim satisfacturum pro ipsius peccatis: aut quia pure & innocenter vixit.
units.tr: Go on. If his sins were forgiven him, either they were forgiven because he believed in the promised Seed and Messiah who would one day make satisfaction for his sins, or because he lived purely and innocently.

units.la: At non illud: 1. Quia justus in sacris literis intelligitur, qui pure & innocenter vixit, sicut injustus, qui impure et flagitiose. Deinde patet hoc ex Responso Dei ad Cainum: Gen. 4.7. Ut quid succensa est iratua tibi? Et ut quid concidit vultus tuus? nonne si benefeceris, erit acceptatio? Ergo Deus iis, qui vel mature vel serum pure & innocenter vivunt, omnium delictorum veniam largitur, eosq; caros habet.
units.tr: But not the latter. First, because in the sacred writings he is understood to be righteous who lived purely and innocently, just as he is unrighteous who lived impurely and shamefully. Next, this is clear from God's answer to Cain, Gen. 4.7: Why is your anger kindled? And why has your countenance fallen? Shall it not be accepted if you do well? Therefore God bestows the pardon of all offences on those who live purely and innocently, whether early or late, and holds them dear.

units.la: EXAMEN.
units.tr: EXAMINATION.

units.la: Ego vero assumo: Atqui Abel fuit justus, quia credidit in Semen mulieris promissum, in satisfacturū [?] pro peccatis suis, in Agnum Dei ab initio mactatum, quia placuit Deo per fidem, ex qua deinde pure & innocenter vixit. Certamen fuit inter Cain & Abel (ut nonnulli ex veteribus scribunt) de hoc, quomodo & propter quid Deus hominem, qui propter peccatum reus est, respiciat, ut aestimonium consequatur, quòd sit justus coram Deo. Heb. 11. 4. Abel quidem obtinuit justificari remissione, i. e. remissione peccati. Gen. 4. 7. Idq; fide promissionis, propter semen. Heb. 11. 4. Et haec fides paulo post, Gen. 4. v. ult. declaratur: Enos coepit invocare nomen Domini.
units.tr: I, however, assume: But Abel was righteous, because he believed in the Seed of the woman promised to make satisfaction for his sins, in the Lamb of God slain from the beginning, and because he pleased God through faith, from which he then lived purely and innocently. There was a dispute between Cain and Abel (as some of the ancients write) about this: how and on what ground God regards a man who is guilty on account of sin, so that he might obtain the testimony that he is righteous before God. Heb. 11.4: Abel indeed obtained to be justified by remission, that is, by the remission of sin. Gen. 4.7. And this by faith in the promise, on account of the seed. Heb. 11.4. And this faith is declared a little later, Gen. 4, last verse: Enos began to call upon the name of the Lord.

units.la: Cain vero negavit justitiam coram Deo esse levatione seu condonationem peccati, fide propter semen: sed judicavit, se posse sacrificiis & aliis operib. peccatum levare & tollere, & quidem irascitur, DEUM ad se & sua sacrificia, propter dignitatem operum, non respicere. Gen. 4. 5. Cain non curavit levationem peccati per fidem, quia non agnovit, quale & quantū on[?] sit peccatum, maximè quando quiescit & mortuum est. Quiescente peccato, potest concipere persuasionem de disciplinâ legis, & ideo minus curat promissionem gratiæ, permittit dominationem concupiscentiæ peccati, & tamen putat se justum esse sacrificiis ex opere operato. Quando vero veniente lege peccatum revivíscit, exclamat Cain: Major est iniquitas mea, quàm ut remittatur.
units.tr: But Cain denied that righteousness before God consists in the lifting up or forgiveness of sin by faith in the seed. He judged that he could lift and take away sin by sacrifices and other works, and indeed he was angry that God did not regard him and his sacrifices on account of the dignity of his works. Gen. 4.5. Cain did not care for the removal of sin through faith, because he did not recognise what and how great sin is, especially when it lies quiet and is dead. While sin is quiet, he can form the persuasion of the discipline of the law, and so he cares less for the promise of grace; he allows the dominion of the lust of sin, and yet thinks himself righteous by sacrifices performed by the mere doing of the rite. But when, with the coming of the law, sin revives, Cain cries out: My iniquity is greater than that it can be forgiven.

units.la: Deinde explosâ hac Pelagianâ opinione, sine fide Evangelii, quosdam solâ observatione legis naturæ, quosdam legis Mosaicæ observatione, coram Deo justificatos & salvatos esse, manet unū & idem Evangelium, quo omnes sancti, omnib. temporibus, ab initio mundi salvati sunt. Statim enim post lapsum Adæ revelata est doctrina Evangelii, de gratuita reconciliatione, fide propter Mediatorem, in illa promissione: Semen mulieris, &c. Et mox Gen. 4. 4. & 7. Deus ipse interpretatur illam promissionem, per levationem seu condonationem peccati, & quod Deus respexit ad Abel. Unde ad Heb. 11. v. 4. dicitur Abel per fidem accepisse testimonium, quòd esset justus coram Deo, & quidem per fidem illam, ipsum etiam post mortem loqui, hoc est, vivere & Deo curae esse.
units.tr: Then, with this Pelagian opinion cast out (that without faith in the Gospel some were justified and saved before God by observance of the law of nature alone, and some by observance of the Mosaic law), there remains one and the same Gospel by which all the saints, in all times from the beginning of the world, were saved. For immediately after the fall of Adam the doctrine of the Gospel, of gratuitous reconciliation by faith in the Mediator, was revealed in that promise: The seed of the woman, etc. And soon after, at Gen. 4.4 and 7, God himself interprets that promise as the lifting up or forgiveness of sin, and says that God had regard for Abel. Whence at Heb. 11.4 it is said that Abel through faith received the testimony that he was righteous before God, and indeed that through that same faith he still speaks even after death, that is, he lives and is a care to God.

units.la: Qui igitur justus est propria & inhaerente justitia, is innocenter & pure vixit: sed & est quis justus in sacris literis per justitiam non legis, sed Evangelii, non operum, sed fidei, de qua Justitia Dei per fidem Jesu Christi, in omnes, & super omnes credentes. Sic fides Abrahae imputata dicitur ei ad justitiam, & adhuc fides cuilibet credenti imputatur ad justitiam, id est, Christus crucifixus apprehensus fide, censetur nostra justitia, censetur, inquam, a Deo, e tribunali suo sententiam justitiae pronunciante.
units.tr: Therefore he who is righteous by his own and inherent righteousness has lived innocently and purely. But there is also one who is righteous in the sacred writings through the righteousness not of the law but of the Gospel, not of works but of faith, concerning which the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ is unto all and upon all who believe. Thus Abraham's faith is said to be reckoned to him for righteousness, and still faith is reckoned to every believer for righteousness; that is, Christ crucified, apprehended by faith, is counted as our righteousness. He is counted so, I say, by God, who pronounces the sentence of righteousness from his tribunal.

units.la: OBJICIUNT:
units.tr: THEY OBJECT:

units.la: Fides, quâ Abel placuit Deo, hæc est, quòd credidit non modò Deum esse, sed etiam eos, qui eum requirunt, hoc est, ei obediunt, large remunerari. Unde factum est, ut vitam suam ad voluntatem Dei componeret. Adeoque fides, sine quâ nemo potest Deo placere, vita puritate & innocentiâ continetur.
units.tr: The faith by which Abel pleased God is this: that he believed not only that God exists, but also that those who seek him, that is, who obey him, are richly rewarded. Hence he came to order his life according to God's will. And so faith, without which no one can please God, is contained in a life of purity and innocence.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: RESPONSE.

units.la: Unus ut Deus est, ita una fides, per quam servamur. Haec fides in cap. 11. 4. Hebr. describitur ex tribus effectis, 1. quod sit substantia rerum, quae sperantur, & index rerum, quae non cernuntur. 2. quod propter eam homines Deo placeant, 3. quod per eum intelligamus res rationi humanae incredibiles. Haec effecta exemplis e sacra historia ordine de-sumtis illustratur, e quibus tria prima Abelis, Enochi, Noachi acciderutan-te diluvium. Si vero ipsam Fidem Salvificam ex sacris literis discere est animus, deprehendere licet.
units.tr: There is one God, and so there is one faith through which we are saved. In chapter 11, verse 4 of Hebrews this faith is described by three effects: (1) it is the substance of things hoped for and the evidence of things not seen; (2) through it men please God; (3) through it we understand things that are incredible to human reason. These effects are illustrated by examples taken in order from sacred history, of which the first three concern Abel, Enoch and Noah before the flood. If we wish to learn the saving faith itself from the sacred writings, we may discover it.

units.la: 1. Fidem, Notitiam, & Scientiam vocari, Luc. 11. 77. Jef. 57. 11. Coloss. 2. 3. Eph. 3. 19. Ex verbo Dei enim cognoscenda historia redemtionis & promissio gratiae, quod propter Christi victimam Deus velit peccatores, fide ad mediatorem confugientes, in gratiam recipere.
units.tr: (1) Faith is called knowledge, acquaintance and understanding: Luke 11. 77. Isaiah 57. 11. Colossians 2. 3. Ephesians 3. 19. For the history of redemption and the promise of grace, namely that for the sake of Christ's sacrifice God wills to receive sinners into favour when they flee to the Mediator in faith, must be learned from the Word of God.

units.la: 2. Cum multi, qui haec audiunt, intelligunt & noverunt, vel negligunt, vel dubitant, vel repugnant, notitiae conjunctam esse oportet assensionem non quide generalem tantum, sed quâ firmâ persuasione, quâ Paul' πληροφορίαν [?] vocat, quisq; statuat universalem illam promissione, privatim, adse quoq; proprie & particulariter pertinere [?], & se quoque includi in illa universali promissione.
units.tr: (2) Since many who hear these things understand and know them, yet neglect them, doubt them or resist them, there must be joined to knowledge an assent that is not merely general but also a firm persuasion, which Paul calls [πληροφορίαν] full assurance. By this a person determines that this universal promise pertains privately, to himself also, personally and particularly, and that he too is included in that universal promise.

units.la: 3. Ex hac notitiâ & assensione, quæ in mente est, cor concipit operatione Spiritus S. gemitum ac desiderium, ut quia serio sentit, se oneratum esse peccatis & irâ Dei, velit, expetat, quæras sibi donari illa beneficia, quæ in promissione Evangelii proponuntur. Illud vero desiderium æstuat intus gemitib9 inenarrabilibus, & exerit se per invocationem.
units.tr: (3) From this knowledge and assent, which are in the mind, the heart, by the working of the Holy Spirit, conceives a groaning and a longing. Because it seriously feels itself burdened with sins and with the wrath of God, it wills and desires to have bestowed upon it those benefits which are set forth in the promise of the Gospel. This desire glows within with groanings that cannot be uttered, and it expresses itself through prayer.

units.la: Roman. 10. v. 4.
units.tr: Romans 10. 4.

units.la: Quando hoc modo, mente, voluntate, & corde te avertis à conspectu peccati & sensu iræ Dei, & respicis ad agnum illum Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi: id est, quando à sententia damnationis, q per legem tibi denuntiatur, confugis ad thronū gratiæ, & ad propitiatorium, quod pater cœlestis ꝓposuit in sanguine Christi; Necesse est accedere fiduciam, quæ firmâ persuasione, ex Verbo Dei statustatuat, Deum tunc tibi donare, communicare & applicare beneficia promissionis gratiæ, & te hoc modo vere apprehendere & accipere ad justitiam, salutem & vitam æternam, ea, quæ gratuita Evangelii promissio offert. Et hæc fiducia luctatur in tentatione cum dubitatione, cum pavoribus trepidantis conscientiæ, imo cum peccato, morte, diabolo & ipsis inferis. Postremo sequitur ex hac fide παῤῥησία[?], quæ habet accessum ad Deum, pacem conscientiæ, & gaudium Spiritus, &c.
units.tr: When in this way, with mind, will and heart, you turn away from the sight of sin and the sense of God's wrath, and look to that Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world; that is, when from the sentence of condemnation which the law pronounces against you, you flee to the throne of grace and to the mercy seat which the heavenly Father has set forth in the blood of Christ, there must come a trust which, by a firm persuasion drawn from the Word of God, determines that God then gives, communicates and applies to you the benefits of the promise of grace, and that in this way you truly lay hold of and receive, for righteousness, salvation and eternal life, what the free promise of the Gospel offers. This trust struggles in temptation against doubt, against the terrors of a trembling conscience, indeed against sin, death, the devil and hell itself. Finally, from this faith there follows [παῤῥησία] boldness, which gives access to God, peace of conscience, joy of the Spirit, and so on.

units.la: Scio, hanc fidei apprehensionem & applicationem ab Adversariis derideri. Sed videamus credente Paulum, q; Gal. 2.16. primò ponit generalé sententiam, quòd non justificetur homo ex operibus legis, nisi per fidé Christi. Secundò ponit applicationé specialem: Nos Judæi in Christum credimus, ut justificemur. Tertiò, v. 20. in applicatione descendit ad individuum usq; : Vivo in fide Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me: non abjicio gratiam Dei. Phil.3. 9. 10. 11. Ut inveniar in Christo non habens meam justitiam, sed illam, quæ ex Deo est, justitiam in fide, ad agnoscendum illum, & virtutem resurrectionis ejus, ut occurram ad resurrectionem. Et addit v. 15. quicunque perfecti sumus, hoc sentiamus, &c. Rom.4. 16. Ut firma sit promissio omnis semini. Item v. 23. 24. Scriptum est non tantum propter Abraham, sed & propter nos, quibus imputabitur credentibus, &c. Et exemplum applicationis singulis credituris apponitur & describitur Rom. 8. 35. 38. Aliud itaq; fides ipsa est, aliud cum fide conjuncta puritas & innocetia vitæ; sicut aliud justificatio, aliud regeneratio seu sanctificatio.
units.tr: I know that this apprehension and application of faith is mocked by our adversaries. But let us see how Paul believes. In Galatians 2. 16. he first states the general sentence, that a man is not justified by the works of the law but only through faith in Christ. Second, he states the special application: We Jews believe in Christ, that we may be justified. Third, at verse 20, in the application he descends to the individual: I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me; I do not set aside the grace of God. Philippians 3. 9, 10, 11: that I may be found in Christ, not having my own righteousness, but that which is of God, the righteousness by faith, to know him and the power of his resurrection, that I may attain to the resurrection. And he adds at verse 15: as many as are mature, let us think this way, etc. Romans 4. 16: so that the promise may be firm to all the seed. Likewise at verses 23 and 24: It is written not only for Abraham's sake, but also for ours, to whom it will be imputed who believe, etc. And an example of application, to be set before each one who is about to believe, is given and described in Romans 8. 35–38. Therefore faith itself is one thing, and purity and innocence of life joined with faith is another, just as justification is one thing and regeneration or sanctification is another.

units.la: OBJICITUR.
units.tr: OBJECTION.

units.la: Si Dei patientia exspectat resipiscentiam hominum, ut illis parcat, & peccata condonet, ne pereat, certè Deus tantum ob resipiscentiam peccata condonat, non ob satisfactionem Christi. At verum primùm, ut ostendit historia Noachi, quia Deus patienter scelera hominum centum & viginti annis tulit, ut mundum resipisceret, ut testatur etiam Petrus, 1. Epist. c. 3. Et 2. Pet. 3. v. 9. Non tardat Dominus promissum, sed patienter agit erga nos, nolens aliquos perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti.
units.tr: If the patience of God waits for men to repent, so that he may spare them and forgive their sins, lest they perish, then surely God forgives sins only on account of repentance, not on account of the satisfaction of Christ. But first, this is true, as the history of Noah shows, because God patiently bore men's wickedness for one hundred and twenty years, so that the world might repent; as Peter also testifies in 1 Peter, chapter 3, and in 2 Peter 3. 9: The Lord does not delay his promise, but acts patiently toward us, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should return to repentance.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Connexum propositionis negatur. Patientia enim Dei non tantum exspectat nostram resipiscentiam; vitæq; innocentiam & puritatem, sed etiam fi-dem in Jesum Christum, per quam ser-vamur. Deus qui & fidem & resi-piscentiam dat, vult omnes etiam homines pervenire ad cognitionem veritatis, quae fide continetur, exspectat itaque & fidem hominum in Christum, qua sibi applicet gratiae promissionem. Non igitur sequitur. Patientia Dei exspectat hominum resipiscentiam. Ergo condonat peccata non propter satisfactionem à Christo justitiam, sed propter resipiscentiam tantum. Ut enim ex parte nostra Deus fidem & resipiscentiam postulat ad salutem, sic ex parte sua Satisfactionem pro nostris peccatis, quae praestita sit justitiae suae, quae satisfactio non tollit, sed ponit simul Dei benignam in nos liberalitatem.
units.tr: The connection of the proposition is denied. For the patience of God does not only wait for our repentance and innocence of life and purity, but also for faith in Jesus Christ, through which we are saved. God, who gives both faith and repentance, wills that all men come to the knowledge of the truth, which is contained in faith. He therefore also waits for men's faith in Christ, by which they apply to themselves the promise of grace. It does not follow, then, that the patience of God waits for men's repentance. Therefore he forgives sins not on account of the satisfaction made by Christ and his righteousness, but on account of repentance only. For just as God, on our part, requires faith and repentance for salvation, so on his part he requires satisfaction for our sins, which has been rendered to his justice. This satisfaction does not abolish God's kindly generosity towards us, but rather establishes it alongside.

units.la: Et sane si concederem absolutionem pœnitetis, adeoq; remissionem peccatorum esse effectum ipsius pœnitentiae salutaris (quae est seria à peccatis ad justitiam conversio) non tamen concedam pœnitentiam, ad quam nos reverti vult Deus patiens, ex nostris ipsorum viribus [?]ribus proficisci, vel per eam & prote-ter eam nos donum illud Dei, utpote vere gratuitum; vere coram Deo romereri: sed tantum ordinem inter haec divinitus sanctum, nempe ordinem antecessionis & consecutionis, non inutiliter observarem.
units.tr: And indeed, even if I granted that the absolution of the penitent, and so the remission of sins, is the effect of saving repentance itself (which is a earnest conversion from sins to righteousness), I would still not grant that the repentance to which the patient God wills us to return springs from our own powers, or that through it, and apart from it, we merit before God that gift of his, which is truly free. I would only observe, not unprofitably, the order divinely established among these things, namely the order of antecedent and consequent.

units.la: OBJICITUR AB ADVERSARIIS.
units.tr: THE OBJECTION OF THE ADVERSARIES.

units.la: Si ex parte Dei, nil nisi misericordia, ex parte nostra nil nisi poenitentia seu conversio requiritur in Veteri Testamento; nullum superesset locus fidei[?] satisfactioni Christi. Atqui antecedens probant Moses, Levitae & Prophetae.
units.tr: If on God's part nothing is required but mercy, and on our part nothing but penitence or conversion, in the Old Testament, then there would be no place left for faith in Christ's satisfaction. But Moses, the Levites and the Prophets prove the antecedent.

units.la: 1. Verba Mosis sunt Deut.4.30. Cum fuerit tibi angustia, invenerintq; te omnia ista in novissimis diebus: Si reversus fueris ad Jehova Deum tuum, & parueris voci ejus, quia Deus misericors est Jehova Deus tuus, non derelinquet te, nec differdet te, nec obliviscetur patrum tuorum, de quo juravit illis. Et cap.30. in initio: Erit autem, cum evenerint tibi omnia verba haec, benedictio & maledictio, quas proposui tibi, & reduxeris ad cor tuum, in cunctis gentibus, ad quas expulerit te Jehova Deus tuus, & conversus fueris ad Jehovam Deum tuum, obedieris voci ejus per omnia, ut ego praecipio tibi hodie, & tum reducet Jehova Deus tuus captivitatem tuam, & miserebitur tui, & conversus congregabit te de cunctis populis.
units.tr: 1. The words of Moses are in Deut. 4:30: When you are in distress, and all these things come upon you in the latter days, if you return to Jehovah your God and obey his voice (for Jehovah your God is a merciful God), he will not forsake you or destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which he swore to them. And in chapter 30, at the beginning: And it shall be, when all these words, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before you, have come upon you, and you have taken them to heart among all the nations to which Jehovah your God has driven you, and you have turned to Jehovah your God and obeyed his voice in all things, as I command you today, then Jehovah your God will restore your captivity and have compassion on you, and he will gather you again from all the peoples.

units.la: 2. Levitæ in oratione sua ad Deum, Nehem. 9. Ipsi vero, ajunt, & Patres nostri superbè egerunt, & induraverunt cervicem su-am, nec audiverunt præcepta tua, &c. Tu tamen Deus veniarum, clemens & multa misericors, longanimis & misericordia non dereliquisti eos.
units.tr: 2. The Levites in their prayer to God, Neh. 9: But they, they say, and our fathers acted proudly and hardened their neck, and did not hear your commandments, etc. Yet you, O God of forgiveness, gracious and very merciful, slow to anger and abounding in mercy, did not forsake them.

units.la: 3. Prophetas hac de re testantes, utpote Ezechielem cap.18.&c.33. Jeremiámq; supra audivimus. His addunt exempla sententiæ, contra delinquentes à DEO lata, propter ipsorum supervenientem pœnitentiam, iterum à DEO revocata & rescissa. Ut exemplum Ezechiæ & Ninivitarum, item Achabi 1. Regum. 21. 21. & 31. Roboami & Israelitarum, 2. Paral. 12. Huc item pertinent testimonia Jeremiæ cap. 18. & Ezech. 33. de quibus supra.
units.tr: 3. We have heard the prophets bearing witness to this matter, such as Ezekiel in chapters 18 and 33, and Jeremiah above. To these they add examples of sentences pronounced by God against offenders, which were revoked and rescinded by God on account of their subsequent repentance: such as the example of Hezekiah and the Ninevites, likewise of Ahab, 1 Kings 21:21 and 29, and of Rehoboam and the Israelites, 2 Chron. 12. To this also pertain the testimonies of Jeremiah ch. 18 and Ezekiel ch. 33, mentioned above.

units.la: Hinc concludunt, Deum ante Christum na-tum, tantum divinam suam misericordiam re-spexisse, per quam pœnitentes liberalissimè à pœ-nis ipsorum delictis debitis exemerit: adeoq; nul-lam omninò satisfactionem pro peccatis voluisse.
units.tr: From this they conclude that before Christ was born God regarded only his divine mercy, by which, most freely, he released penitent sinners from the penalties due to their offences; and therefore that he wished for no satisfaction at all for sins.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Ex his aliud nihil cōficitur, quàm ex Dei Misericordiâ & gratiosâ liberalitate pœnitentibus peccata remitti, quod ultrò concedimus. Satisfactio verò Mediatoris & Sponsoris Christi prædictis neutiquam tollitur. Siquidem positâ caussâ principe, & ejus interiore impulsiva, Deo, dico, & ejus benignitate; non tollitur caussa secundaria & meritoria, nempe Christi satisfactio. Cùm caussa efficiens, cum suis mediis, fit simul ordinata ad peccatorum remissionem.
units.tr: From these passages nothing else follows than that sins are forgiven to penitent people by the mercy and gracious generosity of God, which we readily concede. But the satisfaction of Christ, the Mediator and Surety, is in no way removed by these. For when the principal cause is posited, together with its inner impelling cause, namely God and his goodness, the secondary and meritorious cause is not thereby removed, that is, the satisfaction of Christ. Since the efficient cause, together with its means, is also ordained to the remission of sins.

units.la: Ex parte Dei condonantis peccata, nil nisi liberalis beneficentia requiritur; Ex parte verò nostrâ non nisi voluntaria acceptio: Verùm sicut hoc non excludit ex parte nostrâ pœnitentiam & fidem in Christum: sic ex parte Dei non excluditur satisfactionis conditio; præsertim cùm Deus ipse id dederit, quod sibi solvi voluit. Roman. 8. 32. Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? qui proprio filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, qui non etiam cum eo omnia nobis gratificabitur?
units.tr: On God's part, forgiving sins, nothing but liberal beneficence is required; on our part, only voluntary acceptance. Yet just as this does not exclude on our part repentance and faith in Christ, so on God's part the condition of satisfaction is not excluded, especially since God himself has provided that which he willed to be paid to himself. Rom. 8:32: If God is for us, who can be against us? He who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all, will he not also with him graciously give us all things?

units.la: Deus itaq; Misericors & valde clemens peccata nobis resipiscentibus, & verè credentibus liberaliter condonat, propter Jesu Christi filii sui Mediatoris nostri meritum & satisfactionem. Nos itaq; acquirimus peccatorum condo-nationationem in Christo unico omnium Mediatore, Recociliatore, & Redemtore, cui omnes Prophetæ testimonium perhibent, & remissionem peccatorum accipiant per nomen ejus, omnes, qui credunt. Medium, per quod confertur, est verbum gratiæ, per quod remissio annunciatur. Medium, per quod accipitur, est contritum & humiliatum, quod remissionem capit, dum verbum gratiæ fide accipit.
units.tr: Therefore God, merciful and very gentle, freely forgives sins to us when we repent and truly believe, on account of the merit and satisfaction of Jesus Christ, his Son and our Mediator. We therefore obtain the forgiveness of sins in Christ, the only Mediator, Reconciler and Redeemer of all, to whom all the prophets bear witness, and all who believe receive the remission of sins through his name. The means by which it is conferred is the word of grace, by which remission is proclaimed. The means by which it is received is a contrite and humbled heart, which receives remission while it accepts the word of grace by faith.

units.la: Etsi vero in Christo nobis remissio per verbum reconciliationis annunciatur, & ut donum gratiæ fide accipitur. Requiritur autem a nobis conditio veræ & constantis resipiscentiæ, deinde ut reconciliaremur fratribus, in quos peccavimus, & ipsi etiam cœlestis patris clementiam imitantes debitoribus nostris ignoscamus, omniaq; illis debita remittamus. Hæc omnia non se perimunt, sed mutuo se ponunt.
units.tr: Yet although remission is proclaimed to us in Christ through the word of reconciliation, and is received by faith as a gift of grace, there is also required of us the condition of true and steadfast repentance; then that we be reconciled to the brothers against whom we have sinned, and that we, imitating the clemency of our heavenly Father, forgive our debtors and remit to them all that is owed. None of these things destroys the others; rather they mutually support one another.

units.la: II. Ex Novo Testamento ita argumentari videntur.
units.tr: II. From the New Testament they seem to argue thus:

units.la: Si Deus in salute nobis per Christum parta nullam veram pro delictis nostris satisfactionem accipere voluit; sed ea universa nobis resipiscen-tibus[?] bus condonare, nulla satisfactione, sed sola resipi-entia est causa condonationis, Ac quod antecedit est verum.
units.tr: If God, in the salvation obtained for us through Christ, was unwilling to accept any true satisfaction for our offences, but willed to forgive all these things to us when we repent, and repentance alone, with no satisfaction, is the cause of forgiveness; and what precedes is true.

units.la: 1. Quia ex sanctione novi foederis, quae legitur apud Jeremiam cap. 31. cō-stat, in eo eam vim esse, ut in humanis mentibus, divinae legi parendi, & voluntas & vires per ipsum Christum gignerentur, quod satis est ad erratorum veniam plenissimam consequendam. Inscriptio legis in cordibus nostris, quę ibi praecedit remissionem peccatorum, est poenitentia & resipiscentia.
units.tr: 1. Because from the sanction of the new covenant, which is read in Jeremiah ch. 31, it is established that this covenant has such force that in human minds both the will and the strength to obey the divine law are begotten through Christ himself, which is enough to obtain the most complete pardon of wrongdoers. The writing of the law in our hearts, which there precedes the remission of sins, is repentance and conversion.

units.la: EXAMEN.
units.tr: EXAMINATION.

units.la: Foedus gratiae Mediatoris sponsionem & persolutionem non rejicit, sed requirit. Hoc enim Deus gratuitum suum favorem, in æternum duraturum, promisit omnibus, in Christum Mediatorem & Sponsorem suum credentibus, sub conditione quidem illius fidei, & cum ea conjunctae syncerae pietatis: veruntamen neutrius tanquam propriis credentium viribus praestandae, sed tanquam ex gratuito illo favore ab ipso donandae.
units.tr: The covenant of grace does not reject a promise and payment on the part of the Mediator, but requires them. For God has promised his free favour, which is to last for ever, to all who believe in Christ as their Mediator and Surety. This is on condition of faith, and of sincere godliness joined with it. Yet neither of these is to be supplied by the believers' own powers, as if they were their own; it is to be given by God out of that free favour.

units.la: Promittuntur quidem in illo nobis tria, ex quorum ordine hic collocato, nihil est, quod quis concludat, resipi-scentiam esse priorem remissione, eo quod inscriptio legis praecedat. Ordo enim hic est inversus. Naturalis autem ordo hic est, quod primo omnium Deus nobis remittit peccata propter satisfactionem Christi. Deinde donat eis Spiritum S. qui primum illuminat mentes nostras cognitione gratiae Dei per satisfactionem Christi acquisitae, deinde vero renovat voluntatem, ad studium gratitudinis, pro beneficio liberationis per Christum.
units.tr: Three things are indeed promised to us in that covenant. From their order here, nothing follows that anyone may conclude, namely that repentance comes before remission because the writing of the law comes first. This order is reversed. The natural order is this: first of all God forgives us our sins on account of Christ's satisfaction. Then he gives us the Holy Spirit, who first enlightens our minds with the knowledge of God's grace obtained through Christ's satisfaction, and then renews our will to the eager pursuit of gratitude for the benefit of deliverance through Christ.

units.la: Et sane hic ordo ex parte notatur ipsis Prophetę verbis: Etsi enim remis-sionem peccatorum postremo loco commemorat, tamen illam praecedentibus annectit, per conjunctionem causalem inquiens: Ero enim proprium, &c. Deinde inscriptio legis in cordibus nostris, est renovatio voluntatis nostrae ad obediendum legib. Dei, quae est Dei actio in nobis; non ipsa nostra poenitentia, si proprie loquimur. Luc.1. præcursor Iesu Christi Ioannes, qui omnium viam paratū venit, præmissa salutis scientia ænde[?] destinatus fuit. At v.77. populo remissa peccata testatus est, propter viscera Misericordiæ Dei nostri: non propter satisfactionem Christi. Ideo etiam dicitur prædicasse aptissimum pœnitentiæ in remissionem peccatorum. Marc.1.4. Hic tantum fit mentio Misericordiæ Dei, & pœnitentiæ nostri.
units.tr: Indeed this order is partly marked by the prophet's own words. Although he mentions the forgiveness of sins last, he nevertheless links it with what goes before, using a causal conjunction when he says: For I will be their God, etc. Then the writing of the law in our hearts is the renewal of our will to obey the laws of God, which is God's action in us; strictly speaking, it is not our own repentance. In Luke 1 John, the forerunner of Jesus Christ, who came to prepare the way for all, was appointed to go before, with the knowledge of salvation. Yet at verse 77 he testified to the people that sins were forgiven them on account of the tender mercy of our God, not on account of Christ's satisfaction. Therefore he is also said to have preached the baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins (Mark 1:4). Here only mention is made of God's mercy and of our repentance.

units.la: EXAMEN
units.tr: EXAMINATION.

units.la: Canticum Zachariæ continet duas partes, prior est de Christo, posteriore de Johanne Baptista. In priore parte gratias agit Deo, pro tribus maximis beneficiis, missione Christi, Redemtione nostri per ipsum, sanctificatione. Memineris itaque & Christi, per quem Deus redemit populum suum, & excitavit cornu salutis nobis. In posteriore ait, Johanne fore Doctorem, qui auditores suos præparaturus sit Christo, & traditurus doctrinam Evangelii, de remissione peccatorum, & salute percipienda per Christum, ex Misericordia Dei, erga miseros peccatores. At Misericordia Dei non excludit Christum, neq; Christi satisfactionem. Unde & ipse Joannes prædicans baptismum pœnitentiæ in remissionem peccatorum populum ad Christum reiiciebat, atque ut in eum crederent, monebat. Volebat autem populum in Christum credere, ut in expiatorem peccatorum Mundi. Johan. 1. 29. Ecce Agnus ille Dei, qui tollit peccatum Mundi. Quasi dicat: Hæc est persona illa à Deo ordinata in victimam, ut scilicet instar Agni mactetur, & offeratur ad expiandum peccata nostra. Hic enim tollit & aufert peccata nostra, quatenus pro illis mactatus est in cruce. Hic portat expiandi gratia peccata, quatenus ea perfert in corpore suo super lignum. Hæc ratio non est omittenda, sed ceteris adjungenda.
units.tr: The canticle of Zechariah has two parts. The first is about Christ, the second about John the Baptist. In the first part he gives thanks to God for three very great benefits: the sending of Christ, our redemption through him, and sanctification. So remember both Christ, through whom God has redeemed his people and raised up a horn of salvation for us. In the second part he says that John will be a teacher who is to prepare his hearers for Christ and to deliver the doctrine of the Gospel: that sins are forgiven, and that salvation is to be received through Christ, out of God's mercy towards wretched sinners. But God's mercy does not exclude Christ, nor Christ's satisfaction. Hence John himself, preaching the baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, was directing the people to Christ, and warning them to believe in him. He wanted the people to believe in Christ as the expiator of the sins of the world (John 1:29): Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world. As if he were saying: this is that person appointed by God as the victim, so that, like a lamb, he might be slain and offered to expiate our sins. For he takes away and removes our sins, insofar as he was slain for them on the cross. He bears sins to be expiated, insofar as he carried them in his body upon the tree. This reason is not to be left out, but is to be added to the others.

units.la: III. Sic urgent satisfactionis rejectionem.
units.tr: III. Thus they press the rejection of satisfaction.

units.la: Si satisfactio interveniat in condonatione peccatorum nostrorum, non potest liberalis esse Dei remissio.
units.tr: If satisfaction intervenes in the pardoning of our sins, God's remission cannot be generous.

units.la: Ratio est: Quia nulla videtur esse creditoris liberalitas, si debitori non remittat nisi accepta ab alio satisfactione. Nam Novatio, ut vocant[?] Jurisri consulti, species est vera satisfactionis. Ergo e neganda est liberalis & indebita illa condo-tio a Deo facta, aut Christi pro peccatis nostris satisfactio.
units.tr: The reasoning is this: because there seems to be no generosity in a creditor if he does not remit the debt to the debtor unless satisfaction has been received from another. For novation, as the jurists call it, is a true kind of satisfaction. Therefore either the generous and undeserved pardon granted by God, or Christ's satisfaction for our sins, must be denied.

units.la: EXAMEN.
units.tr: EXAMINATION.

units.la: Neq; connexio, neq; disjunctio est cessaria. Quia & intervenit satisfactio Christi, & liberalis est condonatio peccatorum. Ideo & affirmanda est liberalis remissio, & non est neganda Christi pro peccatis satisfactio. Nec ratio habet probandi vires. Gratuita peccatorum nostrorum remissio manet eo, quia nulla proficiscitur à nobis satisfactio, sed mera est ac benigna Dei ACCEPTILATIO, quippe qui suum ud donum, quod nobis est largitus, co plenissimae solutionis acceptat. [?]terdum enim ipse debitor creditori [?]ersolvit, quod debet, cujus liberatio- nis caussa est PERSOLUTIO.
units.tr: Neither the connection nor the disjunction is necessary. For both Christ's satisfaction intervenes, and the pardon of sins is generous. So the generous remission is to be affirmed, and Christ's satisfaction for sins is not to be denied. Nor does the argument have any force in proving otherwise. The free remission of our sins remains free, because no satisfaction proceeds from us; it is a mere and kind ACCEPTILATION of God, since he accepts in place of full payment his own gift, which he has bestowed on us. For sometimes the debtor himself pays the creditor what he owes, and the cause of his release is PAYMENT.

units.la: Interdum vero creditor debitorem um liberat, substituto in ejus locum idoneo sponsore, vel alio quopiam, ii ipsemet tantùdem debebat, in quo su liberationis caussa est ACCEPTI-LATIO. LATIO. Et hæc est pactispecies, quam Clementissimus ille pater cœlestis nobiscum in Evangelico fœdere pepigit, in quo videlicet Christus Sponsor noster nihil suo nomine debens, sed nostrorum omnium & vitiorum & peccatorum persolvendis in carne nostra poenis sponte obstrictus, nos omnes Persolutione ad ultimum usque quadrantem factâ liberandos Patri obtulit. Ipse vero vicissim pater Apocham[illegible, ~3 letters]guine nostri sponsoris perscriptam tuens, nos per Acceptilationem liberat.
units.tr: But sometimes the creditor frees the debtor, a suitable surety or some other person being substituted in his place, who himself owed just as much; here the cause of release is ACCEPTILATION. And this is the kind of agreement which that most merciful heavenly Father made with us in the Gospel covenant. In it, Christ our Surety, owing nothing on his own account, but voluntarily bound to pay for all our vices and sins by the punishments borne in our flesh, offered us all to the Father to be freed by payment, the last farthing having been paid. Then the Father in turn, looking on the receipt written in the blood of our Surety, frees us by acceptilation.

units.la: Vides itaq;, munificentissimum & liberalissimum in eo Deum fuisse, quod cum nos ipsos, plectere jure posset, noluit tamen: sed impunitis nobis dimissis, filium suum pro nobis gravissimè percussit.
units.tr: You see, therefore, that God was most bounteous and most generous in this, that although he could rightly punish us, he did not wish to. Instead he let us go unpunished, and struck his own Son grievously for us.

units.la: Si ais, tunc hanc libertatem habere [?]ffe locum, si necesse sit aliquo modo nostra [?] puniri. At non esse necesse. Hoc pra objectum est dilutum, & demonstratum, justitiam Dei vindicatis peccatis, omnino requirere punitionem propter immutabile ejus decretum.
units.tr: If you say that this freedom could have a place only if our sins had to be punished in some way: but it is not necessary. This objection has already been refuted and shown, that the justice of God, in avenging sins, absolutely requires punishment on account of his unchangeable decree.

units.la: Ais, Is vere liberalis est, qui de suo donat. Deus Pater vere de suo largitus, quo nobis persolutum est. Non enim proprio filio pepercit, sed pro nobis tradidit eum in mortem.
units.tr: You say: he is truly generous who gives from his own. God the Father truly gave from his own, by which payment was made to us. For he did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us to death.

units.la: Sed dicis, duplicem conspici liberalitatem Dei, in nostrorum peccatorum remissione. Unam, quod gratuito nobis tantum debitum remiserit, deque suo jure decedere suâ sponte voluerit. Alteram, quod, ut nos tam insignis munificentiae fructum perciperemus, Unigenitum Filium suum nobis largitus est, per quem annuntiando salutis viam, eamque nobis in propria persona monstrando & confirmando, liberationem ab aeterna morte, & sempiternae vitae possessione, quib' gratuita haec delictorum nostrorum remissio continetur, re ipsa consequeremur.
units.tr: But you say that God's generosity is seen to be twofold in the remission of our sins. One is that he freely remitted so great a debt to us, and of his own accord chose to give up his right. The other is that, in order for us to receive the fruit of so remarkable a bounty, he gave us his only-begotten Son, through whom, by proclaiming the way of salvation, by showing and confirming it to us in his own person, we would in fact obtain deliverance from eternal death and possession of everlasting life, which are contained in this free remission of our offences.

units.la: Ego vero haec insufficientia & optimâ parte truncata dico, & Misericordiam & benignitatem, adeoq; impervestigabiles divitias gloriae gratiae Dei confidero ex DEi Verbo, in condona-tione tione meorum peccatorum, tum quoad Redemtione, tum quoad Applicationem.
units.tr: But I say that these things are insufficient and have lopped off the best part; I consider the mercy and kindness, and the unsearchable riches of the glory of God's grace, in the pardoning of my sins, from the Word of God, both as to Redemption and as to Application.

units.la: Quoad Redemtionem, Deus ante tempora sæcularia, priusquam jacerentur fundamenta Mundi, cum prævidisset futurà miseriam humani generis, ex merà gratiâ, Misericordiâ & dilectione fecit decretum, demittendo Filio Mediatore, ut fieret victima & propitiatio. 2. Timoth. 1. 9. Tit. 1. 2. Et in illo nos elegit, & prædestinavit. Ephes. 1. 4. 5. Commendavit enim Caritatem suam, quòd in plenitudine temporum filium unigenitum misit, & pro nobis omnibus tradidit. Rom. 5. 8. 1. Johan. 3. 9. Luc. 1. 78. & 54. Per viscera Misericordiæ, recordatus misericordiæ, & Johan. 3. 16. quòdq; illam victimam filii sui acceptavit, pro satisfactione & propitiatione pro peccatis totius Mundi. 1. Johan. 4. v. 10. & 1. Corinth. 1. 30. Factus est nobis à Deo Sapientia, Justitia, Redemtio, Sanctificatio. 2. Corinth. 5. verf. 19. Erat enim D E U S in C H R I S T O Mundum sibi reconcilians.
units.tr: As to Redemption: before the ages of the world, before the foundations of the world were laid, God, foreseeing the future misery of the human race, made the decree out of mere grace, mercy and love, by sending his Son as Mediator, so that he might become the victim and propitiation (2 Tim. 1:9; Titus 1:2). And in him he chose us and predestined us (Eph. 1:4, 5). For he commended his love, in that in the fullness of time he sent his only-begotten Son and gave him up for us all (Rom. 5:8; 1 John 3:9; Luke 1:78, 54). Through the tender mercy, remembering his mercy (and John 3:16), and because he accepted that sacrifice of his Son, as satisfaction and propitiation for the sins of the whole world (1 John 4:10; 1 Cor. 1:30). Christ was made to us by God wisdom, righteousness, redemption and sanctification (2 Cor. 5:19). For God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself.

units.la: Quoad applicationem, multis modis commendatur gratia & benignitas Dei. Deus enim proponit filium suum placamentum in sanguine ejus. Rom.3.25. Ante faciem omnium populorum, Luc.2.32[?] instituens & confervans ministerium reconciliationis, 2.Corint.5.18. Et Deus omnis gratiæ vocat nos ad suam gloriam, 1.Pet.5.10. Gal.1.2[?] Vocavit & me per suam gratiam. Rom.8.28. Qui secundum propositum vocati sumus sancti. 2.Tim.1.9. Qui nos liberavit, & vocavit vocatione sancta, non secundum opera nostra, sed secundum suum propositum & gratiam. Col.1.12. Idoneos nos reddit ad participationem sortis sanctorum, dando resipiscentiam. Act.5.31. Dando fidem. 1.Tim.1.14. Superabundavit misericordia in fide, 2.Thess.2.16. Dilexit nos & dedit consolationem & Spem bonam in gratia, &c. Ephes.2.v.4. &c. Deus igitur, qui dives est in Misericordia, propter nimiam suam caritatem, qua dilexit nos, cum mortui essemus in peccatis, convivificavit nos cum Christo. Unde Ephes.1.7. habemus remisremissionem peccatorum per sanguinem Christi secundum divitias gratiæ ejus. 1. Johan. 3. 1. Videte qualem caritatem nobis dedit, ut filii Dei nominemur. Col. 1. 13. Eripuit nos & transtulit in regnum Dilecti filii sui. Actor. 5. 31. ad dandam remissionem peccatorum, &c. Sed hic subsisto, quia abys-sum divitiarum, gloriæ, gratiæ Dei non possum exhaurire, imò ne pervidere quidem.
units.tr: As regards application, the grace and kindness of God are commended in many ways. For God sets forth his Son as a propitiation in his blood (Rom. 3:25), before the face of all peoples (Luke 2:32), instituting and preserving the ministry of reconciliation (2 Cor. 5:18). And the God of all grace calls us to his glory (1 Pet. 5:10); (Gal. 1:...) "He called me also through his grace"; (Rom. 8:28) "who are called according to his purpose, the saints"; (2 Tim. 1:9) "who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace"; (Col. 1:12) "he has made us fit to share in the inheritance of the saints," giving repentance (Acts 5:31), giving faith (1 Tim. 1:14), "the grace of our Lord abounded with faith" (2 Thess. 2:16); "he has loved us and given us good consolation and good hope in grace," etc. (Eph. 2:4, etc.). God therefore, who is rich in mercy, because of his great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead in sins, has made us alive together with Christ. Hence (Eph. 1:7) we have "the forgiveness of sins through the blood of Christ, according to the riches of his grace." (1 John 3:1) "See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God." (Col. 1:13) "He has delivered us and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son." (Acts 5:31) "to give forgiveness of sins," etc. But here I stop, because I cannot exhaust, nor even fully look into, the abyss of God's riches, glory and grace.

units.la: Rursum regetis. Quorsum inutile illud circuitu? cum simplici debuit remissione, & debitorem liberare & largitatem suam ostendere creditor posset? Et cum Deus sine ulla justitia immunitione id facere posset?
units.tr: Again you will object: "Why that roundabout way? Could the creditor not have released the debtor by a simple remission and shown his generosity? And could God not have done this without any diminution of justice?"

units.la: Ideo opus fuit hoc, quem dicis, circuitu, ut ostenderet Deus, quanto odio peccatum persequatur, qui, ut illud puniret, ne proprio quidem, carissimóq; filio pepercisset, sed eum miserabili morte excruciandum & necădum tradidisset, atq; hac ratione curasset, ut à peccando in posterum retraheremur. Utrumque enim verum est. Evangeli-um concionatur, Deum dilexisse Mũ-dum, & suam nobis caritatem cōmen-dasse, cum inimici ejus essem"; Immota quoq; sententia legis stat, Maledicti, qui non permanserit in omnibus, quae scripta sunt in libro legis. Item: Faciens Misericordiam his, qui custodiunt mandata mea; &c.
units.tr: This circuitous way, as you call it, was therefore needed, so that God might show how greatly he hates sin: he, in order to punish it, did not spare even his own and dearest Son, but handed him over to be tortured and put to death by a miserable death, and by this means took care that we would be withdrawn from sinning in future. For both things are true. The Gospel proclaims that God loved the world and commended his love to us, when we were his enemies; and the unchanging sentence of the law stands firm: "Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of the law" (Gal. 3:10); likewise: "showing mercy to those who keep my commandments" (Exod. 20:6), etc.

units.la: Proinde nihil est, quod quidam dicunt, Deum esse liberrimum, nulli legi, ne suae [?] quidem subjectum, sed posse eum gratia & misericordia peccatores complecti, licet legis sententiae contrarium sanciat. At lex est immota Regula justitiae: & qui ponerentur duae contradictoriae voluntates in Deo? Inquit autem Malach. 3. 6. Ego Deus, & non mutor. Et impossibile est, legem Dei solvi aut interire. Matth. 5. 18. Extra igitur Christum, pro peccatis victimam, nulla gratia Dei aut Misericordia erga peccatores excogitari recte potest.
units.tr: Therefore it is no argument, what some say: that God is entirely free, subject to no law, not even to his own, but that he can embrace sinners with grace and mercy, although the sentence of the law decrees the contrary. But the law is the unchanging rule of justice; and how could two contradictory wills be posited in God? Indeed he says (Mal. 3:6): "I am God, and I do not change." And "it is impossible for the law of God to be dissolved or to perish" (Matt. 5:18). Therefore, apart from Christ, the victim for sins, no grace or mercy of God toward sinners can rightly be devised.

units.la: Ergo nihil est, quod dicis, sine justitiae divinae imminutione, resipiscentibus peccata, sine satisfactione remitti potuisse: & Deum, se odio peccatum prosequi, satis ostendere, cum, nisi resipiscamus, & peccatis relictis, justitiae deinceps studeamus, nos graviter puniat, atque aeternae morti mancipatos relinquat. Merito puniuntur & impe-nitentes victimam Christi rejicientes, & sanguinem ejus pedibus conculcan-tes, sed ut fiat condonatio peccatorum, fuit necesse sponsore nostrum, in quem Deus conjecerat iniquitates omnium nostrum, dolores nostros portare, & poenas nostris peccatis debitas perferre, ut ejus obedientia & meritum credenti-bus per fidem in ipsum imputaretur. Sed prolixior in hoc argumento meditando fui, ad aliud me converte.
units.tr: So it is no good for you to say that without any diminution of divine justice, sins could have been remitted to those who repent, without satisfaction. And that God shows well enough that he pursues sin with hatred, since, unless we repent and, leaving sins behind, henceforth strive after righteousness, he punishes us severely and leaves us given over to eternal death. Rightly are the impenitent punished, who reject Christ's victim and trample his blood underfoot; but for the forgiveness of sins to take place, it was necessary for our surety, upon whom God had laid the iniquities of us all, to bear our griefs and to undergo the punishments due to our sins, so that his obedience and merit might be imputed to believers through faith in him. But I have been too lengthy in meditating on this subject; I turn now to another.

units.la: CAPITIS I. SECTIO III.
units.tr: CHAPTER I, SECTION III.

units.la: Si pro peccatis satisfactione est opus, nobis peccatoribus erit necessario pereundum.
units.tr: If satisfaction for sins is necessary, we sinners must necessarily perish.

units.la: At nobis non est necessario omnibus pereundum.
units.tr: But we do not all necessarily have to perish.

units.la: Ergo pro peccatis satisfactione non est opus.
units.tr: Therefore satisfaction for sins is not necessary.

units.la: 1. Propositionis connexio sic primo confirmatur.
units.tr: 1. The connection of the premise is first confirmed as follows.

units.la: Si Deus aut non potuisset, aut noluisset, citra veram aliquam pro delictis nostris satisfactionem nobis ignoscere, nos ipsi omnino ei satisfacere debuissemus. Neque enim aliquid Deo dr[?]ebamus, quod alius, quisquilicet non deliquisset, & ita nihil ipse divinæ justitiæ deberet, pro nobis præstare posset. Pœna peccato ipsius DEI voluntate constituta, æterna Mors est; quæ cum corporalis pœna sit, à nemine, præter quam ab eo ipso, qui peccavit, præstari potest. Pecuniaria quidem pœna, unius delicto debita, ab alio præstari queunt. Unius enim pecunia alterius effici potest. Et cum quis in se alterius pecuniariam pœnam transfert, perinde censetur, ac si delinquens eam pecuniam plenissimo jure donasset.
units.tr: If God could not, or would not, forgive our offences without some true satisfaction, we ourselves would have had to satisfy him altogether. For we would owe God nothing that another, who had not sinned himself, could render on our behalf, and so he who owed nothing to divine justice could make it good for us. The penalty for sin, fixed by the will of God himself, is eternal death; since this is a bodily penalty, it can be paid by no one except the very person who sinned. A monetary penalty owed for one man's offence, however, can be paid by another. For one man's money can become another's. And when someone transfers another's monetary penalty to himself, he is regarded as if the offender had given that money to him with full right.

units.la: At mors unius, sive alia quacunque corporis vexatio alterius effici non potest, neque unquam vel lege vel consuetudine receptum fuit, ut pœnam, quam quis corpore [?]ere teneatur, alius quisquis tandem ille sit, pro eo pendere posit.
units.tr: But one man's death, or any other bodily suffering, cannot be transferred to another, nor has it ever been accepted, by law or by custom, that anyone whatsoever should pay on another's behalf the penalty which that person was bound to bear in his body.

units.la: Ergo rationis lumen, quo DEUS nos donavit, aperte ostendit, non debere, nec posse corporalem pœnam, quam unus debeat, ab alio persolvi.
units.tr: Therefore the light of reason, by which God has endowed us, clearly shows that a bodily penalty which one person owes ought neither to be nor can be paid by another.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Sicut hic non disputo de absolutâ Dei potestate, an possit aliquem sine verâ justitiâ absolvere; ita hic nolim lumen naturalis rationis in multis obscuratum in consilium vocari, cum agitur de Mysterio illo magno reconciliationis nostræ; sed judicetur ex verbo revelato. Pau-
units.tr: Just as I am not here disputing God's absolute power, whether he could absolve anyone without true justice, so I would not wish to call in the light of natural reason, which is obscured in many matters, when we are dealing with that great mystery of our reconciliation; rather let it be judged by the revealed word. Paul...

units.la: Paulus, 1. Cor. 2. 7. Loquimur, inquit, sapientiam Dei latentem in mysterio, id est, occultam illam, quam praefinierat Deus ante saecula in gloriam nostram: quam nemo Principum saeculi huius cognovit. Nam si cognovissent, nequaquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent. Praedicamus, sicut scriptum est: quae oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis venerunt, quae paravit Deus his, qui diligunt eum. Nobis autem Deus revelavit per Spiritum suum. Loquatur igitur hic Spiritus Dei, non ratio hominum. Coloss. 1.26. Est enim Mysterium hoc absconditum a ætatibus, nunc autem illud patefactum est sanctis ejus. Nempe, quod paulo ante dixit, quod in Christo placuerit Patri, ut omnis plenitudo inhabitaret. Et pace per sanguinem crucis ejus facta per eum reconciliare omnia sibi.
units.tr: Paul, 1. Cor. 2. 7.: We speak, he says, of the wisdom of God hidden in a mystery, that is, that hidden wisdom which God had predestined before the ages for our glory; which none of the rulers of this age knew. For if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory. We preach, as it is written: what eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man, which God has prepared for those who love him. But God has revealed it to us through his Spirit. Let the Spirit of God speak here, then, and not human reason. Col. 1. 26.: For this mystery is hidden from the ages, but now has been made manifest to his saints. Namely, what he said a little before: that it pleased the Father that all fullness should dwell in Christ, and, by making peace through the blood of his cross, to reconcile all things to himself through him.

units.la: Fateor prolixè, nobis omnibus satis-faciendum & pereundum, ppter[?] peccata nostra fuisse. Quod autem non teneamur jam satisfacere & luere poenas, in causa est Sponsor noster Christus, qui se loco nostro stitit, & a nobis persolvit. Nego igitur nobis non pereuntibus posse justitiæ Dei satisfieri. Indubitatum est, legem promittere Misericordiam illis, qui diligūt Deum, & custodiunt mandata ejus: illis vero, quibus non permanent in omnibus, quæ scripta sunt in lege, æternam maledicti-onem denunciare. Certum & hoc est, normam illam justitiæ in Deo, quæ in lege patefacta est, æternam, immotam & immutabilem esse, Matth. 5. 18. Non igitur vult, necesse est Deum sine vera aliquâ justitiâ interveniente, justificare & peccata remittere, sive non imputare. Dixit enim, abominationem coram Deo esse, justificare impium sine justitiâ, Prov. 17. 15. Is. 5. 23. Et ipsum negare non potest.
units.tr: I freely admit that we all had to make satisfaction and to perish on account of our sins. But that we are not now bound to make satisfaction and to pay the penalties is due to our Surety, Christ, who stood in our place and paid on our behalf. I deny, therefore, that the justice of God can be satisfied while we are not perishing. It is beyond doubt that the law promises mercy to those who love God and keep his commandments, but to those who do not persevere in all the things written in the law it threatens eternal curse. It is also certain that that norm of justice in God which is revealed in the law is eternal, unchanging and immutable, Matth. 5. 18. Therefore it is necessary that God should not justify and remit sins, or not impute them, without some true justice intervening. For he said that it is an abomination before God to justify the wicked without justice, Prov. 17. 15. Is. 5. 23. And he cannot deny it himself.

units.la: Quia igitur illam legis justitiam, cui promittitur vita æterna, nec habem[?], nec præstare possumus in hac vita, & tamen Deus proposuerat nos in gratiam recipere & nobis peccata condonare; non autem poterat fieri solutio, destructio & interitus legis à se latæ, Matth. 5. Rom. 3. vlt. facta ita est translatio legis, Hebr. 7. 12. in Mediatorem, scilicet Filium Dei, hoc modo, ut pro nobis sub lege factus, legi satisfaceret, solvendo pœnas nas pro peccatis totius Mundi, & præ-stando perfectissimam obedientiam, ut esset sancta victima: itaque nobis esset vera & perfecta justitia, juxta normam voluntatis divinæ, quâ gratia & Misericordia Dei credentes justificet & ac-ceptet ad vitam æternam[?].
units.tr: Since, then, we neither have nor can render in this life that justice of the law to which eternal life is promised, and yet God had purposed to receive us into favour and to grant us forgiveness of sins, and since the law he had himself given could not be dissolved, destroyed or brought to an end (Matth. 5. Rom. 3. last verse), a transfer of the law was made (Heb. 7. 12.) to the Mediator, namely the Son of God, in this way: that, made under the law on our behalf, he should satisfy the law by paying our penalties for the sins of the whole world and by rendering most perfect obedience, so that he might be a holy victim; and thus there would be for us true and perfect justice, according to the norm of the divine will, by which God justifies and accepts believers to eternal life through grace and mercy.

units.la: Quia verò hæc satisfactio debebat talis esse, quæ satisfaceret ad redemptionem omnium nostrum, ideo oportuit personam Mediatoris esse Deum & hominem, ut pretium esset æquivalens.
units.tr: But since this satisfaction had to be such as would make satisfaction for the redemption of all of us, it was therefore necessary that the person of the Mediator be God and man, so that the price would be of equal value.

units.la: CHRISTUS ergo Sponsor & Mediator noster est causa condonationis peccatorum nostrorum SUO MERITO. Primum quod Deus Pater respicit, & propter quos credentes gratis suam gratiam à peccatis suis absolvit. Hinc scriptura dicit, CHRISTUM propter peccata nostra esse mortuum, itè pro peccatis mortuum, & impiis mortuus, passum pro peccatis, ἱλασμόν[?] esse pro peccatis, seipsum dedisse ἀντίλυτρον[?] & multis. Unde solus CHRISTUS docetur satisfecisse pro culpâ & pœnâ, ita ut nihil reliquum sit nobis credentibus, nostris vel passionibus, vel satisfactionibus, ad expianda peccata.
units.tr: Christ, therefore, our Surety and Mediator, is the cause of the forgiveness of our sins by HIS MERIT. First, it is what God the Father regards, and for whose sake he freely absolves believers from their sins by his grace. Hence Scripture says that Christ died for our sins, died indeed for sins, and, dead for the impious, suffered for sins, is the propitiation [ἱλασμόν] for sins, and gave himself as a ransom [ἀντίλυτρον] for many. Whence Christ alone is taught to have satisfied for guilt and punishment, so that nothing remains for believers, by their own sufferings or satisfactions, to expiate sins.

units.la: [no printed footnotes]
units.tr: [no printed footnotes]

units.la: Deinde CHRISTUS non ita me-ruit, ut per nos, vel per alios, ea quae ad salutem nostram ac justificationé pertinent, efficerentur, sed ea & effecit, & adhuc efficit, in quibus justificatio & salus nostra consistit; qualia sunt, liberatio à peccato, ira Dei, Diabolo & morte, & applicatio horum beneficiorum. Sic igitur dicit scriptura, nos redemtos esse sanguine Agni, sanatos livore ejus, nos per ipsum redemtos à maledictione legis; purgatione peccatorum facta p sanguine ejus, ipsum ingressu per proprium sanguinem & aeternam redemtionem invenisse, adeoq; sanguinem Jesu nos purgare ab omnib. peccatis nostris.
units.tr: Next, Christ did not so merit that the things which pertain to our salvation and justification should be brought about through us or through others; rather he both brought about and still brings about those things in which our justification and salvation consist, such as deliverance from sin, from the wrath of God, from the Devil and from death, and the application of these benefits.
