Sed gratiam perpetuo opponit Apostolus operibus, hoc est, merito nostro; & fidei in Christum, comitem eam ac sociam facit. Optimè profecto convenit gratiæ Dei cum Merito Christi Fide apprehenso, non ideo tantum, quod Meritum illud non sit nostrum, sed Christi, hoc est, ipsiusmet Dei, sed vel multò magis, quod Christi satisSatisfactio & meritum illud alienum ex Dei gratia sit, meraq; liberalitate. Non enim pepercit Deus filio suo, sed pro nobis tradidit eum in morte. Rom. 8. 32.
units.tr: That would be true if the merits of Christ were set directly against the grace of God. But the Apostle always sets grace against works, that is, against our own merit, and makes faith in Christ its companion and partner. Certainly the grace of God agrees very well with the merit of Christ, received by faith. This is not only because that merit is not ours but Christ's, that is, God's own, but much more because the satisfaction of Christ and that foreign merit come from the grace of God and from pure generosity. For God did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all to death. Rom. 8. 32.

units.la: Atq; hac de causa fit, ut in Christi illa Satisfactione & Merito ipsius magis eluceat gratia Dei, majorq; appareat, quàm si sine ullo merito, vel nostro, vel alieno, quo satisfiat ipsius justitiæ, nos justificet. Optimè igitur consistit gratia, qua nos justificat Deus, cum merito illo, & λύτρῳ[?], quod ipse Deus de suo dedit.
units.tr: For this reason, in Christ's satisfaction and his merit, the grace of God shines forth all the more, and it appears greater than if God justified us without any merit, ours or another's, by which his justice might be satisfied. The grace by which God justifies us therefore agrees very well with that merit and with the ransom [λύτρον] that God himself gave from his own.

units.la: Quod si autem λύτρον illud & pretium redemptionis ab ipso Deo non dissolveretur, tum profecto in merito illo ac λύτρῳ[?], non adeo conspiceretur gratia.
units.tr: But if that ransom [λύτρον] and price of redemption were not given by God himself, then indeed in that merit and ransom [λύτρον] the grace would not be so clearly seen.

units.la: II. Ex sententia vestra sequitur, Deum aut non potuisse aut noluisse, nulla vero pro peccatis nostris accepta Satisfactione, ea nobis liberaliter condonare.
units.tr: II. From your position it follows that God either could not or would not forgive us our sins freely, without receiving any satisfaction for them.

units.la: Quod si dicitis, eum non potuisse, Majestatem ejus, authoritatemq; supremam ac infinitam imminutis, & certis limitibus circumscriptam coercetis.
units.tr: For if you say that he could not, you diminish his majesty and supreme and infinite authority, and confine him within fixed limits.

units.la: Si vero noluisse dicitis, propriam ejus & veram Misericordiam non obscuratis solum sed & funditus deletis.
units.tr: But if you say that he would not, you not only obscure but utterly destroy his own true mercy.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Agnoscimus Dei potestatem & authoritatem non modo esse supremam & inde pendentem, sed etiam universalem, perfectam, liberrimam. Interim nulla species divinæ potestatis ad eas res pertinet, quæ a naturæ divinæ necessitate pendent, vel absolutè, vel saltem ex hypothesi divinæ voluntatis jam certo ad hanc vel illā partem determinatæ. Etenim fieri non potest, ut Deus contra suam ipsius voluntatē semel definitam, nedum contra suam ipsius na-turam, quicquam jure statuat. ut supra est plurib. disputatur. Ideo igitur hoc, de quo agimus, non potuit, quia contra naturam ejus justam & voluntate fuit.
units.tr: We acknowledge that the power and authority of God is not only supreme and dependent on nothing else, but also universal, perfect and most free. Yet no form of divine power extends to those things that depend on the necessity of the divine nature, either absolutely, or at least on the supposition of a divine will already certainly determined to this or that side. For God cannot decree anything rightly against his own will once determined, much less against his own nature, as has been discussed above in many places. Therefore this, of which we are speaking, could not be done, because it was contrary to his nature, just as it was contrary to his will.

units.la: 2. Agnoscimus deinde, in Deo ef-fe MISERICORDIAM & CLEMEN-TIAM miseris succurrendi: sed & VO-LUNTATEM vindicantem hominum scelera, quibus irascitur, agnoscimus. Inconsequens est, Deum propterea non esse MISERICORDEM, quod nobis peccata nostra non condonet, nisi præ-stita a ꝑprio filio sibi satisfactione. Imo Dei gratia & misericordia erga genus nostrū hinc magis elucescit, uti supra.
units.tr: Next, we acknowledge that there is in God MERCY and CLEMENCY to help the wretched; but we also acknowledge a WILL that punishes the wickedness of men, with which he is angry. It does not follow that God is therefore not MERCIFUL because he does not forgive us our sins unless satisfaction has been made to him by his own Son. Indeed, the grace and mercy of God toward our race shine forth all the more from this, as above.

units.la: III. Si Christus pro nobis dicitur vere satisfecisse, Dei vera justitia, hoc est, rectitudo & aequitas penitus labefactatur & convellitur: sed neq; illa justitia, quae est Dei in delictis puniendis severitas, qua adversus contumaces uti solet, illa ex parte conservatur; aut retinetur; sed ejus loco, temeraria quaedam immanitas constituitur.
units.tr: III. If Christ is said to have truly satisfied for us, the true justice of God, that is, his rectitude and equity, is utterly weakened and overthrown; but neither is that justice, which is God's severity in punishing sins, by which he is accustomed to deal with the stubborn, preserved on that side or retained; rather, in its place some reckless savagery is set up.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Omninò falsum est connexum hoc. Manet naturae divinae integritas & rectitudo, quia aequitatem & clementiam[?] tum erga se, tum erga nos homines sanctissimè observat, dum Deus ipse sic mundum dilexit, ut filium suum mise-rit, ut omnis qui credit in eum, nō per-eat, sed habeat vitam aeternam, & eos qui non credunt, condemnat, omnes. Hic-vide ejus judicium.
units.tr: This connection is altogether false. The integrity and righteousness of the divine nature remain, because God most holily observes justice and mercy both toward himself and toward us men, since God himself so loved the world that he sent his Son, so that everyone who believes in him should not perish but have eternal life, and he condemns all who do not believe. See here his judgment.

units.la: Jus Deus unicuiq; suum convenien-ter tribuit, prout illi personae, q[?] Deus in aliqua actione sustinet, consentaneum est. Gerit autem persona jam Patris, jam Domini, jam judicis, jam Servatoris. Non modò constituit mercedem pie-tati, sed etiam contumacibus irrogat poenas. Quippe, qui nō modo promi-sit, verum etiam comminatus est. Justiti-am vero vindicantem, dum juste in fi-lio, Sponsore nostro, pro suo benepla-cito exercuit peccata nostra, quæ ipsi imputata erant, puniendo; gratiam & misericordiam suam admirabilem in nobis peccatoribus parcendis incredibiliter declaravit. Sed & hac de re supra.
units.tr: God rightly gives each his due, as is fitting to the person which God sustains in any action. Now the person bears at one time the Father's, at another the Lord's, at another the judge's, at another the Saviour's role. He not only appoints a reward for godliness but also inflicts punishments on the stubborn, for he not only promised but also threatened. Indeed, while he exercised justice in vindicating, by justly punishing our sins, which were imputed to him, in his Son, our Surety, according to his good pleasure, he also declared incredibly his admirable grace and mercy in sparing us sinners. But I have spoken of this matter above as well.

units.la: IV. Ubi hujus vestrae sententia Christi glo-ria non minima ex parte obscuratur. Nam & ejus erga nos Caritatem, in morte pro nobis sub-eunda deprimit: & ipsius proprium ac peculiare munus Evangelii cum annuntiandi, tum con-firmandi, Apostolis & Prophetis pene ex æquo fit commune & æternæ salutis nobis danda potestas, quam ut homo habet, illi ut homini, magna cum impietate & sacrilegio adimitur atq; eripitur. Nec interea quomodo morte & obedientia sua cunctis, qui ipsius dicto audientes fuerint, omnium peccatorum veniam pepererit, vel agnoscitur, vel recte intelligitur.
units.tr: IV. Where this opinion of yours obscures the glory of Christ to no small degree. For it both diminishes his love toward us, in undergoing death for us; and the proper and peculiar office of his Gospel, both to announce and to confirm, becomes almost equally common to the Apostles and Prophets, and the power of giving eternal salvation to us, which he has as man, is taken away and snatched from him as man, with great impiety and sacrilege. Nor is it meanwhile acknowledged or rightly understood how by his death and obedience he has won forgiveness of all sins for all who have listened to his word.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: 1. Gravis hæc est accusatio. Audiantur rei: Gloriam Christi non obscuramus, [?]um ad gloriam ejus credimus, & dici-ius, Christum Jesum dando seipsum pretium redemtionis pro peccatis no-ris, [?] nobis satisfecisse. Nō deprimimus caritatem ineffabilem filii Dei, qui x nimia caritate, qua nos complexus est, animam suam pro nobis dedit, & sanguinem suum effudit in remissione peccatorum nostrorum. Nemo enim majorem caritatem habet, quam qui vitam suam pro alio profundit, Manifesta est hæc calumnia.
units.tr: 1. This is a grave accusation. Let the accused be heard: we do not obscure the glory of Christ, since we believe and teach to his glory that Jesus Christ, by giving himself as the price of redemption for our sins, has made satisfaction for us. We do not diminish the ineffable love of the Son of God, who, out of the great love with which he embraced us, gave his soul for us and poured out his blood for the remission of our sins. For no one has greater love than he who lays down his life for another. This calumny is plain.

units.la: 2. Deinde proprium Christi munus [?]non nos, sed illi faciunt commune cum Prophetis & Apostolis. Tradunt enim, Christum esse Servatorem nostrum, quatenus æternæ salutis viam ipse nobis annuntiavit; & voluntatem Patris de redemtione generis humani nobis exposuit. Sed Prophetæ & Apostoli eandem viam salutis, & Patris voluntatem nobis annuntiarunt, & non paucos suorum auditorum servasse dicuntur.
units.tr: 2. Next, it is not we but they who make Christ's proper office common with the Prophets and Apostles. For they teach that Christ is our Saviour in so far as he himself announced to us the way of eternal salvation and set forth to us the will of the Father concerning the redemption of mankind. But the Prophets and Apostles also announced the same way of salvation and the will of the Father to us, and are said to have saved not a few of their hearers.

units.la: Neq; refert, quod Prophetæ non nisi de ventura salute, & quidem obscurius prophetarunt, Apostoli vero nomine Christi tanquam ejus legati prae-dicarunt. Satis est utrosque eandem salutis viam annuntiasse: cum & ipse CHRISTUS legatus-Patris sui dicatur. Ergo quoad annuntiationem salutis officium salvationis ipsi cum Prophetis & Apostolis Christo communereddunt.
units.tr: Nor does it matter that the Prophets prophesied only of the salvation to come, and that rather obscurely, whereas the Apostles preached in the name of Christ as his envoys. It is enough that both announced the same way of salvation, since Christ himself is called the envoy of his Father. Therefore, as regards the announcement of salvation, they make the office of saving common to Christ together with the Prophets and Apostles.

units.la: Quod attinet ad confirmationem annuntiatae salutis, nō nos, sed ipsi Christi Servatoris munus commune faciunt. Docent enim, SERVATOREM noftrū esse CHRISTUM eatenus etiam, quatenus nobis viam salutis suo exemplo in sua ipsius persona ostenderit, & miraculis, sanguine & morte sua confirmarit & obsignarit: At non tantum Christi, sed etiam sanctorum Prophetarum & Apostolorum exempla nobis in scriptura imitanda proponuntur: & non est dubium, plurima a Prophetis & Apostolis miracula ad doctrinae ipsorum confirmationem edita fuisse. Deniq; plurimi Martyres suo etiam sanguine veritate coelestis doctrinae obsignantes, Ecclesiae commodis non parum com-modaverunt. Ratione igitur hujus confirmationis salvationis munus ipsi Christo cum sanctis commune faciunt.
units.tr: As regards the confirmation of the salvation announced, they make it an office common not to us but to Christ the Saviour himself. For they teach that Christ is our Saviour also in so far as he showed us the way of salvation by his example in his own person, and confirmed and sealed it by his miracles, his blood and his death. But not only the examples of Christ but also those of the holy Prophets and Apostles are set before us in Scripture to be imitated, and there is no doubt that many miracles were performed by the Prophets and Apostles to confirm their teaching. Finally, many martyrs, sealing the truth of heavenly doctrine even with their blood, have not a little benefited the interests of the Church. Therefore, by reason of this confirmation, they make the office of salvation common to Christ together with the saints.

units.la: 3. Nequaquam Christo homini, qui & verus est Deus in una persona, adimimus potestatem aeternae salutis nobis dandae, quam etiam ideo a patre accepit, quod pretium redemtionis pro nobis seipsum Deo Patri dederit, & obediens patri usque ad mortem crucis, seipsum Patri hostiam obtulerit in odore bonae fragrantiae. Christus itaque SPON-SOR & SERVATOR noster peccata nostra suo sanguine expiavit, & accepta a patre plenissima potestate in caelo & terra, nobis credentib. in novissimo illo die daturus est vitam aeternam: ipse abolita morte, omnibusque hostibus sibi subiectis, nos ab omni miseria liberatos, in societatem caelestis gloriae est adducturus.
units.tr: 3. By no means do we take from Christ, who is both true God and man in one person, the power of giving eternal salvation to us, which he also received from the Father for this reason, that he gave himself as the price of redemption for us to God the Father, and, being obedient to the Father even to the death of the cross, offered himself to the Father as a sacrifice of sweet-smelling savour. Christ therefore, our Surety and Saviour, expiated our sins with his blood, and, having received from the Father the fullest power in heaven and on earth, he will give eternal life to us who believe on that last day; having abolished death, and with all enemies subjected to himself, he will lead us, freed from all misery, into the fellowship of heavenly glory.

units.la: 4. Posita etiam satisfactione Christi, non efficitur, nos non agnoscere vel recte intelligere, quomodo morte & obedientia sua Christus, cunctis qui ipsi obediunt, veniam peccatorum pepe-rerit[?].
units.tr: 4. Even when the satisfaction of Christ is affirmed, it does not follow that we do not acknowledge or rightly understand how Christ, by his death and obedience, has won forgiveness of sins for all who obey him.

units.la: Etc.
units.tr: Etc.

units.la: Etenim ex verbo Dei agnoscimus CHRISTUM obdientia & morte sua expiasse peccata nostra, & nos effuso[?] suo sanguine in remissionem peccatorum DEO reconciliasse, & non modo hoc effecisse, verum etiam impetrasse nobis Spiritum sanctum, regeneratem nos per vocationem efficacem, illuminantem mentes nostras fidejustificante, & voluntatem nostram excitantem ad studium bonorum operum, ut sicut ipse Christus excitatus postea est ex mortuis in gloriam patris, ita & nos in novitate vitę ambulemus, ut enervetur corpus peccati, ne posthac serviamus peccato. Novimus enim sanguinem Christi purgare conscientiam nostram à mortuis operibus ad serviendum Deo vivo; & Christum peccata nostra pertulisse in corpore suo super lignum, ut peccatis mortui, justitiæ viveremus.
units.tr: For from the word of God we acknowledge that Christ by his obedience and death expiated our sins, and that by pouring out his blood for the remission of sins he reconciled us to God; and that he not only accomplished this but also obtained for us the Holy Spirit, regenerating us through effectual calling, enlightening our minds, justifying by faith, and stirring up our will to zeal for good works, so that, as Christ himself was afterwards raised from the dead to the glory of the Father, so we too may walk in newness of life, that the body of sin may be made powerless and we may no longer serve sin. For we know that the blood of Christ cleanses our conscience from dead works to serve the living God; and that Christ bore our sins in his body on the tree, so that, dead to sins, we might live to righteousness.

units.la: V. Absurdum: & praeparatio ad alteram hujus Assertionis partem.
units.tr: V. An absurdity, and preparation for the other part of this assertion.

units.la: Aliud malum, ex affirmata Christi satisfactione, pullulat, ꝗ[?] omnium est nocentissimum, nimirum omne pieta-
units.tr: Another evil, springing from the affirmed satisfaction of Christ, is the most harmful of all, namely that all zeal for piety

units.la: Studium, ut experientia ipsa declarat, frigescit atque exstinguitur; dum tant[?] homines jam reipsa ejustos[?] esse, quia licet omnium suorum peccatorum universa ma[?] divina justitia persoluta fuerint.
units.tr: Zeal, as experience itself declares, grows cold and is extinguished, while men already think themselves in fact righteous, because, although the whole of all their sins has been paid to divine justice.

units.la: Item ajunt: Ut per speciem sanctimonia vitae bilienda[?], omnis vera sanctitas convelleretur: humani generis hoste versutissimo persuasi prudentes, imputationem justitia Christi exstitarunt; per quam scilicet nobis, licet adhuc [?]catis servissimus, ea sanctimonia adscribatur.
units.tr: Likewise they say: that under the appearance of holiness of life, all true sanctity would be overthrown; the most crafty enemy of the human race persuaded the prudent to devise the imputation of Christ's righteousness, through which, namely, that holiness is ascribed to us, although we are still slaves to sin.

units.la: Clamant itaque adversarii, doctrinam de merito & satisfactione Christi, aut prorsus tollere, aut vehementer saltem impedire studium sanc-monia, sine qua nemo Deum videbit, Heb.12. dum nimirum homines persuasi, pro omnibus peccatis Deo planissime esse satisfactum, opinantur jam se vere justos esse alienâ justitiâ, nec posse gratia Dei excidere, quamvis indulgeant [?]eleribus: nec interea animadvertunt, Deum omnino exigere conditionem resipiscentiae, sine qua omnia[?] peccata remitti possunt. Jes.1.16.17.18. Zech.18.21.22. Actor.2.20. & cap.5.19.
units.tr: So the adversaries cry out that the doctrine of Christ's merit and satisfaction either utterly removes, or at least greatly hinders, zeal for holiness, without which no one will see God (Heb. 12.), since men persuaded that full satisfaction has been made to God for all sins suppose they are already truly righteous by another's righteousness, and cannot fall from the grace of God, however much they indulge their sins; yet meanwhile they do not notice that God altogether requires the condition of repentance, without which not all sins can be forgiven. Isa. 1.16.17.18. Zech. 18.21.22. Acts 2.20 and 5.19.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: ANSWER.

units.la: Usus servetur verus, tollatur abusus. Ut dissentimus ab illis, qui ita resipiscentiam & vitae sanctimoniam urgent, ut meritum & satisfactionem Jesu Chri-sti
units.tr: Let the right use be kept and the abuse removed. We dissent from those who press repentance and holiness of life in such a way that they do away with the merit and satisfaction of Jesus Christ for our sins.

units.la: Responsio. sti pro nostris peccatis e medio tollant: ita maxime improbamus eos, qui ita meritis Filii Dei inani & mortua fide confisi immorantur, ut carnali securi-tati immoriantur, nec resipiscunt ut peccatis mortui vivant jufticiæ.
units.tr: We equally condemn those who rely on the merits of the Son of God with an empty and dead faith, and so linger in carnal security, and do not repent, so that, dead to sins, they might live to righteousness.

units.la: Statuimus & profitemur, neminem hujus satisfactionis vel redemtionis per Christum comparatæ participem fieri, nisi vera fide Christo sit insitus. Joh.3, 16. Ita enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut filium suum unigenitum dederit, ut quisquis credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam. Et cap.6.35. Ego sum panis ille vitæ, qui venit ad me, nequaquam esuriet; & qui credit in me, non sitiet unquam. Johan.15.2. Omnem palmitem in me non ferentem fructum, tollit: & omnem qui fert fructum purgat, ut plus fructus adferat. Rom.3.22. Justitia Dei per fidem Jesu Christi in omnes & super omnes qui credunt. Gal.2.10. Vna cum Christo crucifixus sum. Vivo autem non amplius ego, sed vivit in me Christus; et vitam quam nunc vivo in carne, vivo per fidem filii Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me.
units.tr: We affirm and profess that no one becomes a partaker of this satisfaction or of the redemption obtained through Christ unless he is engrafted into Christ by true faith. John 3:16: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. And chapter 6:35: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. John 15:2: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Rom. 3:22: The righteousness of God, which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe. Gal. 2:20: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

units.la: Porro veram fidem non esse mortuam didicimus, Jacob. 2, 17, Fides si opera z[?] habeat mortua est per se: sed efficacem eam per opera caritatis novimus. Galat. 5. 6. In Christo enim Jesu neque circumcisio quicquam valet, neque praeputium, sed fides per Caritatem ens[?].
units.tr: Moreover, we have learned that true faith is not dead. James 2:17: Faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone. But we know that it is made effective through works of love. Gal. 5:6: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith working through love.

units.la: Ergo etiam justificati per Christum simul etiam justificantur. Rom. 6.
units.tr: Therefore those who are justified through Christ are at the same time also made righteous in their lives. Rom. 6.

units.la: 8. Etenim qui mortuus est, liber est a peccato: quod si mortui sumus cum Christo, credimus ut etiam vivamus cum eo. Item, Colligite vos ipsos tum mortuos esse peccato, tum vero vivere Deo per Christum Jesum Dominum nostrum. Ne[?] regnet igitur peccatum in mortali corpore vestro, ut obediatis peccato in cupiditatibus corporis: neque sistite membra vestra instrumenta peccato, sed sistite vos Deo, ut ex mortuis vivos, et membra vestra arma justitiae Deo.
units.tr: 8. For he that is dead is freed from sin. Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him. Likewise: Reckon yourselves also to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof. Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

units.la: Non ergo negamus debere nos tanquam bonas arbores fructus proferre bonos. Matth. 7. 17. et vosmet non nerabitis doctrinae nostrae abusum non ipsi doctrinae, sed hominum male feriatorum vitio imputari debere.
units.tr: We therefore do not deny that we ought, like good trees, to bring forth good fruit. Matt. 7:17. And you yourselves will not deny that the abuse of our teaching is to be imputed not to the teaching itself, but to the fault of wicked men.

units.la: Quapropter nos hanc doctrinam de merito et satisfactione Jesu Chr. auditoribus nostris sic inculcare omni studio et ope annitimur, ut eos doceamus Christi Iesu praeceptis pie obtemperare, & viam illam arctam, quae ducit ad vitam, & qua pauci inveniunt, insistere. Matth. 7.13. &c. Introite enim, inquit Christus, per angustam portam, quoniam lata est porta & spatiosa via, quae abducit in exitium, multique sunt, qui introeunt per eam: quia angusta est porta & stricta via, quae ducit ad vitam, & pauci sunt, qui inveniunt eam. Item: Non quisquis dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, introibit in regnum coelorum, sed qui facit, quod vult Pater meus, qui in coelis est. Multi dicent mihi in illo die: Domine, Domine, nonne per nomen tuum prophetavimus, & per nomen tuum daemonia ejecimus, & per nomen tuum multas virtutes edidimus? Tunc autem profitebor eis: Nunquam novi vos, discedite a me, qui facitis iniquitatem. Quisquis igitur audit ex me sermones istos, & eos praestat, assimulabo eum viro prudenti, qui aedificavit domum suam super petram &c.
units.tr: Wherefore we strive with all zeal and effort to impress this doctrine of the merit and satisfaction of Jesus Christ upon our hearers in such a way that we teach them to obey the precepts of Christ Jesus piously, and to walk in that narrow way which leads to life, and which few find. Matt. 7:13, etc. Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it. Likewise: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity. Whosoever therefore heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, who built his house upon a rock, etc.

units.la: Christus enim legitur iis tantum fa-ctus auctor salutis; qui ipsi auscultant. Hebr. s. 9. hoc est, qui ambulant, sicuti ipse ambulavit. 1. Johan. 2. 5. 6. Qui ser-vat sermonem ejus, vere in hoc caritas Dei exple-ta est: per hoc scimus nos in ipso esse. Qui dicit se in eo habitare, debet sicut ipse ambulavit, ita & ipse. & ipse ambulare. Et Galat. 5. 24. Qui Christi sunt, carnem crucifixerunt, cum affectibus & concupiscentiis. Si igitur vivimus spiritu, spi-ritu etiam incedamus. Non enim omnibus praeparata est gloria coelestis, sed tantummodo diligentibus Deum ex toto animo. 1. Corint. 2. 9. Quae oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in mentem hominis venerunt, quae paravit Deus iis, qui ipsum diligunt. Et 1. Joh. 3. 14. 15. Nos scimus, nos translatos esse ex morte ad vitam, quia diligimus fratres: qui non diligit fratrem, manet in morte. Quisquis odit fratrem suum, homicida est, & nostis nullum homicidam habere vitam aeternam in se manentem.
units.tr: For Christ is said to be the author of salvation only to those who obey him, Heb. 5:9, that is, to those who walk just as he walked. 1 John 2:5-6: But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him. He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked. And to walk as he walked. Gal. 5:24: And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit. For the heavenly glory is not prepared for all, but only for those who love God with their whole heart. 1 Cor. 2:9: Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. And 1 John 3:14-15: We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death. Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.

units.la: Non igitur diffitemur, reliquos omnes, quantumvis glorientur Christo Servatore, & dicant se niti merito & satisfactione Jesu Christi, nec viva fide in ipsum credunt, quae fides operetur per caritatem erga Deum & proximum suum, in morte & damnatione sempiterna manere. 1. Johan. 2 v. 4. Per hoc scimus, nos eum nosse, si mandata ejus observamus. Quidicit: Novi eum, & mandata ejus non servat, mendax est, & in eo veritas non est. Et Cap. 3. v. 6, &c. Quisquis in eo manet, non peccat, quisquis peccat, non vidit eum, neq; novit eum. Filioli, nemo vos seducat, Qui ex[?]ercet justitiam, justus est, sicut ipse justus est. Qui committit peccatum ex diabolo est: quoniam a principio Diabolus peccat: ad hoc patefistus est Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera Diaboli. Item, Per hoc manifesti sunt Filii Dei & Filii Diaboli: Quisquis non exercet justitiam, non est ex Deo, & qui non diligit fratrem suum. Cap. 4. vers. 8. Qui enim non diligit, non novit Deum, quia Deus est caritas. Quapropter, ut est Apocal. 21. ver. 8. timidis & incredulis, & execrabilibus, & homicidis, & scortatoribus, & veneficis, & idololatris, & omnibus mendacibus pars assignata est in stagno ardenti igne & sulphure, quod est mors secunda.
units.tr: We therefore do not deny that all the rest, however much they boast of Christ the Saviour, and say that they rest on the merit and satisfaction of Jesus Christ, yet do not believe in him with a living faith, which works through love toward God and their neighbour, remain in death and everlasting damnation. 1 John 2:4: Hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments. He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him. And chapter 3:6, etc.: Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither known him. Little children, let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous. He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil. Likewise: In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. Chapter 4:8: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love. Therefore, as is said in Revelation 21:8: But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.

units.la: Quisq; igitur ex satisfactione & propitiatione Christi solidum vult percipere gaudium, esto verè fidelis; Verè autem fidelem eum dico, qui veram salutis viam à CHRISTO annunciatam & confirmatam ingreditur & ambulat. Haec autem via salutis nobis Christia-nis non est alia, quam vera & viva in CHRISTUM Fides, qua ipsius obedientia nobis præstita ad justitiam imputatur.
units.tr: Whoever therefore wishes to receive solid joy from the satisfaction and propitiation of Christ, let him be a truly faithful man. I call him truly faithful who enters upon and walks in the true way of salvation announced and confirmed by Christ. This way of salvation, for us Christians, is nothing other than true and living faith in Christ, by which his obedience, rendered on our behalf, is imputed to us for righteousness.

units.la: Sic enim nos ex Paulo, ut credimus, etiam docemus, Roman. 5. verf. 25. iustificamur gratis, hoc est, ejus gratia, per redemptionem factam in Iesu Christo: quem proposuit Deus placamentum in sanguine ipsius per fidem, ad declarandam iustitiam suam per remissionem praeteritorum peccatorum. Cap. 4. et f. 25.[?] Iesus Dominus noster, traditus est in mortem propter offensas nostras, & excitatus est propter iustificationem nostri. Et cap. 4. v. 19. Sicut per inobedientiam unius hominis constituti sunt peccatores multi: ita per unius obedientiam iusti constituentur multi. Galat. 1. verf. 16. Scientes non iustificari hominem ex operibus legis, sed per fidem Iesu Christi: Proinde etiam nos in Christum Iesum credidimus, ut iustificaremur ex fide Iesu Christi, & non ex operibus legis, propterea quod non iustificabitur ex operibus legis ulla caro. Et cap. 3. verf. 11. Nullum igitur per legem iustificari manifestum est, siquidem iustus ex fide vivet.
units.tr: For thus we also teach, as we believe, from Paul: Rom. 3:24-25: we are justified freely, that is, by his grace, through the redemption that is in Jesus Christ, whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past. Chapter 4:25: Jesus our Lord was delivered for our offences and raised again for our justification. And chapter 5:19: For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. Gal. 2:16: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. And chapter 3:11: But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.

units.la: Hac ipsa fide Christus in cordibus nostris habitat: sicut dicitur Ephes. 3. verf. 17. ut inhabitet Christus in cordibus vestris. Et Johan. 6. Qui edit carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, in me manet, & ego in eo. Ita quidem inhabitat, ut nos ipsius Spiritu acti (Roman. 8. ver. 14.) & nova creatura in ipso facti (2. Corinth. v. 17. Galat. 6. v. 15.) ipsum salutis principem per medias afflictiones imitemur (Heb. 2. v. 10.) Viventes ad Dei gloriam, & proximi aedificationem, firma spe in Deo reposita ad beatam illam immortalitatem contendamus. Illuxit enim, inquit Apostolus Christi Tit. 2. gratia illa Dei salutifera omnibus hominibus, erudiens, nos ut abnegata impietate & mundanis cupiditatibus, temperanter, & juste, & pie vivamus in praesenti seculo, expectantes beatam illam spem, & illustrem illum adventum gloriae Magni illius Dei & servatoris nostri Iesu Christi, qui dedit semetipsum pro nobis, ut redimeret nos ab omni iniquitate, & purificaret sibi ipsi populum peculiarem studiosum bonorum operum.
units.tr: By this very faith Christ dwells in our hearts, as it is said in Eph. 3:17, "that Christ may dwell in your hearts." And John 6: "He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him." He dwells in such a way that, moved by his Spirit (Rom. 8:14) and made a new creature in him (2 Cor. 5:17; Gal. 6:15), we imitate the Author of salvation himself through the midst of afflictions (Heb. 2:10), living to the glory of God and the building up of our neighbour, and, with firm hope placed in God, strive toward that blessed immortality. For, as the Apostle says in Titus 2, "the saving grace of God has appeared to all men, training us so that, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, righteously and godly in the present age, awaiting that blessed hope and the glorious appearing of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people of his own, zealous for good works."

units.la: Sic igitur cum gratia liberalissimi & beneficentissimi Dei Patris, propitiationem & satisfactionem filii Dei Iesu Christi; & cum gratia Dei & Merito Iesu Christi fidem & resipiscentiam conjungimus & urgemus.
units.tr: Thus we join and press together faith and repentance with the grace of the most bountiful and beneficent God the Father, and the propitiation and satisfaction of God's Son Jesus Christ; and with the grace of God and the merit of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Orandus autem est nobis, & exo-andus DEus, ut furores Satanae ipse ompescat, & eorum, qui dissidia volunt in Ecclesia, conatus reprimat: At nos in veritate tueatur ac conservet, ac proinde benignus efficiat, ut in Christo Iesu simus omnes unum. AMEN.
units.tr: We must pray to God, and earnestly beseech him, that he himself restrain the rage of Satan and check the attempts of those who desire divisions in the Church; and that he keep and preserve us in the truth, and so graciously grant that in Christ Jesus we may all be one. AMEN.
